````bash
install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Weekly cleanup of the GitLab Runner host: Docker, runner caches, packages, logs, temp files.
set -Eeuo pipefail
RETENTION_DAYS="${RETENTION_DAYS:-7}"
JOURNAL_MAX="${JOURNAL_MAX:-500M}"
SHARED_CACHE_DIR="${SHARED_CACHE_DIR:-/srv/ci-cache}"
SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS="${SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS:-14}"
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
CACHE_DIRS=(/home/gitlab-runner/cache /home/gitlab-runner/.cache /var/lib/gitlab-runner/cache /root/.cache)
BUILD_DIRS=(/home/gitlab-runner/builds /var/lib/gitlab-runner/builds)
log()  { logger -t runner-weekly-cleanup -- "$*"; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*"; }
disk() { df --output=used,avail,pcent -h / | tail -1 | xargs; }
run() {
  log "-> $*"
  [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]] && return 0
  "$@" || log "WARN: failed: $*"
}
wipe_dir() {
  local dir="$1" age="${2:-}"
  [[ -d "$dir" ]] || return 0
  if [[ -n "$age" ]]; then
    log "-> cleaning $dir older than ${age}d"
    [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]] && return 0
    find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -mtime +"$age" -delete 2>/dev/null || log "WARN: partial cleanup of $dir"
  else
    log "-> wiping $dir"
    [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]] && return 0
    find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || log "WARN: partial wipe of $dir"
  fi
}
usage() {
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 [--dry-run] [--help]
  --dry-run                   same as DRY_RUN=1: show what would be cleaned without deleting anything
Env:
  RETENTION_DAYS              keep images, builds and temp files newer than N days (default: 7)
  JOURNAL_MAX                 max systemd journal size (default: 500M)
  SHARED_CACHE_DIR            shared CI cache directory (default: /srv/ci-cache)
  SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS   prune shared cache files not accessed for N days (default: 14)
  DRY_RUN=1                   show what would be cleaned without deleting anything
USAGE
}
while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    -n|--dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    *) usage >&2; echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
exec 9>/run/runner-weekly-cleanup.lock
flock -n 9 || { log "another cleanup is running, exit"; exit 0; }
hours=$(( RETENTION_DAYS * 24 ))
log "start (dry_run=${DRY_RUN}), disk before: $(disk)"
if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # docker not answering is not "no jobs"; stderr is kept apart so a warning is not counted as a job
  ps_err=$(mktemp)
  trap 'rm -f "$ps_err"' EXIT
  if ! job_ids=$({ docker ps -q --filter "label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true" && docker ps -q --filter "label=io.server-init.github-runner=job"; } 2>"$ps_err"); then
    log "ERROR: docker is not responding, cleanup skipped: $(cat "$ps_err")"
    exit 1
  fi
  running=$(wc -w <<<"$job_ids")
  if (( running > 0 )); then
    log "WARN: ${running} job container(s) running, skipping cache wipe"
  else
    run /usr/share/gitlab-runner/clear-docker-cache prune-volumes
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]]; then
      docker volume ls -q --filter name=runner- | xargs -r docker volume rm >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: some runner volumes in use"
    fi
    for dir in "${CACHE_DIRS[@]}"; do wipe_dir "$dir"; done
  fi
  run docker container prune -f --filter "until=${hours}h"
  run docker image prune -af --filter "until=${hours}h"
  # the prune takes the pinned GitHub runner images too: fetch them again
  for img in $(sed -n 's/^GH_\(RUNNER\|BUILDKIT\)_IMAGE=//p' "${GHR_CONFIG:-/etc/github-runner/config.env}" 2>/dev/null); do
    docker image inspect "$img" >/dev/null 2>&1 || run docker pull -q "$img"
  done
  run docker builder prune -af --filter "until=${hours}h"
  run docker network prune -f --filter "until=${hours}h"
fi
for dir in "${BUILD_DIRS[@]}"; do wipe_dir "$dir" "$RETENTION_DAYS"; done
if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 autoremove --purge -y -q
  run apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 autoclean -q
  run apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 clean -q
elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run dnf -y -q autoremove
  run dnf -q clean all
fi
run journalctl --vacuum-time="$(( RETENTION_DAYS * 2 ))d" --vacuum-size="$JOURNAL_MAX"
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]]; then
  log "-> removing rotated logs older than 30d"
  find /var/log -type f \( -name '*.gz' -o -name '*-[0-9]*' -o -name '*.[0-9]' -o -name '*.old' \) -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  find /tmp /var/tmp -xdev -mindepth 1 -type f -atime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -delete 2>/dev/null || true
fi
run systemd-tmpfiles --clean
if [[ -d "$SHARED_CACHE_DIR" && "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]]; then
  log "-> pruning ${SHARED_CACHE_DIR} files not used for ${SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS}d"
  find "$SHARED_CACHE_DIR" -xdev -type f -atime +"$SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS" -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  find "$SHARED_CACHE_DIR" -xdev -mindepth 2 -type d -empty -delete 2>/dev/null || true
fi
log "done, disk after: $(disk)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emergency cleanup when the root filesystem crosses HARD_LIMIT percent.
set -Eeuo pipefail
HARD_LIMIT="${HARD_LIMIT:-85}"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  (env: HARD_LIMIT=85) runs runner-weekly-cleanup.sh with RETENTION_DAYS=1 when disk usage >= HARD_LIMIT%"
  exit 0
fi
used=$(df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
if (( used >= HARD_LIMIT )); then
  logger -t runner-disk-guard -- "disk ${used}% >= ${HARD_LIMIT}%, running emergency cleanup"
  RETENTION_DAYS=1 /usr/local/bin/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh
fi
__SIC_EOF__

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/runner-engine-update.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Weekly upgrade of Docker CE and GitLab Runner while no CI job runs (GitLab jobs, GitHub runner pods): runner and github-runner-ctl
# stopped gracefully, jobs checked again, Docker upgraded and restarted, gitlab-runner last; a job in between: all started again.
# One result line in /var/log/runner-engine-update.log. Env: DRY_RUN=1 plan only; STOP_WAIT seconds for the graceful stop (1800).
set -Eeuo pipefail
LOG="${ENGINE_UPDATE_LOG:-/var/log/runner-engine-update.log}"   # overridable for tests
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
STOP_WAIT="${STOP_WAIT:-1800}"
DROPIN="${ENGINE_UPDATE_DROPIN:-/etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/graceful-stop.conf}"
PKGS=(docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin gitlab-runner)
note() { logger -t runner-engine-update -- "$*" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 [--dry-run]   upgrades ${PKGS[*]} when no CI job runs"
  exit 0
fi
[[ "${1:-}" == "--dry-run" ]] && DRY_RUN=1
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
exec 9>/run/runner-engine-update.lock
flock -n 9 || { note "SKIP another update is running"; exit 0; }
# A docker error is not "no jobs".
job_ids() { docker ps -q --filter "label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true" && docker ps -q --filter "label=io.server-init.github-runner=job"; }
if ! jobs=$(job_ids 2>/dev/null); then
  note "SKIP docker does not answer, cannot tell whether jobs run"
  exit 0
fi
if [[ -n "$jobs" ]]; then
  note "SKIP $(wc -w <<<"$jobs") CI job(s) running, will retry next week"
  exit 0
fi
installed=()
if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && installed+=("$p"); done
  upgrade() { dnf -y -q upgrade "$@"; }
  pending() { dnf -q check-update "${installed[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; [[ $? -eq 100 ]]; }
elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do dpkg -s "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && installed+=("$p"); done
  upgrade() { DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q --only-upgrade "$@"; }
  pending() { apt-get update -q >/dev/null 2>&1; apt-get -s install --only-upgrade "${installed[@]}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Inst '; }
else
  note "FAIL no supported package manager"
  exit 1
fi
(( ${#installed[@]} )) || { note "SKIP none of the packages is installed"; exit 0; }
if ! pending; then
  note "OK nothing to upgrade (${installed[*]})"
  exit 0
fi
docker_pkgs=(); runner_pkgs=()
for p in "${installed[@]}"; do if [[ "$p" == gitlab-runner ]]; then runner_pkgs+=("$p"); else docker_pkgs+=("$p"); fi; done
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == 1 ]]; then
  note "DRY-RUN would upgrade ${installed[*]}"
  exit 0
fi
before=$(for p in "${installed[@]}"; do if command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then rpm -q --qf '%{NAME}-%{VERSION}-%{RELEASE} ' "$p"; else dpkg-query -W -f='${Package}-${Version} ' "$p"; fi; done)
# From here whatever happens: start the runner again.
runner_stopped=0 ctl_stopped=0
ctl_back() { if (( ctl_stopped )); then systemctl start --no-block github-runner-ctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; }
runner_back() { systemctl start --no-block gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; ctl_back; }
trap '[[ $runner_stopped -eq 1 ]] && runner_back' EXIT
runner_state() { systemctl show -p ActiveState --value gitlab-runner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown; }
# SIGQUIT = graceful stop (jobs finish). Returns 1 when still running after STOP_WAIT.
stop_runner_wait() {
  local waited=0 st
  systemctl stop --no-block gitlab-runner
  while :; do
    st=$(runner_state)
    [[ "$st" == inactive || "$st" == failed ]] && return 0
    (( waited >= STOP_WAIT )) && return 1
    sleep 5
    waited=$((waited + 5))
  done
}
no_jobs() { local j; j=$(job_ids 2>/dev/null) && [[ -z "$j" ]]; }
# SIGTERM would end jobs; TimeoutStopSec=infinity: systemd never SIGKILLs the runner.
if ! grep -qs '^KillSignal=SIGQUIT' "$DROPIN" 2>/dev/null || ! grep -qs '^TimeoutStopSec=infinity' "$DROPIN" 2>/dev/null; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DROPIN")"
  printf '[Service]\nKillSignal=SIGQUIT\nTimeoutStopSec=infinity\n' > "$DROPIN"
  systemctl daemon-reload
fi
runner_stopped=1
# no new GitHub pod during the upgrade
if systemctl is-active --quiet github-runner-ctl 2>/dev/null; then systemctl stop github-runner-ctl && ctl_stopped=1; fi
if ! stop_runner_wait; then
  note "SKIP gitlab-runner did not stop within ${STOP_WAIT}s (jobs still running), will retry next week"
  exit 0
fi
if ! no_jobs; then
  note "SKIP a CI job appeared or docker does not answer after the runner stopped; will retry next week"
  exit 0
fi
if (( ${#docker_pkgs[@]} )) && ! upgrade "${docker_pkgs[@]}" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
  note "FAIL Docker package upgrade failed, see ${LOG}"
  exit 1
fi
# a package scriptlet may have started the runner and it may have taken a job
if [[ "$(runner_state)" != inactive ]]; then
  if ! stop_runner_wait; then
    note "SKIP Docker packages upgraded, but gitlab-runner is busy again; Docker not restarted (retry next week)"
    exit 0
  fi
fi
if ! no_jobs; then
  note "SKIP Docker packages upgraded, but a CI job runs or docker does not answer; Docker not restarted (retry next week)"
  exit 0
fi
bad=""
if (( ${#docker_pkgs[@]} )); then
  systemctl restart docker
  sleep 5
  # reapply the isolation rules
  if systemctl cat ci-job-isolation.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemctl restart ci-job-isolation.service || bad+=" ci-job-isolation"; fi
fi
if (( ${#runner_pkgs[@]} )) && ! upgrade "${runner_pkgs[@]}" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
  note "FAIL gitlab-runner upgrade failed, see ${LOG}"
  exit 1
fi
systemctl start gitlab-runner || true
runner_stopped=0
ctl_back
sleep 5
for s in docker gitlab-runner; do systemctl is-active --quiet "$s" || bad+=" $s"; done
if [[ -n "$bad" ]]; then
  note "FAIL not active after the upgrade:${bad}; was: ${before}"
  exit 1
fi
note "OK upgraded ${installed[*]}; was: ${before}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/runner-engine-update.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/ci-job-isolation.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Keeps CI jobs away from the cloud metadata service (DOCKER-USER drops 169.254.169.254) and from host services (INPUT from docker0
# and br-* goes through CI-JOBS-IN: replies, ping and the npm cache, docker0 IP port 4873, pass; br-* only from GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL).
# Run by ci-job-isolation.service at boot and after every Docker start; IPv4 only. Remove: disable the unit, iptables -F CI-JOBS-IN,
# delete the two "ci-job-isolation" rules shown by iptables -S.
set -Eeuo pipefail
META_IP="${META_IP:-169.254.169.254}"
NPM_PORT="${NPM_PORT:-4873}"
TAG=ci-job-isolation
log() { logger -t "$TAG" -- "$*" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "$*"; }
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0   blocks CI jobs from ${META_IP} and from host services (except the npm cache on the docker0 IP, port ${NPM_PORT})"
  exit 0
fi
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v iptables >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "iptables not found, nothing applied"; exit 1; }
# Docker creates DOCKER-USER when it starts; wait for it after a boot.
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  if iptables -n -L DOCKER-USER >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
iptables -n -L DOCKER-USER >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "chain DOCKER-USER does not exist (is Docker running?), nothing applied"; exit 1; }
# Insert a rule at the top of a chain unless it is there already.
ensure() {
  local chain="$1"
  shift
  iptables -C "$chain" "$@" 2>/dev/null || iptables -I "$chain" 1 "$@"
}
ensure DOCKER-USER -d "$META_IP" -m comment --comment "$TAG" -j DROP
BRIDGE_IP="${BRIDGE_IP:-}"
if [[ -z "$BRIDGE_IP" ]] && command -v ip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  BRIDGE_IP=$(ip -4 -o addr show docker0 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $4 }' | cut -d/ -f1 | head -1 || true)
fi
iptables -N CI-JOBS-IN 2>/dev/null || true
iptables -F CI-JOBS-IN
iptables -A CI-JOBS-IN -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A CI-JOBS-IN -p icmp --icmp-type echo-request -j ACCEPT
if [[ -n "$BRIDGE_IP" ]]; then
  iptables -A CI-JOBS-IN -i docker0 -d "$BRIDGE_IP" -p tcp --dport "$NPM_PORT" -j ACCEPT
fi
POOL=$(sed -n 's/^GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL=//p' "${GHR_CONFIG:-/etc/github-runner/config.env}" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '"' | head -1 || true)
if [[ -n "$POOL" && -n "$BRIDGE_IP" ]]; then
  # only a private /16 to /27 block with zero host bits (as the controller checks it); a failing rule must not skip the DROP
  IFS=. read -r o1 o2 o3 o4 <<<"${POOL%/*}"
  if [[ "$POOL" =~ ^(10(\.[0-9]{1,3}){3}|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])(\.[0-9]{1,3}){2}|192\.168(\.[0-9]{1,3}){2})/(1[6-9]|2[0-7])$ ]] \
     && (( ((10#$o1 << 24 | 10#$o2 << 16 | 10#$o3 << 8 | 10#$o4) & ((1 << (32 - ${POOL#*/})) - 1)) == 0 )); then
    iptables -A CI-JOBS-IN -i 'br-+' -s "$POOL" -d "$BRIDGE_IP" -p tcp --dport "$NPM_PORT" -j ACCEPT || { log "WARN: pool rule failed"; POOL=""; }
  else
    log "WARN: GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL '${POOL}' is not an aligned private /16-/27 block, ignored"; POOL=""
  fi
fi
iptables -A CI-JOBS-IN -j DROP
ensure INPUT -i docker0 -m comment --comment "$TAG" -j CI-JOBS-IN
ensure INPUT -i 'br-+' -m comment --comment "$TAG" -j CI-JOBS-IN
log "applied: ${META_IP} blocked for containers; host services closed to job networks (npm cache: ${BRIDGE_IP:-none}:${NPM_PORT}${POOL:+, also for ${POOL}})"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/ci-job-isolation.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/systemd"
cat > "$R/runner/systemd/runner-engine-update.service" <<'__SIC_EOF__'

Description=Weekly upgrade of Docker CE and GitLab Runner when no CI job runs
After=docker.service network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/runner-engine-update.sh
Nice=10
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/systemd/runner-engine-update.service"

[Timer]

__SIC_EOF__

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
__SIC_EOF__

cat > "$R/common/sysctl-hardening.conf" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
````

<a id="firewall"></a>
## Host firewall and fail2ban

firewalld on Rocky, ufw on Debian, with SSH (22 and the port sshd listens on) allowed and everything else closed, plus the fail2ban sshd jail (5 tries in 10 minutes, 1 hour ban). The firewall starts only after SSH is in the saved rules and stops again if SSH is not allowed. Open the same ports in the Hetzner Cloud Firewall. If Docker was already running on Rocky, docker0 is moved into the firewalld docker zone, so Docker needs no restart.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/host-firewall.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Host firewall and fail2ban for the runner host: firewalld on Rocky/Alma/CentOS, ufw on Debian/Ubuntu.
# Self-contained (no lib.sh) so cloud-init can embed it. Safe to rerun.
#
# Nothing is opened except SSH (22 and every port sshd listens on) and, when Grafana is published on a domain
# (override file exists), 80/443. Services of the host
# (monitoring, logging, caches) listen on 127.0.0.1 or the docker0 IP and need no rule. Lockout guard, as in
# server/server-init-*.sh: the firewall is only started or enabled when SSH is in the saved rules, and it is
# stopped again when SSH is not allowed in the running rules. Also open the same ports in the Hetzner Cloud Firewall.
#
# Docker keeps working: on Rocky firewalld puts docker0 into its own docker zone when Docker starts after firewalld;
# if Docker was already running, this script moves docker0 into that zone (no Docker restart). On Debian
# ufw does not touch the chains Docker manages. Jobs are kept away from the host by ci-job-isolation.sh.
# fail2ban: sshd jail on the journal, 5 tries in 10 minutes, 1 hour ban.
set -Eeuo pipefail

JAIL_FILE="${JAIL_FILE:-/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/50-sshd.local}"   # overridable for tests
GRAFANA_OVERRIDE="${GRAFANA_OVERRIDE:-/opt/monitoring/docker-compose.override.yml}"   # exists once grafana-domain.sh ran

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0   enables firewalld (Rocky) or ufw (Debian) with SSH allowed, plus the fail2ban sshd jail"
  exit 0
fi
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"

web_published() { [[ -f "$GRAFANA_OVERRIDE" ]]; }

ssh_ports() {
  { echo 22; sshd -T 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "port" { print $2 }'; } | sort -un
}

put_jail() {
  local banaction="$1" tmp ports
  ports=$(ssh_ports | paste -sd, -)   # the jail must watch every port sshd listens on, not only 22
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  {
    if [[ -n "$banaction" ]]; then
      printf '[DEFAULT]\nbanaction = %s\nbanaction_allports = %s[type=allports]\n\n' "$banaction" "$banaction"
    fi
    printf '[sshd]\nenabled  = true\nport     = %s\nbackend  = systemd\nmaxretry = 5\nfindtime = 10m\nbantime  = 1h\n' "$ports"
  } > "$tmp"
  install -D -m 0644 "$tmp" "$JAIL_FILE"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$JAIL_FILE" || true; fi
}

firewalld_setup() {
  local running=0 changed=0 p zone set_zone
  command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 || dnf -y -q install firewalld || die "cannot install firewalld"
  systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld && running=1
  # SSH is allowed in the public zone, so the uplink must be in it: make it the default zone (as server-init does).
  if (( running )); then zone=$(firewall-cmd --get-default-zone) || die "cannot read the default zone"; else zone=$(firewall-offline-cmd --get-default-zone) || die "cannot read the default zone"; fi
  # Running: the default zone is switched after the reload, so SSH is never refused in between.
  set_zone=0
  if [[ "$zone" != public ]]; then
    log "firewalld: default zone was ${zone}, set to public"
    if (( running )); then set_zone=1; else firewall-offline-cmd --set-default-zone=public >/dev/null || die "cannot set the default zone"; fi
  fi
  # Permanent rules are written first (offline when firewalld is stopped), then the daemon is started or reloaded.
  fw() { if systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld; then firewall-cmd --permanent "$@"; else firewall-offline-cmd "$@"; fi; }
  fw --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || fw --zone=public --add-service=ssh >/dev/null || die "cannot add ssh to the public zone"
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    [[ "$p" == 22 ]] && continue
    fw --zone=public --query-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fw --zone=public --add-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null || die "cannot add port ${p}"
  done
  if web_published; then
    for p in http https; do
      fw --zone=public --query-service="$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fw --zone=public --add-service="$p" >/dev/null || die "cannot add ${p} to the public zone"
    done
    log "firewalld: http and https kept open (Grafana is published on a domain)"
  fi
  # Lockout guard: the saved rules must allow SSH before the firewall runs.
  fw --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ssh missing from the saved public zone; firewall left as it was"
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    [[ "$p" == 22 ]] && continue
    fw --zone=public --query-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "port ${p} missing from the saved public zone; firewall left as it was"
  done
  if (( running )); then firewall-cmd --reload >/dev/null || die "firewalld reload failed"; else systemctl enable --now firewalld || die "firewalld did not start"; fi
  systemctl enable firewalld >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if (( set_zone )); then firewall-cmd --set-default-zone=public >/dev/null || die "cannot set the default zone"; fi
  if ! firewall-cmd --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null; then
    systemctl stop firewalld
    die "ssh not allowed after start; firewalld stopped"
  fi
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    [[ "$p" == 22 ]] && continue
    if ! firewall-cmd --zone=public --query-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null; then
      systemctl stop firewalld
      die "ssh port ${p} not allowed after start; firewalld stopped"
    fi
  done
  # The default public zone opens cockpit (and mdns on some images); a runner host needs neither. Only these services
  # are removed, never ssh.
  for p in cockpit mdns; do
    if firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --query-service="$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      if firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service="$p" >/dev/null; then changed=1; else log "WARN: could not remove $p from the public zone"; fi
    fi
  done
  if (( changed )); then
    firewall-cmd --reload >/dev/null || die "firewalld reload failed"
    if ! firewall-cmd --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null; then systemctl stop firewalld; die "ssh not allowed after reload; firewalld stopped"; fi
  fi
  log "firewalld: active, public zone: $(firewall-cmd --zone=public --list-services) $(firewall-cmd --zone=public --list-ports)"
  docker_zone
}

# Docker that was running before firewalld left docker0 in the default zone, where firewalld rejects job traffic to
# the host (the npm cache on the docker0 address). Put docker0 into the docker zone (target ACCEPT, as Docker makes it),
# permanently and now, without restarting Docker. iptables rules (ci-job-isolation.sh) still apply on top.
docker_zone() {
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet docker || return 0
  ip link show docker0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  [[ "$(firewall-cmd --get-zone-of-interface=docker0 2>/dev/null)" == docker ]] && return 0
  if ! firewall-cmd --permanent --get-zones | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx docker; then
    firewall-cmd --permanent --new-zone=docker >/dev/null && firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=docker --set-target=ACCEPT >/dev/null \
      && firewall-cmd --reload >/dev/null || { log "WARN: cannot create the firewalld docker zone; restart Docker while no CI job runs: systemctl restart docker"; return 0; }
  fi
  if firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=docker --add-interface=docker0 >/dev/null && firewall-cmd --zone=docker --change-interface=docker0 >/dev/null; then
    log "firewalld: docker0 put into the docker zone"
  else
    log "WARN: docker0 is not in the docker zone; restart Docker while no CI job runs: systemctl restart docker"
  fi
}

ufw_setup() {
  local p o was_active=0
  command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 || { DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q ufw >/dev/null || die "cannot install ufw"; }
  o=$(ufw status 2>/dev/null) || true
  if grep -q '^Status: active' <<<"$o"; then was_active=1; fi
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do ufw allow "${p}/tcp" >/dev/null || die "cannot allow ${p}/tcp"; done
  if web_published; then
    ufw allow 80/tcp >/dev/null && ufw allow 443/tcp >/dev/null || die "cannot allow 80/443 in ufw"
    log "ufw: 80/tcp and 443/tcp kept open (Grafana is published on a domain)"
  fi
  # Lockout guard: every SSH port must be in the saved rules before ufw is enabled.
  o=$(ufw show added 2>/dev/null) || true
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    grep -qE "^ufw (allow|limit) (in )?${p}/tcp([[:space:]]|\$)" <<<"$o" || die "${p}/tcp missing from the saved ufw rules; ufw left as it was"
  done
  if (( ! was_active )); then
    ufw default deny incoming >/dev/null
    ufw default allow outgoing >/dev/null
    ufw --force enable >/dev/null
  fi
  systemctl enable ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  o=$(ufw status 2>/dev/null) || true
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    if ! grep -qE "^${p}/tcp([[:space:]]+\\(v6\\))?[[:space:]]+(ALLOW|LIMIT)" <<<"$o"; then
      if (( ! was_active )); then ufw disable >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
      die "ssh port ${p} not allowed in the running ufw; ufw disabled again"
    fi
  done
  log "ufw: $(ufw status | head -1); allowed: $(ssh_ports | tr '\n' ' ')"
}

# FIREWALL_BACKEND=firewalld|ufw overrides the choice by package manager (used by the tests).
backend="${FIREWALL_BACKEND:-}"
if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then backend=firewalld; elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then backend=ufw; fi
fi

if [[ "$backend" == firewalld ]]; then
  dnf -y -q install epel-release >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  dnf -y -q install fail2ban-server fail2ban-firewalld >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: fail2ban not available (EPEL?), sshd jail skipped"
  firewalld_setup
  if command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    put_jail ""
    systemctl enable --now fail2ban >/dev/null && systemctl restart fail2ban
  fi
elif [[ "$backend" == ufw ]]; then
  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q fail2ban >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: fail2ban not installed, sshd jail skipped"
  ufw_setup
  if command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    put_jail nftables
    systemctl enable --now fail2ban >/dev/null && systemctl restart fail2ban
  fi
else
  die "no supported package manager"
fi
if command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "fail2ban: $(fail2ban-client status 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
fi
log "OK: host firewall on. If you lock yourself out, use the Hetzner web console: systemctl stop firewalld (or: ufw disable)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/host-firewall.sh"

echo "files written to $R: 2"
bash "$R/runner/install/host-firewall.sh" </dev/null
INSTALL
````

<a id="security"></a>
## Security tools: audit, network, scan

Optional. Tools to test and audit your own server; use them only on systems you own or are authorized to test. Default: lynis, OpenSCAP, auditd (small ruleset), ssh-audit, testssl.sh, nmap and other network tools, and trivy, gitleaks, hadolint, cosign, osv-scanner, trufflehog, dockle as release binaries at pinned versions, checked against the checksums file of the same release. Options for the installer (`sudo bash /root/server-init-config/common/security-tools.sh --help`; `/root` is not readable by `ops`): `--aide`, `--clamav`, `--rkhunter`, `--chkrootkit`, `--grype`, `--syft`, `--k8s`, `--kali`, `--audit-timer`.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/security-tools.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Security tools to audit, test and scan YOUR OWN servers. Use them only on systems you own or are authorized to test.
# No option = --audit --network --scan. Groups:
#   --audit    lynis, OpenSCAP (EL/Fedora, evaluation only, never --remediate), auditd with a minimal ruleset, ssh-audit, testssl.sh, debsums (Debian)
#   --network  nmap, tcpdump, tshark, iperf3, socat, ncat, whois, dig, lsof, mtr, traceroute, iftop, nethogs, bmon
#   --scan     trivy, gitleaks, hadolint, cosign, osv-scanner, trufflehog, dockle: official release binaries at pinned versions, checked against the checksums file of the same release
# Opt-in (not part of the default, they use RAM, disk IO or are noisy): --aide --clamav --rkhunter --chkrootkit --arp-scan --grype --syft --k8s
#   --kali     the `kali` helper (Kali in a Docker container; nothing offensive is installed on the host)
#   --audit-timer  weekly systemd timer: lynis, oscap, aide --check, rkhunter (whatever is installed) into /var/log/security-audit
# Every package is installed on its own: one that is missing on this release is logged and skipped. Safe to rerun.
# Supported: CentOS Stream / Rocky / AlmaLinux 10, Fedora 44, Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

# --- pinned versions of the release binaries (override with the same-named environment variable) -----------------
# Each is downloaded from the project's GitHub release page and compared with the checksums file published in the same
# release. That catches corrupt or truncated downloads; it does not protect against a replaced release, because the
# checksums come from the same place as the binary.
: "${TRIVY_VERSION:=0.76.1}"
: "${GRYPE_VERSION:=0.121.0}"
: "${SYFT_VERSION:=1.55.0}"
: "${GITLEAKS_VERSION:=8.30.1}"
: "${HADOLINT_VERSION:=2.14.0}"
: "${DOCKLE_VERSION:=0.4.15}"
: "${COSIGN_VERSION:=3.1.4}"
: "${OSV_SCANNER_VERSION:=2.7.0}"
: "${TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION:=3.99.7}"
: "${KUBESCAPE_VERSION:=4.0.17}"
: "${KUBE_BENCH_VERSION:=0.16.0}"
# ssh-audit from PyPI into /opt/ssh-audit (only when the distro has no package); the wheel hash is checked by pip.
: "${SSH_AUDIT_VERSION:=3.9.0}"
: "${SSH_AUDIT_WHEEL_SHA256:=3dad48d4678e0de31f6332cc7674f9d7dd1805f86babf3796f41c2fd879cb812}"
# testssl.sh: distro package where there is one; otherwise a git checkout of the tag, accepted only when the commit
# is the pinned one (a commit id is a content hash of the whole tree).
: "${TESTSSL_VERSION:=3.2.4}"
: "${TESTSSL_COMMIT:=97763a411c525720a5f9bd9d2cded416b10f210a}"

SEC_STATE=/var/lib/security-tools
AUDIT_LOG_DIR=/var/log/security-audit

WANT_AUDIT=0 WANT_NETWORK=0 WANT_SCAN=0 WANT_KALI=0 WANT_TIMER=0
WANT_AIDE=0 WANT_CLAMAV=0 WANT_RKHUNTER=0 WANT_CHKROOTKIT=0 WANT_ARP=0 WANT_GRYPE=0 WANT_SYFT=0 WANT_K8S=0

usage() {
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 [--audit] [--network] [--scan] [opt-in tools] [--kali] [--audit-timer]

Installs security tools for testing and auditing systems you own or are authorized to test.
No option = --audit --network --scan. Any option given = only what you name.

  --audit        lynis, OpenSCAP (EL/Fedora; audit only, never remediates: CIS remediation breaks Docker forwarding),
                 auditd with a small ruleset (sudoers, sshd_config, runner config, docker; no execve; ~200 MB log cap),
                 ssh-audit, testssl.sh, debsums (Debian family)
  --network      nmap, tcpdump, tshark (nobody is added to the wireshark group), iperf3, socat, ncat, whois, dig,
                 lsof, mtr, traceroute, iftop, nethogs, bmon
  --scan         trivy ${TRIVY_VERSION}, gitleaks ${GITLEAKS_VERSION}, hadolint ${HADOLINT_VERSION}, cosign ${COSIGN_VERSION}, osv-scanner ${OSV_SCANNER_VERSION},
                 trufflehog ${TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION}, dockle ${DOCKLE_VERSION} (release binaries, SHA256 verified; a mismatch is refused)

Opt-in, because they cost RAM, IO or produce noise:
  --aide         AIDE file integrity, scoped to /etc /usr/local /boot /usr/bin /usr/sbin; the baseline scan runs at idle IO priority
  --clamav       clamscan on demand + a daily freshclam timer. Never the clamd daemon: a loaded signature set needs
                 ~1.2 GB RAM (clamscan needs about as much while it runs), a lot on a 4 GB runner host
  --rkhunter     rkhunter; baseline refreshed after package updates (apt hook; dnf action on EL). Noisy on Docker hosts
  --chkrootkit   chkrootkit. Overlaps with rkhunter, false positives on Docker hosts are common
  --arp-scan     arp-scan (little use on Hetzner's routed network)
  --grype --syft grype ${GRYPE_VERSION}, syft ${SYFT_VERSION} (trivy already does vulnerability scans and SBOMs)
  --k8s          kubescape ${KUBESCAPE_VERSION}, kube-bench ${KUBE_BENCH_VERSION} (only useful where you run Kubernetes)

  --kali         the 'kali' helper: Kali Linux in a Docker container, built on first use (2-3 GB); needs Docker
  --audit-timer  weekly timer (idle priority): lynis, oscap, aide --check, rkhunter, reports in ${AUDIT_LOG_DIR}
  --all          --audit --network --scan --kali and every opt-in tool except --audit-timer

Supported: CentOS Stream / Rocky / AlmaLinux 10, Fedora 44, Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04.
USAGE
}

ANY=0
while (( $# )); do
  ANY=1
  case "$1" in
    --audit) WANT_AUDIT=1 ;;
    --network) WANT_NETWORK=1 ;;
    --scan) WANT_SCAN=1 ;;
    --kali) WANT_KALI=1 ;;
    --audit-timer) WANT_TIMER=1 ;;
    --aide) WANT_AIDE=1 ;;
    --clamav) WANT_CLAMAV=1 ;;
    --rkhunter) WANT_RKHUNTER=1 ;;
    --chkrootkit) WANT_CHKROOTKIT=1 ;;
    --arp-scan) WANT_ARP=1 ;;
    --grype) WANT_GRYPE=1 ;;
    --syft) WANT_SYFT=1 ;;
    --k8s) WANT_K8S=1 ;;
    --all) WANT_AUDIT=1 WANT_NETWORK=1 WANT_SCAN=1 WANT_KALI=1 WANT_AIDE=1 WANT_CLAMAV=1 WANT_RKHUNTER=1 WANT_CHKROOTKIT=1 WANT_ARP=1 WANT_GRYPE=1 WANT_SYFT=1 WANT_K8S=1 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) usage >&2; die "unknown option: $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done
if (( ANY == 0 )); then
  WANT_AUDIT=1 WANT_NETWORK=1 WANT_SCAN=1
fi
require_root

# --- OS ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[[ -r /etc/os-release ]] || die "/etc/os-release missing, cannot detect the OS"
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. /etc/os-release
case "${ID:-}:${VERSION_ID%%.*}" in
  centos:10|rocky:10|almalinux:10|rhel:10) FAMILY=el ;;
  fedora:44)                                FAMILY=fedora ;;
  debian:13|ubuntu:26)                      FAMILY=debian ;;
  *) die "unsupported OS ${PRETTY_NAME:-${ID:-unknown} ${VERSION_ID:-}}: this script supports CentOS Stream/Rocky/AlmaLinux 10, Fedora 44, Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04" ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64|amd64)  ARCH=amd64 ;;
  aarch64|arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
  *)             ARCH="" ;;
esac

INSTALLED=() PRESENT=() MISSING=() SKIPPED=()
CHECKSUM_FAIL=0
DL_TRIED=0   # downloads attempted in this run: release binaries, the testssl git clone, the ssh-audit pip install (tools already present are not counted)
DL_FAILED=0  # of those, how many were not installed (a scan run with no usable curl or architecture counts as one failure)

have_systemd() { [[ -d /run/systemd/system ]]; }

if [[ $FAMILY == debian ]]; then
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  apt-get update -q >/dev/null || log "WARN: apt-get update failed, package lists may be stale"
  pm_installed() { [[ "$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$1" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "install ok installed" ]]; }
  pm_install() { apt-get install -y -q --no-install-recommends "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
else
  pm_installed() { rpm -q --quiet "$1"; }
  pm_install() { dnf -y -q install "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
fi

# pkg_ensure NAME: 0 when installed (already or now), 1 when not available. Records the result.
pkg_ensure() {
  if pm_installed "$1"; then PRESENT+=("$1"); return 0; fi
  if pm_install "$1"; then INSTALLED+=("$1"); return 0; fi
  return 1
}

# want SPEC...: SPEC is a package or alternatives "a|b" (the first one that installs wins). Unavailable ones are logged at the end.
want() {
  local spec alt ok
  for spec in "$@"; do
    ok=0
    for alt in ${spec//|/ }; do
      if pkg_ensure "$alt"; then ok=1; break; fi
    done
    if (( ok == 0 )); then MISSING+=("${spec//|/ or }"); fi
  done
}

if [[ $FAMILY == el ]] && (( WANT_AUDIT || WANT_NETWORK || WANT_AIDE || WANT_CLAMAV || WANT_RKHUNTER || WANT_CHKROOTKIT || WANT_ARP )); then
  dnf -y -q install epel-release >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: epel-release not available, EPEL tools will be missing"
  # some EPEL packages need CRB; enabling it is the documented companion of EPEL
  if command -v crb >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    crb enable >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: could not enable CRB"
  else
    dnf -y -q config-manager --set-enabled crb >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: could not enable CRB (dnf config-manager)"
  fi
fi

# --- audit -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
AIDE_DIR=/var/lib/security-tools/aide
AIDE_CONF=/etc/security-tools/aide.conf

# Own AIDE config, scoped to the places that matter. The distro default (whole filesystem, daily run) is not used.
setup_aide() {
  command -v aide >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  install -d -m 0750 /etc/security-tools "$AIDE_DIR"
  cat > "$AIDE_CONF" <<EOF
# Managed by common/security-tools.sh (scoped baseline: no containers, no CI caches, no home directories)
database_in=file:${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.gz
database_out=file:${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.new.gz
gzip_dbout=yes
report_url=stdout
NORMAL = p+i+n+u+g+s+m+c+sha256
/etc NORMAL
/etc/gitlab-runner NORMAL
/usr/local NORMAL
/boot NORMAL
/usr/bin NORMAL
/usr/sbin NORMAL
!/etc/mtab
!/etc/resolv.conf
!/etc/adjtime
!/etc/security-tools
!/usr/local/share/man
!/var/lib/docker
!/home/gitlab-runner
!/srv/ci-cache
!/opt/[^/]+/data
EOF
  chmod 600 "$AIDE_CONF"
  # Debian's own daily AIDE check would run the default whole-filesystem config
  if have_systemd; then
    systemctl disable --now dailyaidecheck.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  if [[ -s "${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.gz" ]]; then
    log "aide: baseline already present (${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.gz)"
    return 0
  fi
  log "aide: creating the baseline (idle IO priority, a few minutes)"
  nice -n 19 ionice -c3 aide --config "$AIDE_CONF" --init >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if [[ -s "${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.new.gz" ]]; then
    mv -f "${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.new.gz" "${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.gz"
    chmod 600 "${AIDE_DIR}/aide.db.gz"
    log "aide: baseline ready; check with: aide --config ${AIDE_CONF} --check. After planned changes run --update and replace the database"
  else
    log "WARN: aide --init produced no database; run it by hand: aide --config ${AIDE_CONF} --init"
  fi
}

# Minimal ruleset: configuration that decides who can get in. No execve logging (volume), no -e 2 (stays reloadable).
setup_auditd() {
  command -v auditctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  local f=/etc/audit/rules.d/60-security-tools.rules rules conf=/etc/audit/auditd.conf
  rules='# Managed by common/security-tools.sh. Not immutable (no -e 2). Paths that did not exist at install time are left out.
-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k sudoers
-w /etc/sudoers.d/ -p wa -k sudoers
-w /etc/ssh/sshd_config -p wa -k sshd
-w /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ -p wa -k sshd'
  # rerun this script after adding Docker or the runner to pick their paths up
  if [[ -d /etc/gitlab-runner ]]; then rules+=$'\n''-w /etc/gitlab-runner/ -p wa -k gitlab-runner'; fi
  if [[ -S /run/docker.sock ]]; then rules+=$'\n''-w /run/docker.sock -p rwa -k docker-sock'; fi
  install -d /etc/audit/rules.d
  if [[ "$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null || true)" != "$rules" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "$rules" > "$f"
    chmod 640 "$f"
    log "auditd: wrote ${f}"
  fi
  # about 200 MB at most: 4 logs of 50 MB, rotated
  if [[ -f "$conf" ]]; then
    sed -i -E 's/^max_log_file[[:space:]]*=.*/max_log_file = 50/; s/^num_logs[[:space:]]*=.*/num_logs = 4/; s/^max_log_file_action[[:space:]]*=.*/max_log_file_action = ROTATE/' "$conf"
  fi
  if have_systemd; then
    systemctl enable --now auditd >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: could not enable auditd"
    augenrules --load >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: could not load the audit rules now (they apply at the next start of auditd)"
  else
    log "auditd: no systemd here, rules are written and load when auditd starts"
  fi
}

# clamscan on demand; signatures refreshed by a daily timer. The clamd daemon and the packaged freshclam daemon stay off.
setup_clamav() {
  command -v clamscan >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  # EL/Fedora ship freshclam.conf with 'Example', which makes freshclam refuse to run
  if [[ -f /etc/freshclam.conf ]] && grep -q '^Example' /etc/freshclam.conf; then
    sed -i -E 's/^Example/#Example/' /etc/freshclam.conf
  fi
  command -v freshclam >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if have_systemd; then
    systemctl disable --now clamav-freshclam.service clamav-daemon.service clamd@scan.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
  if ! compgen -G '/var/lib/clamav/*.c[lv]d' >/dev/null; then
    log "clamav: fetching signatures (freshclam)"
    timeout 300 freshclam --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: freshclam failed, run it by hand before 'clamscan'"
  fi
  local u
  for u in security-freshclam.service security-freshclam.timer; do
    install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/common/systemd/$u" "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
    restorecon_if "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
  done
  if have_systemd; then
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl enable --now security-freshclam.timer >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: could not enable security-freshclam.timer"
  fi
}

# rkhunter compares file hashes with a baseline; without a refresh after package updates every update is a warning.
setup_rkhunter() {
  command -v rkhunter >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if [[ ! -s /var/lib/rkhunter/db/rkhunter.dat ]]; then
    rkhunter --propupd >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: rkhunter --propupd failed"
  fi
  if [[ $FAMILY == debian ]]; then
    if [[ -f /etc/default/rkhunter ]]; then
      sed -i -E 's/^#?APT_AUTOGEN=.*/APT_AUTOGEN="true"/; s/^#?CRON_DAILY_RUN=.*/CRON_DAILY_RUN="false"/' /etc/default/rkhunter
    fi
  elif [[ $FAMILY == el ]]; then
    pkg_ensure python3-dnf-plugin-post-transaction-actions || true
    if [[ -d /etc/dnf/plugins/post-transaction-actions.d ]]; then
      echo '*:any:/usr/bin/rkhunter --propupd' > /etc/dnf/plugins/post-transaction-actions.d/rkhunter.action
    else
      log "WARN: dnf post-transaction-actions plugin missing: run 'rkhunter --propupd' after package updates"
    fi
  else
    log "rkhunter: run 'rkhunter --propupd' after package updates (no dnf hook is installed on Fedora)"
  fi
}

setup_ssh_audit() {
  if command -v ssh-audit >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ! -x /opt/ssh-audit/venv/bin/ssh-audit ]]; then
    PRESENT+=(ssh-audit); return 0
  fi
  if [[ ! -x /opt/ssh-audit/venv/bin/ssh-audit ]] && pkg_ensure ssh-audit; then return 0; fi
  if [[ -f "${SEC_STATE}/ssh-audit.version" && "$(cat "${SEC_STATE}/ssh-audit.version")" == "$SSH_AUDIT_VERSION" ]]; then
    PRESENT+=("ssh-audit ${SSH_AUDIT_VERSION}"); return 0
  fi
  command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_ensure python3 || { MISSING+=("ssh-audit (no package, no python3)"); return 0; }
  [[ $FAMILY == debian ]] && { pkg_ensure python3-venv || true; }
  local req
  DL_TRIED=$((DL_TRIED + 1))
  req=$(mktemp)
  printf 'ssh-audit==%s --hash=sha256:%s\n' "$SSH_AUDIT_VERSION" "$SSH_AUDIT_WHEEL_SHA256" > "$req"
  if rm -rf /opt/ssh-audit/venv && install -d /opt/ssh-audit && python3 -m venv /opt/ssh-audit/venv >/dev/null 2>&1 \
     && /opt/ssh-audit/venv/bin/pip install -q --no-cache-dir --require-hashes --only-binary :all: --no-deps -r "$req" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /opt/ssh-audit/venv/bin/ssh-audit "$@"\n' > /usr/local/bin/ssh-audit
    chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/ssh-audit
    restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/ssh-audit
    install -d "$SEC_STATE"
    echo "$SSH_AUDIT_VERSION" > "${SEC_STATE}/ssh-audit.version"
    INSTALLED+=("ssh-audit ${SSH_AUDIT_VERSION} (venv)")
  else
    DL_FAILED=$((DL_FAILED + 1))
    MISSING+=("ssh-audit (pip install failed)")
  fi
  rm -f "$req"
}

setup_testssl() {
  if command -v testssl >/dev/null 2>&1 \
     || { [[ -x /opt/testssl/testssl.sh ]] && [[ "$(cat "${SEC_STATE}/testssl.version" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "$TESTSSL_VERSION" ]]; }; then
    PRESENT+=(testssl); return 0
  fi
  if pkg_ensure testssl.sh || pkg_ensure testssl; then
    if ! command -v testssl >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v testssl.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      ln -sfn "$(command -v testssl.sh)" /usr/local/bin/testssl
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_ensure git || { SKIPPED+=("testssl.sh (no package, no git)"); return 0; }
  local tmp
  DL_TRIED=$((DL_TRIED + 1))
  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch "v${TESTSSL_VERSION}" https://github.com/testssl/testssl.sh.git "$tmp/t" 2>/dev/null; then
    DL_FAILED=$((DL_FAILED + 1))
    SKIPPED+=("testssl.sh ${TESTSSL_VERSION} (git clone failed)")
  elif [[ "$(git -C "$tmp/t" rev-parse HEAD)" != "$TESTSSL_COMMIT" ]]; then
    log "ERROR: testssl.sh v${TESTSSL_VERSION} is not commit ${TESTSSL_COMMIT}, refusing to install"
    CHECKSUM_FAIL=1
  else
    rm -rf /opt/testssl
    install -d /opt/testssl
    rm -rf "$tmp/t/.git"
    cp -a "$tmp/t/." /opt/testssl/
    printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /opt/testssl/testssl.sh "$@"\n' > /usr/local/bin/testssl
    chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/testssl
    restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/testssl
    install -d "$SEC_STATE"
    echo "$TESTSSL_VERSION" > "${SEC_STATE}/testssl.version"
    INSTALLED+=("testssl ${TESTSSL_VERSION}")
  fi
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

fetch() { curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 --connect-timeout 15 --max-time 900 -o "$2" "$1"; }

install_audit() {
  log "=== audit tools ==="
  local pk=(lynis)
  if [[ $FAMILY == debian ]]; then
    pk+=(auditd debsums)
  else
    pk+=(audit openscap-scanner scap-security-guide)
  fi
  want "${pk[@]}"
  setup_auditd
  setup_ssh_audit
  setup_testssl
  local ds
  ds=$(compgen -G '/usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-*-ds.xml' | head -1 || true)
  if [[ -n "$ds" ]]; then log "openscap: datastream ${ds} (profiles: oscap info ${ds}); evaluation only, never --remediate"; fi
}

install_optional() {
  log "=== opt-in tools ==="
  if (( WANT_AIDE )); then want aide; setup_aide; fi
  if (( WANT_CLAMAV )); then
    if [[ $FAMILY == debian ]]; then want clamav clamav-freshclam; else want clamav "clamav-freshclam|clamav-update"; fi
    setup_clamav
  fi
  if (( WANT_RKHUNTER )); then want rkhunter; setup_rkhunter; fi
  if (( WANT_CHKROOTKIT )); then want chkrootkit; fi
  if (( WANT_ARP )); then want arp-scan; fi
}

# --- network -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
install_network() {
  log "=== network tools ==="
  if [[ $FAMILY == debian ]]; then
    # tshark asks whether non-root users may capture; answer no without a prompt
    if command -v debconf-set-selections >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo 'wireshark-common wireshark-common/install-setuid boolean false' | debconf-set-selections || true
    fi
    want nmap tcpdump tshark iperf3 socat "ncat|netcat-openbsd" whois dnsutils lsof "mtr|mtr-tiny" traceroute iftop nethogs "bmon|nload"
  else
    want nmap tcpdump wireshark-cli iperf3 socat nmap-ncat whois bind-utils lsof mtr traceroute iftop nethogs "bmon|nload"
  fi
}

# --- release binaries --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# release_tool NAME VERSION REPO ASSET SUMS_FILES MODE [BIN]
#   ASSET: file name of the release asset for this arch (empty: no build for this arch)
#   SUMS_FILES: candidate names of the checksums file in the same release
#   MODE: tar (binary inside a tarball), bin (the asset is the binary), tarcfg (tarball with config dir, kept in /opt/NAME)
# Returns 0 on success or skip, 2 on checksum mismatch; the asset is never installed unless its SHA256 matches.
release_tool() {
  local name="$1" ver="$2" repo="$3" asset="$4" sums_list="$5" mode="$6" bin="${7:-$1}"
  local marker="${SEC_STATE}/${name}.version" tmp rc=0
  if [[ -z "$asset" ]]; then
    SKIPPED+=("${name} (no ${ARCH:-$(uname -m)} build)")
    return 0
  fi
  if [[ "$(cat "$marker" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "$ver" && -x "/usr/local/bin/${bin}" ]]; then
    PRESENT+=("${name} ${ver}")
    return 0
  fi
  DL_TRIED=$((DL_TRIED + 1))
  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  release_fetch_install "$tmp" "$name" "$ver" "$repo" "$asset" "$sums_list" "$mode" "$bin" || rc=$?
  rm -rf "$tmp"
  case "$rc" in
    0) INSTALLED+=("${name} ${ver}"); install -d "$SEC_STATE"; echo "$ver" > "$marker" ;;
    2) CHECKSUM_FAIL=1; DL_FAILED=$((DL_FAILED + 1)); SKIPPED+=("${name} ${ver} (CHECKSUM MISMATCH, not installed)") ;;
    *) DL_FAILED=$((DL_FAILED + 1)); SKIPPED+=("${name} ${ver} (not downloaded)") ;;
  esac
  return 0
}

release_fetch_install() {
  local tmp="$1" name="$2" ver="$3" repo="$4" asset="$5" sums_list="$6" mode="$7" bin="$8"
  local base="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/v${ver}" s got="" want_sum have_sum src
  if ! fetch "${base}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}"; then
    log "WARN: ${name} ${ver}: cannot download ${base}/${asset}"
    return 1
  fi
  for s in $sums_list; do
    if fetch "${base}/${s}" "${tmp}/sums" 2>/dev/null; then got=1; break; fi
  done
  if [[ -z "$got" ]]; then
    log "WARN: ${name} ${ver}: no checksums file (${sums_list}) in the release, refusing to install unverified"
    return 1
  fi
  want_sum=$(awk -v f="$asset" '{ n = $2; sub(/^\*/, "", n); if (n == f) print $1 }' "${tmp}/sums")
  if [[ -z "$want_sum" && "$(grep -c . "${tmp}/sums")" -eq 1 ]]; then
    want_sum=$(awk '{ print $1 }' "${tmp}/sums")   # single-asset .sha256 file
  fi
  if [[ ! "$want_sum" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$ ]]; then
    log "WARN: ${name} ${ver}: ${asset} has no usable entry in the checksums file, refusing to install"
    return 1
  fi
  have_sum=$(sha256sum "${tmp}/${asset}" | awk '{ print $1 }')
  if [[ "${have_sum,,}" != "${want_sum,,}" ]]; then
    log "ERROR: ${name} ${ver}: SHA256 MISMATCH for ${asset} (published ${want_sum}, got ${have_sum}); refusing to install"
    return 2
  fi
  case "$mode" in
    bin)
      install -m 0755 "${tmp}/${asset}" "/usr/local/bin/${bin}"
      ;;
    tar)
      install -d "${tmp}/x"
      tar -xzf "${tmp}/${asset}" -C "${tmp}/x"
      src=$(find "${tmp}/x" -type f -name "$bin" | head -1)
      [[ -n "$src" ]] || { log "WARN: ${name}: ${bin} not found in ${asset}"; return 1; }
      install -m 0755 "$src" "/usr/local/bin/${bin}"
      ;;
    tarcfg)
      install -d "${tmp}/x"
      tar -xzf "${tmp}/${asset}" -C "${tmp}/x"
      [[ -f "${tmp}/x/${bin}" ]] || { log "WARN: ${name}: ${bin} not found in ${asset}"; return 1; }
      rm -rf "/opt/${name}"
      install -d "/opt/${name}"
      cp -a "${tmp}/x/." "/opt/${name}/"
      chmod 755 "/opt/${name}/${bin}"
      printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec /opt/%s/%s --config-dir /opt/%s/cfg --config /opt/%s/cfg/config.yaml "$@"\n' \
        "$name" "$bin" "$name" "$name" > "/usr/local/bin/${bin}"
      chmod 755 "/usr/local/bin/${bin}"
      ;;
  esac
  restorecon_if "/usr/local/bin/${bin}"
  return 0
}

install_scan() {
  log "=== scanners (release binaries, SHA256 verified) ==="
  if [[ -z "$ARCH" ]]; then
    DL_TRIED=$((DL_TRIED + 1)); DL_FAILED=$((DL_FAILED + 1))
    SKIPPED+=("scan tools (unsupported architecture $(uname -m))")
    return 0
  fi
  command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_ensure curl || { DL_TRIED=$((DL_TRIED + 1)); DL_FAILED=$((DL_FAILED + 1)); SKIPPED+=("scan tools (curl missing)"); return 0; }
  local a="$ARCH" big small x
  if [[ $ARCH == amd64 ]]; then big=64bit; small=x86_64; x=x64; else big=ARM64; small=arm64; x=arm64; fi
  if (( WANT_SCAN )); then
    release_tool trivy "$TRIVY_VERSION" aquasecurity/trivy "trivy_${TRIVY_VERSION}_Linux-${big}.tar.gz" \
      "trivy_${TRIVY_VERSION}_checksums.txt" tar
    release_tool gitleaks "$GITLEAKS_VERSION" gitleaks/gitleaks "gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_linux_${x}.tar.gz" \
      "gitleaks_${GITLEAKS_VERSION}_checksums.txt" tar
    release_tool hadolint "$HADOLINT_VERSION" hadolint/hadolint "hadolint-linux-${small}" \
      "hadolint-linux-${small}.sha256" bin
    release_tool cosign "$COSIGN_VERSION" sigstore/cosign "cosign-linux-${a}" \
      "cosign_checksums.txt" bin cosign
    release_tool osv-scanner "$OSV_SCANNER_VERSION" google/osv-scanner "osv-scanner_linux_${a}" \
      "osv-scanner_SHA256SUMS" bin
    release_tool trufflehog "$TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION" trufflesecurity/trufflehog "trufflehog_${TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION}_linux_${a}.tar.gz" \
      "trufflehog_${TRUFFLEHOG_VERSION}_checksums.txt" tar
    release_tool dockle "$DOCKLE_VERSION" goodwithtech/dockle "dockle_${DOCKLE_VERSION}_Linux-${big}.tar.gz" \
      "dockle_${DOCKLE_VERSION}_checksums.txt" tar
  fi
  if (( WANT_GRYPE )); then
    release_tool grype "$GRYPE_VERSION" anchore/grype "grype_${GRYPE_VERSION}_linux_${a}.tar.gz" \
      "grype_${GRYPE_VERSION}_checksums.txt" tar
  fi
  if (( WANT_SYFT )); then
    release_tool syft "$SYFT_VERSION" anchore/syft "syft_${SYFT_VERSION}_linux_${a}.tar.gz" \
      "syft_${SYFT_VERSION}_checksums.txt" tar
  fi
  if (( WANT_K8S )); then
    release_tool kubescape "$KUBESCAPE_VERSION" kubescape/kubescape "kubescape_${KUBESCAPE_VERSION}_linux_${a}.tar.gz" \
      "checksums.sha256 kubescape_${KUBESCAPE_VERSION}_checksums.txt checksums.txt" tar
    release_tool kube-bench "$KUBE_BENCH_VERSION" aquasecurity/kube-bench "kube-bench_${KUBE_BENCH_VERSION}_linux_${a}.tar.gz" \
      "kube-bench_${KUBE_BENCH_VERSION}_checksums.txt checksums.txt" tarcfg
  fi
}

# --- kali helper -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
install_kali() {
  log "=== kali helper (container only) ==="
  install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/common/kali" /usr/local/bin/kali
  install -d -m 0755 /usr/local/share/kali-tools
  install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/common/security/kali/Dockerfile" /usr/local/share/kali-tools/Dockerfile
  restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/kali /usr/local/share/kali-tools/Dockerfile
  INSTALLED+=("kali helper")
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: docker is not installed; 'kali' needs it (this script does not install Docker)"
}

# --- audit timer -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
install_timer() {
  log "=== weekly audit timer ==="
  install -d -m 0750 "$AUDIT_LOG_DIR"
  install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/common/security-audit-run.sh" /usr/local/sbin/security-audit-run
  local u
  for u in security-audit.service security-audit.timer; do
    install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/common/systemd/$u" "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
    restorecon_if "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
  done
  restorecon_if /usr/local/sbin/security-audit-run
  if have_systemd; then
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl enable --now security-audit.timer >/dev/null
    systemctl list-timers security-audit.timer --no-pager | head -3
  else
    log "WARN: no systemd here, timer files installed but not enabled"
  fi
}

(( WANT_AUDIT ))   && install_audit
(( WANT_AIDE || WANT_CLAMAV || WANT_RKHUNTER || WANT_CHKROOTKIT || WANT_ARP )) && install_optional
(( WANT_NETWORK )) && install_network
(( WANT_SCAN || WANT_GRYPE || WANT_SYFT || WANT_K8S )) && install_scan
(( WANT_KALI ))    && install_kali
(( WANT_TIMER ))   && install_timer

log "installed now (${#INSTALLED[@]}): ${INSTALLED[*]:-}"
log "already present (${#PRESENT[@]}): ${PRESENT[*]:-}"
if (( ${#MISSING[@]} )); then log "WARN: not available on this release (${#MISSING[@]}): ${MISSING[*]}"; fi
if (( ${#SKIPPED[@]} )); then log "WARN: skipped (${#SKIPPED[@]}): ${SKIPPED[*]}"; fi
for c in lynis rkhunter chkrootkit aide auditctl clamscan oscap ssh-audit testssl nmap tcpdump tshark iperf3 socat ncat \
         trivy grype syft gitleaks hadolint dockle cosign osv-scanner trufflehog kubescape kube-bench kali; do
  if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '  %-12s ok\n' "$c"; fi
done
log "Use these tools only on systems you own or are authorized to test."
if (( CHECKSUM_FAIL )); then
  die "at least one download failed its SHA256 check and was not installed (see ERROR lines above)"
fi
if (( DL_TRIED > 0 && DL_FAILED == DL_TRIED )); then
  die "every download failed (${DL_FAILED} of ${DL_TRIED}), nothing was installed (see WARN lines above)"
fi
if (( DL_FAILED > 0 )); then
  log "WARN: ${DL_FAILED} of ${DL_TRIED} downloads failed, the others were installed"
fi
log "OK"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/security-tools.sh"

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/kali" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# kali: Kali Linux tools in a Docker container, nothing offensive is installed on the host.
# Use only against systems you own or are authorized to test.
set -Eeuo pipefail

IMAGE="${KALI_IMAGE_NAME:-local/kali-tools}"
VOLUME="${KALI_VOLUME:-kali-home}"
HOME_IN=/home/kali

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
Usage: kali [--host-net] [COMMAND [ARGS...]]
       kali update | remove [-y] | --help

Runs Kali Linux (kalilinux/kali-rolling, headless tool set) in a container that is deleted on exit.
````
