  # Grafana encrypts stored credentials (data source passwords, API keys) with secret_key, which is a public default unless set.
  # Generated only on a first install: data that exists under the default key (a volume left over from an earlier install) cannot be
  # read with a new one, so there the default stays. The key belongs next to every backup archive (runner/README.md).
  sk=""
  # A failed `docker volume ls` (daemon down) must not read as "no volume": a key generated over a default-key volume locks its data.
  vols=$(docker volume ls -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=monitoring --filter label=com.docker.compose.volume=grafana-data) \
    || die "cannot list docker volumes (is the Docker daemon running?)"
  if [[ -z "$vols" ]]; then
    sk=$(head -c 96 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | cut -c1-40)
  else
    # The volume may have been written under a key of the earlier install; this run has no way to know it, so it adds none.
    log "NOTE: a Grafana data volume exists, so no new encryption key is generated and Grafana uses its built-in default key"
    log "NOTE: if the earlier install's .env had a GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY line, put that same line back in ${DIR}/.env; Grafana is started by this run on the default key, so after adding it run: cd ${DIR} && sudo docker compose up -d grafana (recreates Grafana with the key). An existing .env is kept, so restoring the earlier .env before the installer also works; see runner/README.md, Grafana upgrade and rollback"
  fi
  (umask 077
   sed "s/^GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=.*/GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${pw}/" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/env.example" | grep -v '^#' > "$DIR/.env"
   if [[ -n "$sk" ]]; then printf 'GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY=%s\n' "$sk" >> "$DIR/.env"; fi)
  unset pw sk vols
fi
chmod 600 "$DIR/.env"
stack_ids "$DIR"
own_stack_dir "$DIR"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

prom_image=$(awk '/image: prom\/prometheus/ { print $2 }' "$DIR/docker-compose.yml")
jq empty "$DIR/grafana/dashboards/gitlab-runner.json"
docker compose -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml" config -q
docker run --rm --user "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" --entrypoint promtool -v "$DIR/prometheus:/etc/prometheus:ro" "$prom_image" \
  check config /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml

cd "$DIR"
docker compose pull -q
chown_volumes "$DIR"
docker compose up -d

for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/ready >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 2
done
for _ in $(seq 1 15); do
  down=$(curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '[.data.activeTargets[] | select(.health != "up")] | length')
  [[ "$down" == "0" ]] && break
  sleep 2
done

docker compose ps --format 'table {{.Service}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Status}}'
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/targets | jq -r '.data.activeTargets[] | "\(.labels.job)\t\(.health)\t\(.lastError)"'
ss -ltn | awk 'NR==1 || /:(9090|9100|3000|9252) /'

exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk '/:(9090|9100|3000) / && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || die "a monitoring port is not bound to 127.0.0.1"
log "OK: monitoring up. Grafana password: sudo grep GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD $DIR/.env"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/monitoring.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/docker-compose.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
name: monitoring

services:
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.15.1
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 512m
    command:
      - --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml
      - --storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.time=15d
      - --storage.tsdb.retention.size=2GB
      - --web.listen-address=127.0.0.1:9090
      - --web.enable-lifecycle
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts.yml:/etc/prometheus/alerts.yml:ro
      - prometheus-data:/prometheus

  node-exporter:
    image: prom/node-exporter:v1.12.1
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    pid: host
    security_opt:
      - label=disable
    mem_limit: 64m
    command:
      - --path.rootfs=/host
      - --web.listen-address=127.0.0.1:9100
    volumes:
      - /:/host:ro,rslave

  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:13.3.0
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    # Grafana 13 migrates dashboards and folders into unified storage on the first start; 512 MB is the documented minimum.
    mem_limit: 512m
    env_file: .env
    depends_on: [prometheus]
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana-data:/var/lib/grafana

volumes:
  prometheus-data:
  grafana-data:
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/docker-compose.yml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/env.example" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
# Copied to /opt/monitoring/.env by runner/install/monitoring.sh; the password is generated there.
# On a first install the installer also appends GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY (random, 40 characters). Grafana encrypts stored credentials
# with it; without it Grafana uses a default key that is public, so a copy of grafana.db could be decrypted by anyone. Never add or
# change it on an install that already has data: what was encrypted under the old key becomes unreadable. Keep the key with every
# backup archive (runner/README.md, "Grafana upgrade and rollback").
GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=generated-on-install
GF_SERVER_HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1
GF_SERVER_HTTP_PORT=3000
GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
GF_ANALYTICS_REPORTING_ENABLED=false
GF_ANALYTICS_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/env.example"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus/alerts.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
groups:
  - name: runner-host
    rules:
      - alert: GitLabRunnerDown
        expr: up{job="gitlab-runner"} == 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: GitLab Runner metrics endpoint is down
      - alert: DiskSpaceHigh
        expr: (1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/",fstype!="rootfs"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/",fstype!="rootfs"}) * 100 > 80
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: Root filesystem usage above 80%
      - alert: MemoryHigh
        expr: (1 - node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes / node_memory_MemTotal_bytes) * 100 > 90
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: Memory usage above 90%
      - alert: RunnerJobFailures
        expr: sum(increase(gitlab_runner_failed_jobs_total[30m])) > 3
        for: 0m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: More than 3 runner job failures in 30 minutes
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus/alerts.yml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus/prometheus.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
  evaluation_interval: 15s

rule_files:
  - /etc/prometheus/alerts.yml

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: prometheus
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:9090"]
  - job_name: node
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:9100"]
  - job_name: gitlab-runner
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:9252"]
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus/prometheus.yml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/grafana/dashboards"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/gitlab-runner.json" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
{
  "uid": "gitlab-runner-host",
  "title": "GitLab Runner Host",
  "schemaVersion": 39,
  "version": 1,
  "refresh": "30s",
  "time": { "from": "now-6h", "to": "now" },
  "tags": ["gitlab", "runner"],
  "panels": [
    {
      "id": 1, "type": "stat", "title": "Runner up",
      "gridPos": { "h": 4, "w": 6, "x": 0, "y": 0 },
      "datasource": { "type": "prometheus", "uid": "prometheus" },
      "fieldConfig": { "defaults": { "mappings": [ { "type": "value", "options": { "0": { "text": "DOWN", "color": "red" }, "1": { "text": "UP", "color": "green" } } } ], "color": { "mode": "thresholds" }, "thresholds": { "mode": "absolute", "steps": [ { "color": "red", "value": null }, { "color": "green", "value": 1 } ] } } },
      "targets": [ { "refId": "A", "expr": "up{job=\"gitlab-runner\"}" } ]
    },
    {
      "id": 2, "type": "stat", "title": "Running jobs",
      "gridPos": { "h": 4, "w": 6, "x": 6, "y": 0 },
      "datasource": { "type": "prometheus", "uid": "prometheus" },
      "targets": [ { "refId": "A", "expr": "sum(gitlab_runner_jobs) or vector(0)" } ]
    },
    {
      "id": 3, "type": "stat", "title": "Concurrent limit",
      "gridPos": { "h": 4, "w": 6, "x": 12, "y": 0 },
      "datasource": { "type": "prometheus", "uid": "prometheus" },
      "targets": [ { "refId": "A", "expr": "gitlab_runner_concurrent" } ]
    },
    {
      "id": 4, "type": "gauge", "title": "Disk used",
      "gridPos": { "h": 4, "w": 6, "x": 18, "y": 0 },

      "targets": [ { "refId": "A", "expr": "(1 - node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint=\"/\",fstype!=\"rootfs\"} / node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint=\"/\",fstype!=\"rootfs\"}) * 100" } ]
    },

    },
    {
      "id": 7, "type": "timeseries", "title": "CPU usage",

}

<a id="logging"></a>
## Logging: Loki + Grafana Alloy

Container logs (not CI jobs) and the journal, 7 days. Run after monitoring so Grafana gets the Loki datasource.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/logging.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log collection: Loki (storage, 7 days) + Grafana Alloy (container logs and the systemd journal).
# CI job containers are not collected, their output is the job log in GitLab.
# Alloy reads the Docker socket, which is root-equivalent on the host. Everything listens on 127.0.0.1.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR=/opt/logging
MON=/opt/monitoring
PROM_CFG="${MON}/prometheus/prometheus.yml"
DATASOURCE="${MON}/grafana/provisioning/datasources/loki.yml"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs Loki + Grafana Alloy into $DIR and adds Loki to Grafana if monitoring is installed"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
mon_ids
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not installed"
docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker compose plugin missing"
command -v jq >/dev/null || pkg_install jq
if [[ -f "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml" ]]; then
  log "${DIR} exists: re-applying the repo files and finishing the setup (safe after a failed run)"
elif ss -ltn | awk '$4 ~ /:(3100|9096|12345)$/' | grep -q .; then
  die "port 3100, 9096 or 12345 already in use"
fi
[[ -f /etc/machine-id ]] || die "/etc/machine-id missing, the journal cannot be read"

if [[ ! -d /var/log/journal ]]; then
  log "enabling persistent journal in /var/log/journal"
  install -d -m 2755 -g systemd-journal /var/log/journal
  systemd-tmpfiles --create --prefix /var/log/journal
  systemctl restart systemd-journald
fi

selinux_label_dir "$DIR"
cp -a "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/docker-compose.yml" "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/loki.yaml" "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/config.alloy" "${DIR}/"
stack_ids "$DIR" logging
own_stack_dir "$DIR"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

loki_image=$(awk '/image: grafana\/loki/ { print $2 }' "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml")
alloy_image=$(awk '/image: grafana\/alloy/ { print $2 }' "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml")

cd "$DIR"
docker compose config -q
docker compose pull -q
docker run --rm --user "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" -v "${DIR}/loki.yaml:/etc/loki/config.yaml:ro" "$loki_image" \
  -config.file=/etc/loki/config.yaml -verify-config || die "Loki rejected loki.yaml"
docker run --rm --user "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" --entrypoint /bin/alloy -v "${DIR}/config.alloy:/config/config.alloy:ro" "$alloy_image" \
  fmt /config/config.alloy >/dev/null || die "Alloy rejected config.alloy"
chown_volumes "$DIR"
docker compose up -d --force-recreate

ready=0
for _ in $(seq 1 45); do
  if curl -fsS -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:3100/ready >/dev/null 2>&1 && curl -fsS -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:12345/-/ready >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
if (( ! ready )); then
  docker compose logs --tail 40
  die "Loki or Alloy did not become ready"
fi

if [[ -d "${MON}/grafana/provisioning/datasources" ]]; then
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/grafana-datasource.yml" "$DATASOURCE"
  chown "root:${MON_USER}" "$DATASOURCE"
  chmod 640 "$DATASOURCE"
  restorecon_if "$DATASOURCE"
  (cd "$MON" && docker compose restart grafana >/dev/null)
  log "Loki added to Grafana as a datasource"
fi
if [[ -f "$PROM_CFG" ]] && ! grep -q 'job_name: loki' "$PROM_CFG"; then
  backup "$PROM_CFG"
  prom_jobs_logging >> "$PROM_CFG"
  curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/reload || log "WARN: prometheus reload failed"
fi

marker="logging-install-check-$(date +%s)"
logger -t logging-install -- "$marker"
found=0
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  n=$(curl -fsS -G -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range \
        --data-urlencode "query={source=\"journal\"} |= \"${marker}\"" --data-urlencode "since=10m" 2>/dev/null \
      | jq '.data.result | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [[ "${n:-0}" != "0" ]]; then
    found=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
if (( found )); then
  log "journal -> Alloy -> Loki works"
else
  log "WARN: test line not in Loki yet, check: docker compose -f ${DIR}/docker-compose.yml logs alloy"
fi

docker compose ps --format 'table {{.Service}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Status}}'
exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk '/:(3100|9096|12345) / && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || die "a logging port is not bound to 127.0.0.1"
log "OK: logs in Grafana > Explore > Loki, e.g. {unit=\"gitlab-runner.service\"} or {compose_project=\"registry-cache\"}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/logging.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/logging"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/logging/config.alloy" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
// Container logs and the systemd journal to the local Loki.
// CI job containers are skipped: their output is already the job log in GitLab (or in GitHub, for the pods of the GitHub Actions runner).

logging {
  level = "warn"
}

loki.write "local" {
  endpoint {
    url = "http://127.0.0.1:3100/loki/api/v1/push"
  }
}

discovery.docker "containers" {
  host             = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
  refresh_interval = "15s"
}

discovery.relabel "containers" {
  targets = []

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_gitlab_gitlab_runner_managed"]
    regex         = "true"
    action        = "drop"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_io_server_init_github_runner"]
    regex         = "job"
    action        = "drop"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_name"]
    regex         = "/(.*)"
    target_label  = "container"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_project"]
    target_label  = "compose_project"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_service"]
    target_label  = "compose_service"
  }
}

loki.source.docker "containers" {
  host          = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
  targets       = discovery.docker.containers.targets
  labels        = {source = "docker"}
  relabel_rules = discovery.relabel.containers.rules
  forward_to    = [loki.write.local.receiver]
}

loki.relabel "journal" {
  forward_to = []

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__journal__systemd_unit"]
    target_label  = "unit"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__journal_priority_keyword"]
    target_label  = "level"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__journal_syslog_identifier"]
    target_label  = "identifier"
  }
}

loki.source.journal "system" {
  path          = "/var/log/journal"
  max_age       = "12h"
  labels        = {source = "journal"}
  relabel_rules = loki.relabel.journal.rules
  forward_to    = [loki.write.local.receiver]
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/logging/config.alloy"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/logging"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/logging/docker-compose.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
name: logging

services:
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.7.9
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 512m
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/loki/config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./loki.yaml:/etc/loki/config.yaml:ro
      - loki-data:/loki

  # Runs as the monitoring service user. Docker socket and journal access come from group_add
  # (docker and systemd-journal); note that reading the Docker socket is root-equivalent on the host.
  # The journal group is added by docker-compose.override.yml, which stack_ids (common/lib.sh) writes
  # only when its gid differs from the docker gid: compose rejects a group_add list with equal items.
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.21.3
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 256m
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    group_add:
      - "${DOCKER_GID:?run runner/install/logging.sh}"
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt:
      - label=disable
      - no-new-privileges:true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=127.0.0.1:12345
      - --storage.path=/data
      - --disable-reporting
      - /config/config.alloy
    volumes:
      - ./config.alloy:/config/config.alloy:ro
      - alloy-data:/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log/journal:/var/log/journal:ro
      - /etc/machine-id:/etc/machine-id:ro
    depends_on: [loki]

volumes:
  loki-data:
  alloy-data:
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/logging/docker-compose.yml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/logging"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/logging/grafana-datasource.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
apiVersion: 1
datasources:
  - name: Loki
    uid: loki
    type: loki
    access: proxy
    url: http://127.0.0.1:3100
    editable: false
    jsonData:
      maxLines: 1000
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/logging/grafana-datasource.yml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/logging"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/logging/loki.yaml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
auth_enabled: false

server:
  http_listen_address: 127.0.0.1
  http_listen_port: 3100
  grpc_listen_address: 127.0.0.1
  grpc_listen_port: 9096
  log_level: warn

common:
  instance_addr: 127.0.0.1
  path_prefix: /loki
  replication_factor: 1
  storage:
    filesystem:
      chunks_directory: /loki/chunks
      rules_directory: /loki/rules
  ring:
    kvstore:
      store: inmemory

schema_config:
  configs:
    - from: 2024-04-01
      store: tsdb
      object_store: filesystem
      schema: v13
      index:
        prefix: index_
        period: 24h

limits_config:
  retention_period: 168h
  ingestion_rate_mb: 4
  ingestion_burst_size_mb: 8
  max_query_series: 5000
  allow_structured_metadata: true
  volume_enabled: true

compactor:
  working_directory: /loki/compactor
  compaction_interval: 10m
  retention_enabled: true
  retention_delete_delay: 2h
  delete_request_store: filesystem

analytics:
  reporting_enabled: false
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/logging/loki.yaml"

echo "files written to $R: 6"
bash "$R/runner/install/logging.sh" </dev/null

````

<a id="npm-cache"></a>
## npm cache (Verdaccio)

Needs a registered runner. Points `npm` and `yarn` in jobs at the cache. Run it while no jobs are running. Verdaccio binds to the docker0 IP: if it changes (`bip` in daemon.json), rerun this block or `runner/install/update.sh`.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/npm-cache.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verdaccio npm pull-through cache on the docker0 bridge IP, exposed to CI jobs via runner env.
# If the cache is down, npm ci in jobs fails (npm has no automatic fallback).
# Storage and the server secret are prepared by the container itself at every start (config "start" in the compose file):
# storage of an older major is moved aside to backup-*, Verdaccio 7 needs a secret of exactly 32 characters.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR=/opt/npm-cache
CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs Verdaccio into $DIR and points runner jobs at it"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
require_compose_min 2.23.1 "npm-cache"   # the compose file carries its start script as inline "configs: content:"
if ! { [[ -f "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$CFG"; }; then die "runner not registered yet, run runner/install/register-runner.sh first"; fi

BRIDGE_IP=$(ip -4 -o addr show docker0 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $4 }' | cut -d/ -f1)
[[ -n "$BRIDGE_IP" ]] || die "docker0 bridge not found"
REG="http://${BRIDGE_IP}:4873/"
require_runner_idle

selinux_label_dir "$DIR"
sed "s/172\.17\.0\.1:4873/${BRIDGE_IP}:4873/" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/npm-cache/config.yaml" > "$DIR/config.yaml"
sed "s/172\.17\.0\.1:4873/${BRIDGE_IP}:4873/" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/npm-cache/docker-compose.yml" > "$DIR/docker-compose.yml"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

cd "$DIR"
docker compose config -q
docker compose pull -q
docker compose up -d
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS "${REG}-/ping" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done
curl -fsS "${REG}-/ping" >/dev/null || { docker compose logs --tail 30; die "verdaccio did not start"; }
docker compose logs --no-log-prefix verdaccio 2>&1 | grep '^npm-cache:' || true

exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk -v want="${BRIDGE_IP}:4873" '/:4873 / && $4 != want' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || { ss -ltn | awk '/:4873 /'; die "port 4873 is not bound to ${BRIDGE_IP} only"; }

edit_with_backup "$CFG" runner_env_merge "npm_config_registry=${REG}" "YARN_NPM_REGISTRY_SERVER=${REG}" "YARN_UNSAFE_HTTP_WHITELIST=${BRIDGE_IP}"
systemctl restart gitlab-runner
sleep 3

docker run --rm -e npm_config_registry="$REG" node:22-alpine sh -c \
  'cd /tmp && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install --no-audit --no-fund lodash >/dev/null && echo "npm install via cache OK"' \
  || die "npm install through verdaccio failed"

grep -n 'environment =' "$CFG"
ss -ltn | awk 'NR==1 || /:4873 /'
gitlab-runner verify 2>&1 | grep -E 'is valid|is not valid' || true
log "OK: npm cache at ${REG}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/npm-cache.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/config.yaml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
# Verdaccio 7. The server secret is not a setting here: 7.x reads it only from data/.verdaccio-db.json in the storage and
# accepts exactly 32 characters. The start script in docker-compose.yml creates it (mode 600) and moves older storage aside.
storage: /verdaccio/storage/data
plugins: /verdaccio/plugins

listen:
  - 172.17.0.1:4873

auth:
  htpasswd:
    file: /verdaccio/storage/htpasswd
    max_users: -1

uplinks:
  npmjs:
    url: https://registry.npmjs.org/
    timeout: 60s
    maxage: 30m
    cache: true

packages:
  '@*/*':
    access: $all
    publish: $authenticated
    proxy: npmjs
  '**':
    access: $all
    publish: $authenticated
    proxy: npmjs

server:
  keepAliveTimeout: 60

web:
  enable: false

log:
  type: stdout
  format: pretty
  level: warn
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/config.yaml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/docker-compose.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
name: npm-cache

services:
  verdaccio:
    image: verdaccio/verdaccio:7.0.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 1g
    # The image's default command passes --listen 0.0.0.0:4873, which overrides "listen:" in config.yaml
    # and exposes the cache (access: $all) on every interface. runner/install/npm-cache.sh and update.sh
    # replace 172.17.0.1 below with the docker0 IP, as they do in config.yaml.
    # npm-cache-start.sh (the config below) runs first and then execs verdaccio.
    command: ["sh", "/usr/local/bin/npm-cache-start.sh", "verdaccio", "--config", "/verdaccio/conf/config.yaml", "--listen", "http://172.17.0.1:4873"]
    configs:
      - source: start
        target: /usr/local/bin/npm-cache-start.sh
    volumes:
      - ./config.yaml:/verdaccio/conf/config.yaml:ro
      - verdaccio-storage:/verdaccio/storage

# Runs on every start, so it also covers update.sh, which only syncs this file and config.yaml. In "content:" a literal
# dollar sign is written $$ (compose would interpolate a single one). Inline "content:" needs Docker Compose >= 2.23.1
# (npm-cache.sh and update.sh check it first).
configs:
  start:
    content: |
      set -eu
      S=/verdaccio/storage
      DB=$$S/data/.verdaccio-db.json
      STATE=$$S/.deployed-major
      WANT=7
      say() { echo "npm-cache: $$*" >&2; }
      # live storage = everything except the state file and earlier backups
      live() { for e in "$$S"/* "$$S"/.[!.]*; do [ -e "$$e" ] || continue; case $${e##*/} in backup-*|.deployed-major) ;; *) echo "$$e" ;; esac; done; }
      have=$$(cat "$$STATE" 2>/dev/null || true)
      if [ -z "$$have" ]; then
        if [ -n "$$(live)" ]; then have=6; say "no $$STATE but storage exists: treating it as 6.x"; else have=none; fi
      fi
      if [ "$$have" != "$$WANT" ] && [ -n "$$(live)" ]; then
        B=$$S/backup-$$have.x-$$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
        say "storage of $$have.x found, moving it to $$B (nothing is deleted; $$WANT.x starts empty and refills from npmjs)"
        mkdir "$$B"
        chmod 700 "$$B"
        live | while IFS= read -r e; do mv "$$e" "$$B/"; done
      fi
      # Record the major now, before the secret step: a crash after the move must not make the next start take the fresh 7.x
      # storage for 6.x and move it aside too. Backups can hold old credentials (htpasswd, secret): only the verdaccio uid reads them.
      [ "$$have" = "$$WANT" ] || printf '%s' "$$WANT" > "$$STATE"
      for b in "$$S"/backup-*; do [ -d "$$b" ] && { chmod 700 "$$b" || say "cannot chmod $$b"; }; done
      # 7.x refuses a server secret that is not exactly 32 characters (6.x accepted others), and has no config key or env var for it:
      # it reads it from the storage database. Keep a valid one, otherwise write a new one from the kernel CSPRNG. Never printed.
      mkdir -p "$$S/data"
      cur=$$(sed -n 's/.*"secret":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$$DB" 2>/dev/null || true)
      if [ "$${#cur}" -ne 32 ]; then
        new=$$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')
        [ "$${#new}" -eq 32 ] || { say "cannot generate a secret"; exit 1; }
        if [ -s "$$DB" ]; then
          grep -q '"secret":"' "$$DB" || { say "$$DB has no secret field, not touching it"; exit 1; }
          ( umask 077; sed "s/\"secret\":\"[^\"]*\"/\"secret\":\"$$new\"/" "$$DB" > "$$DB.new" )
        else
          ( umask 077; printf '{"list":[],"secret":"%s"}' "$$new" > "$$DB.new" )
        fi
        mv "$$DB.new" "$$DB"
        say "wrote a new server secret to $$DB (32 characters, mode 600)"
      fi
      chmod 600 "$$DB"
      exec "$$@"

volumes:
  verdaccio-storage:
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/docker-compose.yml"

echo "files written to $R: 4"
bash "$R/runner/install/npm-cache.sh" </dev/null
INSTALL
````

<a id="shared-cache"></a>
## Shared cache /srv/ci-cache

Needs a registered runner. Mounts `/srv/ci-cache` into every job for npm and Sonar. Trusted projects only.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/shared-cache.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared host cache /srv/ci-cache mounted into every job as /ci-cache (npm tarballs, Sonar plugins).
# The cache is shared across all projects on this runner: only use it for trusted projects.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

HOST_DIR=/srv/ci-cache
MOUNT=/ci-cache
CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  mounts $HOST_DIR into all jobs and sets npm_config_cache and SONAR_USER_HOME"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
if ! { [[ -f "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$CFG"; }; then die "runner not registered yet"; fi
require_runner_idle

install -d -m 1777 "$HOST_DIR" "$HOST_DIR/npm" "$HOST_DIR/sonar"
if selinux_on; then
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  grep -q "^${HOST_DIR}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)" || semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${HOST_DIR}(/.*)?"
  restorecon -R "$HOST_DIR"
fi

add_shared_cache() {
  if ! grep -q "${HOST_DIR}:${MOUNT}" "$CFG"; then
    grep -qE '^    volumes = \["/cache"\]' "$CFG" || die "unexpected volumes line in [runners.docker], edit manually"
    sed -i -E "s|^    volumes = \[\"/cache\"\]|    volumes = [\"/cache\", \"${HOST_DIR}:${MOUNT}:rw\"]|" "$CFG"
  fi
  runner_env_merge "npm_config_cache=${MOUNT}/npm" "SONAR_USER_HOME=${MOUNT}/sonar"
}
edit_with_backup "$CFG" add_shared_cache
systemctl restart gitlab-runner
sleep 3

docker run --rm --user 1000:1000 -v "${HOST_DIR}:${MOUNT}:rw" "$HELPER_IMAGE" \
  sh -c "touch ${MOUNT}/npm/.probe && rm ${MOUNT}/npm/.probe && echo 'non-root write OK'" \
  || die "containers cannot write to ${HOST_DIR}"

grep -nE 'volumes =|environment =' "$CFG"
gitlab-runner verify 2>&1 | grep -E 'is valid|is not valid' || true
log "OK: shared cache ${HOST_DIR} mounted as ${MOUNT} in all jobs"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/shared-cache.sh"

echo "files written to $R: 2"
bash "$R/runner/install/shared-cache.sh" </dev/null
INSTALL
````

<a id="github-runner"></a>
## GitHub Actions runner (private repositories)

Optional, needs the per-job limits. Ephemeral just-in-time runners for the private repositories of a GitHub App installation, one job at a time, image builds through a rootless BuildKit sidecar, no Docker socket in jobs. Create the GitHub App first (permissions, no webhook, install on All repositories: see runner/docs/github-runner.md, including its trust requirements and unverified live-host checks), download its private key and copy it to the server, laptop, any directory: `scp app-key.pem ops@SERVER_IP:/home/ops/app-key.pem`. The last line asks for your GitHub user, the App's client ID and the path of the key (`/home/ops/app-key.pem`), runs a self-test that lists which repositories would be served, and only then enables the service. }

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/github-runner.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Opt-in ephemeral GitHub Actions runner for the PRIVATE repositories of one GitHub App installation (a personal account), on this host
# next to the GitLab Runner. Installs the controller (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl) and its systemd unit, the service user
# github-runner, /etc/github-runner/config.env (no secrets) and the GitHub App private key /etc/github-runner/app.pem (mode 0600,
# owner github-runner), pulls the pinned images (common/lib.sh), runs a self-test against GitHub and only then enables the service.
# Each job gets a just-in-time runner in its own pod (network, rootless BuildKit sidecar, runner container); no Docker socket in jobs.
# Needs: Docker, runner/install/job-limits.sh (ci-jobs.slice), a GitHub App (see runner/README.md). Safe to rerun: values already in
# config.env are kept unless you pass them in the environment, a changed file gets a backup.
#
# Asks (read -rp) for what is missing: GH_OWNER (GitHub user), GH_APP_CLIENT_ID (the App's client ID) and the path of the downloaded
# private key (.pem; copied, never printed; delete the download afterwards). Without a terminal pass them in the environment: GH_OWNER,
# GH_APP_CLIENT_ID, GH_KEY_SRC.
# Env (all optional, kept from config.env on a rerun): GH_INSTALLATION_ID (found by itself), GH_LABELS (default
# self-hosted,linux,<arm64|x64>,hetzner), GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID (1), GH_MAX_JOBS (1), GH_POLL_INTERVAL (30), GH_IDLE_TIMEOUT (300),
# GH_EXCLUDE_REPOS, GH_BUILDKIT (1), GH_JOB_CPUS / GH_JOB_MEMORY (the GitLab per-job values from config.toml, else 1.5 / 1536m),
# GH_BUILDKIT_CPUS (1), GH_BUILDKIT_MEMORY (768m), GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL (10.213.0.0/20), GH_MAX_RUNTIME. See runner/README.md.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../common/lib.sh"

ETC=/etc/github-runner
CFG="${ETC}/config.env"
KEY="${ETC}/app.pem"
KEY_RESTART="${ETC}/key-restart-required"
SVC_USER=github-runner
UNIT=github-runner-ctl.service
CTL=/usr/local/bin/github-runner-ctl
SLICE=/etc/systemd/system/ci-jobs.slice
USERNS_DROPIN=/etc/sysctl.d/91-github-runner-userns.conf
GITLAB_CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
DO_PULL=1 DO_SELFTEST=1 DO_START=1 ONLY_SELFTEST=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,/^set -E/{/^set -E/!p}' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  cat <<USAGE

Usage: $0 [--self-test] [--no-self-test] [--no-start] [--no-pull]
  --self-test     only run the self-test with the installed config: mint a JWT, get an installation token, list the repositories and
                  print which would be served (names and visibility); starts and changes nothing
  --no-self-test  install and enable without the live check against GitHub (offline)
  --no-start      enable the service but do not start it
  --no-pull       do not pull the images now (the controller pulls a missing image before its first job)
Removal: see runner/docs/github-runner.md (Remove it). Stop the controller, review and remove only containers and networks labelled
  io.server-init.github-runner=job; never prune unrelated networks. Running pods survive a controller stop.
USAGE
}

while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --self-test) ONLY_SELFTEST=1 ;;
    --no-self-test) DO_SELFTEST=0 ;;
    --no-start) DO_START=0 ;;
    --no-pull) DO_PULL=0 ;;
    *) usage >&2; die "unknown option: $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done
require_root

run_selftest() {
  runuser -u "$SVC_USER" -- env GHR_CONFIG="$CFG" "$CTL" self-test
}

if (( ONLY_SELFTEST )); then
  [[ -x "$CTL" && -f "$CFG" ]] || die "not installed yet: run $0 first"
  run_selftest
  exit $?
fi

# ---- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker is not installed"
systemctl is-active --quiet docker || die "docker is not running"
systemctl cat ci-job-isolation.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ci-job-isolation.service missing: install the runner host tools first"
getent group docker >/dev/null || die "no docker group"
[[ -f "$SLICE" ]] || die "${SLICE} missing: run runner/setup.sh --job-limits first (the pods run inside ci-jobs.slice, which caps all CI jobs together)"
read -r cgdrv cgver < <(docker info --format '{{.CgroupDriver}} {{.CgroupVersion}}' 2>/dev/null || echo "? ?")
[[ "$cgdrv" == systemd && "$cgver" == 2 ]] || die "Docker must use cgroup v2 with the systemd cgroup driver (found: ${cgdrv} v${cgver}); --cgroup-parent ci-jobs.slice needs it"
for t in curl jq openssl; do command -v "$t" >/dev/null || pkg_install "$t"; done
command -v runuser >/dev/null || die "runuser (util-linux) is missing"
[[ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl" && -f "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/systemd/${UNIT}" ]] || die "incomplete copy of the repository"

existing() { # existing KEY: the value in config.env, quotes removed
  [[ -f "$CFG" ]] || return 0
  { grep -m1 "^$1=" "$CFG" || true; } | cut -d= -f2- | sed -E 's/^"(.*)"$/\1/'
}
# pick KEY DEFAULT: environment, else config.env, else DEFAULT
pick() {
  local v=${!1:-}
  [[ -n "$v" ]] || v=$(existing "$1")
  printf '%s' "${v:-$2}"
}

# Rootless BuildKit needs user namespaces for non-root (kernel: user.max_user_namespaces > 0). Only written when it is 0.
buildkit_wanted=$(pick GH_BUILDKIT 1)
if [[ "$buildkit_wanted" == 1 ]]; then
  maxns=$(sysctl -n user.max_user_namespaces 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [[ "$maxns" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( maxns == 0 )); then
    printf '# Written by runner/install/github-runner.sh: rootless BuildKit needs user namespaces.\nuser.max_user_namespaces = 28633\n' > "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new"
    if ! cmp -s "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new" "$USERNS_DROPIN" 2>/dev/null; then mv "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new" "$USERNS_DROPIN"; else rm -f "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new"; fi
    sysctl -q -w user.max_user_namespaces=28633 || log "WARN: could not set user.max_user_namespaces now; it applies after a reboot"
    log "user.max_user_namespaces was 0: set to 28633 (${USERNS_DROPIN}); rootless BuildKit needs it"
  else
    log "user.max_user_namespaces = ${maxns}: ok for rootless BuildKit"
  fi
  if [[ "$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" == 1 ]]; then
    log "WARN: kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 (Ubuntu): rootless BuildKit will fail; set it to 0 in /etc/sysctl.d or use GH_BUILDKIT=0"
  fi
fi

# ---- service user ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOLOGIN=$(command -v nologin || echo /sbin/nologin)
if ! id "$SVC_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  useradd -r -U -M -d /nonexistent -s "$NOLOGIN" -c "GitHub Actions runner controller" "$SVC_USER"
  log "created service user ${SVC_USER}"
fi
usermod -s "$NOLOGIN" "$SVC_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
usermod -L "$SVC_USER" 2>/dev/null || true
usermod -aG docker "$SVC_USER"   # root-equivalent: it is what the controller needs to start the pods
install -d -m 0750 -o root -g "$SVC_USER" "$ETC"

# ---- the key ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
changed=0
src=${GH_KEY_SRC:-}
if [[ -z "$src" && ! -f "$KEY" ]]; then
  [[ -t 0 ]] || die "no private key yet: pass its path in GH_KEY_SRC (the .pem downloaded from the GitHub App page)"
  read -rp "Path of the downloaded GitHub App private key (.pem): " src
fi
if [[ -n "$src" ]]; then
  [[ -f "$src" && -r "$src" ]] || die "cannot read ${src}"
  openssl rsa -in "$src" -passin pass: -noout >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "${src} is not an RSA private key (download it from the GitHub App page, Generate a private key)"
  if ! cmp -s "$src" "$KEY" 2>/dev/null; then
    [[ ! -f "$KEY" ]] || backup "$KEY"
    install -m 0600 -o "$SVC_USER" -g "$SVC_USER" "$src" "$KEY"
    ( umask 077; : > "$KEY_RESTART" )
    changed=1   # clear cached credentials after a successful self-test, even when config and code are unchanged
    log "private key installed: ${KEY} (mode 0600, owner ${SVC_USER})"
  fi
