````bash
# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/image-prewarm.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily pre-pull of all tags of the CI images in a GitLab Container Registry.
# Needs a project deploy token with read_registry scope.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

CRANE_VERSION="${CRANE_VERSION:-v0.20.2}"
CONF=/etc/ci-prewarm.conf
REPOS="${REPOS:-mirror/alpine mirror/node mirror/playwright mirror/snyk mirror/sonar-scanner-cli docker}"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0
Asks for the full path of one image (copy icon in Container Registry) and a deploy token.
Env: REPOS (space separated, relative to the project registry), CRANE_VERSION
USAGE
  exit 0
fi
require_root

case "$(uname -m)" in
  aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
  x86_64)  arch=x86_64 ;;
  *) die "unsupported arch $(uname -m)" ;;
esac

if ! command -v crane >/dev/null; then
  log "installing crane ${CRANE_VERSION}"
  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  base="https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/releases/download/${CRANE_VERSION}"
  tarball="go-containerregistry_Linux_${arch}.tar.gz"
  curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/$tarball" "$base/$tarball"
  curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/checksums.txt" "$base/checksums.txt"
  (cd "$tmp" && grep " ${tarball}\$" checksums.txt | sha256sum -c -) || { rm -rf "$tmp"; die "crane checksum mismatch"; }
  tar -xzf "$tmp/$tarball" -C "$tmp" crane
  install -m 0755 "$tmp/crane" /usr/local/bin/crane
  rm -rf "$tmp"
  restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/crane
fi

read -ra repo_list <<<"$REPOS"
[[ ${#repo_list[@]} -gt 0 ]] || die "REPOS is empty"
first_repo="${repo_list[0]}"
read -rp "Paste the full path of ${first_repo} (copy icon in Container Registry): " ref
ref="${ref%%:*}"
[[ "$ref" == registry.gitlab.com/*/"${first_repo}" ]] || die "expected registry.gitlab.com/.../${first_repo}, got: $ref"
BASE="${ref%/"${first_repo}"}"
# /etc/ci-prewarm.conf is sourced as root: accept only plain registry path characters.
path_re='^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$'
[[ "$BASE" =~ $path_re ]] || die "registry path contains unexpected characters: $BASE"
for r in "${repo_list[@]}"; do [[ "$r" =~ $path_re ]] || die "REPOS entry contains unexpected characters: $r"; done

read -rp "Deploy token username (gitlab+deploy-token-...): " dt_user
read -rsp "Deploy token: " dt_token; echo
[[ "$dt_user" == gitlab+deploy-token-* ]] || die "unexpected deploy token username"
printf '%s' "$dt_token" | docker login registry.gitlab.com -u "$dt_user" --password-stdin >/dev/null
unset dt_token
chmod 600 /root/.docker/config.json
crane ls "$BASE/$first_repo" >/dev/null || die "cannot list $BASE/$first_repo with this token"

{
  printf 'BASE=%q\n' "$BASE"
  printf 'REPOS=(%s)\n' "$(printf '%q ' "${repo_list[@]}")"
} > "$CONF"
chmod 644 "$CONF"

install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/runner/scripts/ci-image-prewarm.sh" /usr/local/bin/ci-image-prewarm.sh
restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/ci-image-prewarm.sh
for u in ci-image-prewarm.service ci-image-prewarm.timer; do
  install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/runner/systemd/$u" "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
  restorecon_if "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
done
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now ci-image-prewarm.timer

log "first prewarm run (playwright images are large, this can take minutes)"
systemctl start ci-image-prewarm.service || true
journalctl -t ci-image-prewarm --since "-30min" --no-pager -o cat | grep -E 'OK|NO ARM|FAIL|summary' | sed -E 's/^[0-9T:-]+ //'
log "NO ARM lines: re-mirror those tags with crane copy (see runner/ci/mirror-images.yml)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/image-prewarm.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/ci-image-prewarm.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Pre-pull every tag of the CI images listed in /etc/ci-prewarm.conf so jobs start from local images.
set -Eeuo pipefail

CONF="${CONF:-/etc/ci-prewarm.conf}"
log() { logger -t ci-image-prewarm -- "$*"; echo "$(date +%FT%T) $*"; }

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  (pulls all tags of REPOS under BASE from $CONF)"
  exit 0
fi
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
command -v crane >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "ERROR: crane not installed"; exit 1; }
[[ -f "$CONF" ]] || { log "ERROR: $CONF not found"; exit 1; }

BASE=""
REPOS=()
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
source "$CONF"
[[ -n "$BASE" && ${#REPOS[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { log "ERROR: BASE or REPOS empty in $CONF"; exit 1; }

exec 9>/run/ci-image-prewarm.lock
flock -n 9 || { log "another prewarm is running, exit"; exit 0; }

ok=0; noarm=0; fail=0
for repo in "${REPOS[@]}"; do
  if ! tags=$(crane ls "${BASE}/${repo}" 2>&1); then
    log "FAIL    ${BASE}/${repo}: cannot list tags: ${tags}"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
    continue
  fi
  for tag in $tags; do
    ref="${BASE}/${repo}:${tag}"
    if out=$(docker pull -q "$ref" 2>&1); then
      log "OK      $ref"
      ok=$((ok + 1))
    elif grep -qiE 'no matching manifest|does not match the specified platform' <<<"$out"; then
      log "NO ARM  $ref"
      noarm=$((noarm + 1))
    else
      log "FAIL    $ref: $out"
      fail=$((fail + 1))
    fi
  done
done

log "summary: ok=${ok} no_arm=${noarm} failed=${fail}, disk: $(df -h --output=pcent / | tail -1 | xargs)"
(( fail == 0 ))
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/ci-image-prewarm.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/systemd"
cat > "$R/runner/systemd/ci-image-prewarm.service" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
[Unit]
Description=Pre-pull CI images from GitLab Registry
After=docker.service network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ci-image-prewarm.sh
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=idle
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/systemd/ci-image-prewarm.service"

install -d "$R/runner/systemd"
cat > "$R/runner/systemd/ci-image-prewarm.timer" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
[Unit]
Description=Pre-pull CI images daily and after boot

[Timer]
OnBootSec=5min
OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:15:00
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/systemd/ci-image-prewarm.timer"

echo "files written to $R: 5"
INSTALL
sudo bash /root/server-init-config/runner/install/image-prewarm.sh
````

## Grafana on a domain (HTTPS via Caddy)

First: A record to the server IP, ports 80/443 open in the Hetzner Firewall. Replace `grafana.example.com` and `you@example.com` on the last line with your domain and email.

````bash

R=/root/server-init-config

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi

  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"

  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)

  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/grafana-domain.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish Grafana on an HTTPS domain via Caddy (automatic Let's Encrypt).
# Requires: monitoring installed, A record pointing to this server (DNS only, no proxy), ports 80/443 open.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DOMAIN="${DOMAIN:-}"
ACME_EMAIL="${ACME_EMAIL:-}"
CADDY_IMAGE="${CADDY_IMAGE:-caddy:2.10.0}"
DIR=/opt/monitoring

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" || -z "$DOMAIN" || -z "$ACME_EMAIL" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: DOMAIN=grafana.example.com ACME_EMAIL=you@example.com $0"
  [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]] && exit 0
  exit 1
fi
require_root
[[ -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml" && -f "$DIR/.env" ]] || die "monitoring stack not found in $DIR"
command -v openssl >/dev/null || pkg_install openssl

server_ip=$(curl -fsS --max-time 5 http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/public-ipv4 2>/dev/null || curl -4 -fsS --max-time 5 https://ifconfig.me)
dns_ip=$(getent ahostsv4 "$DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1 { print $1 }')
log "server ip: $server_ip, dns ip: ${dns_ip:-<none>}"
[[ -n "$dns_ip" ]] || die "$DOMAIN does not resolve yet"
[[ "$dns_ip" == "$server_ip" ]] || die "$DOMAIN points to $dns_ip, expected $server_ip (DNS proxy enabled?)"
if ss -ltn | awk '$4 ~ /:(80|443)$/' | grep -q .; then die "ports 80/443 already in use"; fi

# Let's Encrypt (HTTP-01, TLS-ALPN) and visitors reach Caddy on the host network: open 80/443 in the host firewall if
# one runs. Only added, never removed, and SSH rules are not touched.
if command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld; then
  for svc in http https; do
    firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-service="$svc" >/dev/null && firewall-cmd --zone=public --add-service="$svc" >/dev/null \
      || die "cannot open ${svc} in firewalld"
  done
  log "firewalld: http and https opened in the public zone"
elif command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 && ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active'; then
  ufw allow 80/tcp >/dev/null && ufw allow 443/tcp >/dev/null || die "cannot open 80/443 in ufw"
  log "ufw: 80/tcp and 443/tcp opened"
fi

set_env() {
  if grep -q "^$1=" "$DIR/.env"; then sed -i "s|^$1=.*|$1=$2|" "$DIR/.env"; else echo "$1=$2" >> "$DIR/.env"; fi
}
set_grafana_env() {
  set_env GF_SERVER_DOMAIN "$DOMAIN"
  set_env GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL "https://${DOMAIN}/"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_COOKIE_SECURE "true"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_COOKIE_SAMESITE "lax"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_DISABLE_GRAVATAR "true"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY "true"
}
edit_with_backup "$DIR/.env" set_grafana_env
chmod 600 "$DIR/.env"

install -d -m 0755 "$DIR/caddy"
sed -e "s|__DOMAIN__|${DOMAIN}|g" -e "s|__ACME_EMAIL__|${ACME_EMAIL}|g" \
  "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/caddy/Caddyfile.tmpl" > "$DIR/caddy/Caddyfile"

cat > "$DIR/docker-compose.override.yml" <<YAML
services:
  caddy:
    image: ${CADDY_IMAGE}
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 128m
    cap_add:
      - NET_BIND_SERVICE
    volumes:
      - ./caddy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    depends_on: [grafana]

volumes:
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
YAML
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

docker run --rm -v "$DIR/caddy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro" "$CADDY_IMAGE" \
  caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile

cd "$DIR"
docker compose pull -q caddy
docker compose up -d

ok=0
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
  if curl -fsS --max-time 5 "https://${DOMAIN}/api/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=1; break; fi
  sleep 3
done
if [[ "$ok" != "1" ]]; then
  docker compose logs caddy --tail 40
  die "https://${DOMAIN} not reachable, check firewall ports 80/443 and DNS"
fi

echo | openssl s_client -connect "${DOMAIN}:443" -servername "$DOMAIN" 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -dates
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "http redirect: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" "http://${DOMAIN}/"
exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk '/:(3000|9090|9100|9252) / && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || die "an internal port is exposed"
log "OK: https://${DOMAIN}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/grafana-domain.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/caddy"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/caddy/Caddyfile.tmpl" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
{
	email __ACME_EMAIL__
	admin off
}

__DOMAIN__ {
	encode zstd gzip

	header {
		Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000"
		X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
		X-Frame-Options "DENY"
		Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
		-Server
	}

	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000

	log {
		output stdout
		format console
	}
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/monitoring/caddy/Caddyfile.tmpl"

echo "files written to $R: 3"
INSTALL
sudo DOMAIN=grafana.example.com ACME_EMAIL=you@example.com bash /root/server-init-config/runner/install/grafana-domain.sh
````

<a id="selinux"></a>
## SELinux enforcing

Switches SELinux to enforcing now and after reboot, then restarts and checks Docker and the runner. Refuses to run while CI jobs are running.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")

  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/selinux-enforcing.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Switch SELinux to enforcing now and after reboot (Rocky/RHEL). Rollback: setenforce 0.
# Restarts Docker and the runner: refuses to run while CI jobs are running.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  enables SELinux enforcing mode and verifies Docker and the runner still work"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
command -v getenforce >/dev/null || die "SELinux tools not present on this system"
require_runner_idle
systemctl is-active --quiet auditd || log "WARN: auditd not active, denials will not be logged"

setenforce 1
sed -i -E 's/^SELINUX=.*/SELINUX=enforcing/' /etc/selinux/config

getenforce
grep -E '^SELINUX=' /etc/selinux/config
hello=$(docker run --rm hello-world)
grep -m1 Hello <<<"$hello"
systemctl restart docker
systemctl restart gitlab-runner || true
systemctl is-active docker gitlab-runner || true
denials=$(ausearch --input-logs -m avc -ts recent </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'avc:' || true)
log "recent SELinux denials: ${denials:-0}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/selinux-enforcing.sh"

echo "files written to $R: 2"
bash "$R/runner/install/selinux-enforcing.sh" </dev/null
INSTALL
````

<a id="lock-root"></a>
## Lock root SSH

Only after this works from your laptop: `ssh ops@SERVER_IP 'sudo -n true && echo ok'`. Sets `PermitRootLogin no`. Refuses to run while the admin has no SSH key. Undo, from a session that is still open: `sudo bash /root/server-init-config/runner/install/users.sh --unlock-root`.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/users.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Users and SSH access for the runner host. Self-contained (no lib.sh) so cloud-init can embed it.
#
#   admin          ops (ADMIN_USER): SSH by key, sudo without password, not in the docker group
#   gitlab-runner  service account: no shell, no password, no SSH; the runner service runs as this user
#                  with access to Docker through the docker group (root-equivalent, needed by the executor)
#   monitoring     service account: no shell, no password, no SSH; owns the monitoring and logging containers
#
# SSH: keys only, only members of ssh-users, port SSH_PORT (default 22; remembered from the existing drop-in), no agent or X11 forwarding,
# local port forwarding kept for tunnels.
# Root keeps SSH by key until --lock-root, which refuses to run while the admin has no key. With another
# SSH_PORT, sshd listens on 22 and SSH_PORT until --lock-root, which then closes 22. A locked server stays
# locked on rerun unless --unlock-root is given. Safe to rerun.
set -Eeuo pipefail

ADMIN_USER="${ADMIN_USER:-ops}"
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"
RUNNER_USER=gitlab-runner
SSH_GROUP="${SSH_GROUP:-ssh-users}"
DROPIN=/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-ci-hardening.conf
# SSH_PORT from the environment wins; otherwise the port written by the previous run is kept, so a rerun,
# --lock-root and --unlock-root never fall back to 22 on a host that listens elsewhere.
if [[ -z "${SSH_PORT:-}" ]]; then
  SSH_PORT=$(awk 'tolower($1) == "port" && $2 != 22 { p = $2 } END { print p }' "$DROPIN" 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
SSH_PORT="${SSH_PORT:-22}"
RUNNER_DROPIN=/etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf
RUNNER_CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
LOCK_ROOT=0
UNLOCK_ROOT=0
RELOAD=1

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 [--lock-root | --unlock-root] [--no-reload]

Creates the admin user (ADMIN_USER, default ops), the service
accounts (${MON_USER}, ${RUNNER_USER} if installed), the ${SSH_GROUP} group and the SSH drop-in ${DROPIN}.
The admin gets the keys from /root/.ssh/authorized_keys.

  --lock-root    close root SSH (and port 22 when SSH_PORT is another port). Run it only after
                 "ssh ADMIN@server sudo -n true" works from your laptop.
  --unlock-root  undo --lock-root (root by key again)
  --no-reload    write the config but do not reload sshd or restart gitlab-runner

Env: ADMIN_USER, MON_USER (default monitoring), SSH_GROUP (default ssh-users),
     SSH_PORT (default 22, or the port already in ${DROPIN}; give it once, reruns keep it)
Rollback: delete ${DROPIN} and ${RUNNER_DROPIN}, then: systemctl reload sshd; systemctl daemon-reload; systemctl restart gitlab-runner
USAGE
}

while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    --lock-root) LOCK_ROOT=1 ;;
    --unlock-root) UNLOCK_ROOT=1 ;;
    --no-reload) RELOAD=0 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) usage >&2; die "unknown option: $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done

[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root (sudo $0)"
# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts; this script is self-contained, so it installs it itself.
if ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then { dnf -y -q install diffutils || apt-get install -y -q diffutils; } >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "cmp missing and diffutils not installable"; fi
(( LOCK_ROOT && UNLOCK_ROOT )) && die "--lock-root and --unlock-root exclude each other"
if ! [[ "$SSH_PORT" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( SSH_PORT < 1 || SSH_PORT > 65535 )); then die "invalid SSH_PORT: ${SSH_PORT}"; fi
[[ "$ADMIN_USER" =~ ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$ ]] || die "invalid ADMIN_USER: '${ADMIN_USER}'"
[[ "$ADMIN_USER" != root && "$ADMIN_USER" != "$MON_USER" && "$ADMIN_USER" != "$RUNNER_USER" ]] || die "ADMIN_USER must be a separate user"

NOLOGIN=$(command -v nologin || true)
[[ -n "$NOLOGIN" ]] || NOLOGIN=/sbin/nologin
if getent group wheel >/dev/null; then
  SUDO_GROUP=wheel
elif getent group sudo >/dev/null; then
  SUDO_GROUP=sudo
else
  die "neither wheel nor sudo group exists"
fi
command -v visudo >/dev/null || die "sudo is not installed"

# --- admin -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
getent group "$SSH_GROUP" >/dev/null || groupadd -r "$SSH_GROUP"
if id "$ADMIN_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  usermod -aG "${SUDO_GROUP},${SSH_GROUP}" "$ADMIN_USER"
else
  useradd -m -s /bin/bash -G "${SUDO_GROUP},${SSH_GROUP}" -c "server admin" "$ADMIN_USER"
  log "created admin user ${ADMIN_USER}"
fi
# "!" (locked) can block key logins when sshd runs without PAM; "*" means no password, key login allowed.
if [[ "$(getent shadow "$ADMIN_USER" | cut -d: -f2)" == !* ]]; then
  usermod -p '*' "$ADMIN_USER"
fi
if id -nG "$ADMIN_USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx docker; then
  gpasswd -d "$ADMIN_USER" docker >/dev/null
  log "removed ${ADMIN_USER} from the docker group (root-equivalent); use sudo docker"
fi

sudoers="/etc/sudoers.d/90-${ADMIN_USER}"
tmp=$(mktemp)
# secure_path: the Rocky default can leave out /usr/local/bin, where health and the cleanup scripts live.
printf '%s ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL\nDefaults:%s secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' \
  "$ADMIN_USER" "$ADMIN_USER" > "$tmp"
visudo -cqf "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; die "generated sudoers file is invalid"; }
install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$sudoers"
rm -f "$tmp"

home=$(getent passwd "$ADMIN_USER" | cut -d: -f6)
group=$(id -gn "$ADMIN_USER")
ak="${home}/.ssh/authorized_keys"
install -d -m 0700 -o "$ADMIN_USER" -g "$group" "${home}/.ssh"
touch "$ak"
if [[ -f /root/.ssh/authorized_keys ]]; then
  # Plain key lines only: lines with options (for example cloud-init's "Please login as" command=) are skipped.
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    grep -qxF -- "$line" "$ak" || printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ak"
  done < <(grep -E '^(ssh-(ed25519|rsa)|ecdsa-sha2-|sk-)' /root/.ssh/authorized_keys || true)
fi
chown "$ADMIN_USER:$group" "$ak"
chmod 0600 "$ak"
if [[ -f /root/.tmux.conf && ! -f "${home}/.tmux.conf" ]]; then
  install -m 0644 -o "$ADMIN_USER" -g "$group" /root/.tmux.conf "${home}/.tmux.conf"
fi
if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon -R "${home}/.ssh" || true; fi
keys=$(grep -cE '^(ssh-|ecdsa-|sk-)' "$ak" || true)
log "admin ${ADMIN_USER}: groups $(id -nG "$ADMIN_USER" | tr ' ' ','), ${keys:-0} SSH key(s), sudo without password"

# --- service accounts --------------------------------------------------------------------------
if ! id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  useradd -r -U -M -d /nonexistent -s "$NOLOGIN" -c "monitoring and logging containers" "$MON_USER"
  log "created service user ${MON_USER}"
fi
usermod -s "$NOLOGIN" "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
log "service ${MON_USER}: uid $(id -u "$MON_USER"), gid $(id -g "$MON_USER"), shell ${NOLOGIN}"

if id "$RUNNER_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  usermod -s "$NOLOGIN" "$RUNNER_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  usermod -L "$RUNNER_USER" 2>/dev/null || true
  getent group docker >/dev/null && usermod -aG docker "$RUNNER_USER"
  install -d -m 0755 "$(dirname "$RUNNER_DROPIN")"
  cat > "${RUNNER_DROPIN}.new" <<'EOF'
# Run the runner service as its own user instead of root. Docker access comes from the docker group.
[Service]
User=gitlab-runner
Group=gitlab-runner
SupplementaryGroups=docker
ExecStart=
ExecStart=/usr/bin/gitlab-runner run --working-directory /home/gitlab-runner --config /etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml --service gitlab-runner
EOF
  changed=0
  if ! cmp -s "${RUNNER_DROPIN}.new" "$RUNNER_DROPIN" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv "${RUNNER_DROPIN}.new" "$RUNNER_DROPIN"
    chmod 0644 "$RUNNER_DROPIN"
    changed=1
  else
    rm -f "${RUNNER_DROPIN}.new"
  fi
  # The service reads and rewrites config.toml (token, system id), so it owns /etc/gitlab-runner and its home.
  install -d -m 0700 -o "$RUNNER_USER" -g "$RUNNER_USER" /etc/gitlab-runner
  chown -R "$RUNNER_USER:$RUNNER_USER" /etc/gitlab-runner
  if [[ -f "$RUNNER_CFG" ]]; then chmod 0600 "$RUNNER_CFG"; fi
  install -d -m 0750 -o "$RUNNER_USER" -g "$RUNNER_USER" "/home/${RUNNER_USER}"
  chown -R "$RUNNER_USER:$RUNNER_USER" "/home/${RUNNER_USER}"
  if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon -R /etc/gitlab-runner "$(dirname "$RUNNER_DROPIN")" || true; fi
  if (( RELOAD )); then
    systemctl daemon-reload
    restart=0
    if (( changed )) || [[ "$(ps -o user= -p "$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value gitlab-runner)" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')" != "$RUNNER_USER" ]]; then
      restart=1
    fi
    if (( restart )); then
      main_pid=$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value gitlab-runner)
      if [[ "${main_pid:-0}" == 0 ]]; then
        # Stopped service: nothing to interrupt, and the idle gate would only block the start.
        systemctl start gitlab-runner
        sleep 3
      elif ! job_ids=$(docker ps -q --filter "label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true" 2>/dev/null); then
        # A docker failure is not "0 jobs": restarting could kill running CI jobs.
        log "WARN: cannot confirm that no CI job is running (docker does not answer), gitlab-runner not restarted; check with: docker ps --filter label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true, then: systemctl restart gitlab-runner"
      elif [[ -n "$job_ids" ]]; then
        log "WARN: $(wc -w <<<"$job_ids") CI job(s) running, gitlab-runner not restarted; run: systemctl restart gitlab-runner"
      else
        systemctl restart gitlab-runner
        sleep 3
      fi
    fi
    pid=$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value gitlab-runner)
    if [[ "${pid:-0}" != 0 ]]; then
      log "service ${RUNNER_USER}: runner process runs as $(ps -o user= -p "$pid" | tr -d ' ') (groups: $(ps -o supgrp= -p "$pid" | tr -d ' '))"
    else
      log "WARN: gitlab-runner is not running: journalctl -u gitlab-runner -n 30"
    fi
  fi
else
  log "${RUNNER_USER} not installed yet, rerun this script after installing GitLab Runner"
fi

# --- SSH ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A server that is already locked stays locked, so a rerun never reopens root or port 22 by accident.
if (( ! LOCK_ROOT && ! UNLOCK_ROOT )) && grep -qsx 'PermitRootLogin no' "$DROPIN"; then
  LOCK_ROOT=1
  log "keeping the existing root lock (use --unlock-root to undo it)"
fi
if (( LOCK_ROOT )) && (( ${keys:-0} == 0 )); then
  die "--lock-root refused: ${ADMIN_USER} has no SSH key, root would be the only way in"
fi
if (( LOCK_ROOT )); then
  root_login=no
  allow="AllowGroups ${SSH_GROUP}"
  ports="Port ${SSH_PORT}"
else
  root_login=prohibit-password
  allow="AllowGroups ${SSH_GROUP} root"
  ports="Port 22"
  if [[ "$SSH_PORT" != 22 ]]; then ports+=$'\n'"Port ${SSH_PORT}"; fi
fi

# SELinux only lets sshd bind ports labeled ssh_port_t; firewalld (if active) must allow the port too.
if [[ "$SSH_PORT" != 22 ]] && command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; then
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "semanage missing: install policycoreutils-python-utils"
  if ! semanage port -l | awk '$1 == "ssh_port_t" { for (i = 3; i <= NF; i++) print $i }' | tr -d ',' | grep -qx "$SSH_PORT"; then
    semanage port -a -t ssh_port_t -p tcp "$SSH_PORT" 2>/dev/null || semanage port -m -t ssh_port_t -p tcp "$SSH_PORT"
    log "SELinux: port ${SSH_PORT} labeled ssh_port_t"
  fi
fi
if systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld 2>/dev/null; then
  if [[ "$SSH_PORT" == 22 ]] && firewall-cmd -q --permanent --zone=public --query-service=ssh; then
    log "firewalld: port 22 is covered by the ssh service"   # no extra 22/tcp rule: it would differ from the first run
  else
    firewall-cmd -q --permanent --add-port="${SSH_PORT}/tcp" && firewall-cmd -q --reload
    log "firewalld: port ${SSH_PORT}/tcp allowed"
  fi
fi
# Debian runner hosts get ufw from host-firewall.sh: the new port must be open there too, or sshd listens on a port the
# firewall drops (and --lock-root, which closes port 22, would then lock you out).
if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 && ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active'; then
  ufw allow "${SSH_PORT}/tcp" >/dev/null || die "cannot allow ${SSH_PORT}/tcp in ufw"
  log "ufw: port ${SSH_PORT}/tcp allowed"
fi
# Add this port to the fail2ban sshd jail written by host-firewall.sh.
JAIL_FILE="${JAIL_FILE:-/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/50-sshd.local}"
if [[ -f "$JAIL_FILE" ]] && grep -q '^port ' "$JAIL_FILE" && ! grep -E '^port ' "$JAIL_FILE" | tr -c '0-9\n' ' ' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx "$SSH_PORT"; then
  sed -i -E "s/^(port[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*.*)\$/\1,${SSH_PORT}/" "$JAIL_FILE"
  systemctl reload fail2ban >/dev/null 2>&1 || systemctl restart fail2ban >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  log "fail2ban: sshd jail now also watches port ${SSH_PORT}"
fi
# Never write a config that leaves SSH only on a port the running host firewall drops.
if [[ "$SSH_PORT" != 22 ]]; then
  if systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld 2>/dev/null && ! firewall-cmd --query-port="${SSH_PORT}/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    die "firewalld does not allow ${SSH_PORT}/tcp in the running rules; sshd config left unchanged"
  fi
  if command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 && ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active' \
     && ! ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -qE "^${SSH_PORT}/tcp([[:space:]]+\(v6\))?[[:space:]]+(ALLOW|LIMIT)"; then
    die "ufw does not allow ${SSH_PORT}/tcp in the running rules; sshd config left unchanged"
  fi
fi
[[ -d /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d ]] || die "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d missing (OpenSSH too old for drop-ins?)"
grep -qiE '^\s*Include\s+/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config || die "/etc/ssh/sshd_config does not include sshd_config.d"

new="${DROPIN}.new"
cat > "$new" <<EOF
# Managed by runner/install/users.sh. First match wins in sshd, so this file is named 00- to load first.
${ports}
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
PermitRootLogin ${root_login}
${allow}
MaxAuthTries 3
LoginGraceTime 30
ClientAliveInterval 300
ClientAliveCountMax 2
X11Forwarding no
AllowAgentForwarding no
AllowTcpForwarding local
PermitTunnel no
EOF
chmod 0600 "$new"
old_backup=""
if [[ -f "$DROPIN" ]] && cmp -s "$new" "$DROPIN"; then
  rm -f "$new"   # same content: no backup, no rewrite, a rerun leaves the managed state untouched
else
  if [[ -f "$DROPIN" ]]; then
    old_backup="${DROPIN}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
    cp -a "$DROPIN" "$old_backup"
  fi
  mv "$new" "$DROPIN"
fi
legacy=/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-ci-hardening.conf
[[ -f "$legacy" ]] && mv "$legacy" "${legacy}.disabled"
if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/* 2>/dev/null || true; fi

sshd_bin=$(command -v sshd || echo /usr/sbin/sshd)
if ! "$sshd_bin" -t; then
  if [[ -n "$old_backup" ]]; then mv "$old_backup" "$DROPIN"; else rm -f "$DROPIN"; fi
  [[ -f "${legacy}.disabled" ]] && mv "${legacy}.disabled" "$legacy"
  die "sshd rejected the new config, previous config restored"
fi
if (( RELOAD )); then
  if systemctl is-enabled --quiet ssh.socket 2>/dev/null; then
    # Socket activation (Ubuntu, some Debian setups): the socket generator reads Port from sshd_config.
    systemctl daemon-reload
    systemctl restart ssh.socket
  elif systemctl cat sshd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    systemctl reload sshd
  else
    systemctl reload ssh
  fi
fi
effective=$("$sshd_bin" -T 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei '^(port|permitrootlogin|passwordauthentication|allowgroups|allowtcpforwarding) ' | tr '\n' ';' || true)
log "sshd: ${effective}"

port_opt=""
if [[ "$SSH_PORT" != 22 ]]; then port_opt="-p ${SSH_PORT} "; fi
if (( LOCK_ROOT )); then
  log "OK: root SSH closed. Log in as: ssh ${port_opt}${ADMIN_USER}@<server>"
else
  if [[ -n "$port_opt" ]]; then log "OK: allow TCP ${SSH_PORT} in the Hetzner Firewall first"; fi
  log "OK: test from your laptop:  ssh ${port_opt}${ADMIN_USER}@<server> 'sudo -n true && echo sudo works'"
  log "    then lock root:         sudo $0 --lock-root"
fi
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/users.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/lock-root.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Disable SSH for root. Run only after "ssh ADMIN@server sudo -n true" works. See runner/install/users.sh --help.
# Extra options go to users.sh; --unlock-root and --help replace the default --lock-root.
set -Eeuo pipefail
mode=(--lock-root)
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --unlock-root|-h|--help) mode=() ;;
  esac
done
exec bash "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/users.sh" "${mode[@]}" "$@"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/lock-root.sh"

echo "files written to $R: 3"
bash "$R/runner/install/lock-root.sh" </dev/null
INSTALL
````

<a id="update"></a>
## Update everything installed

Writes the current repo files and runs `update.sh`: syncs what is installed, backs up and restores on failure. Add `--dry-run` to the last line to preview, `--os` to upgrade packages too.

````bash
sudo bash <<'INSTALL'
set -Eeuo pipefail
R=/root/server-init-config

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/lib.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the installers (runner/install, server and common). Sourced, not executed.
# shellcheck shell=bash

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
export REPO_ROOT

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

require_root() { [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"; }

selinux_on() { command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled; }

pkg_install() {
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y -q install "$@"
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q && apt-get install -y -q "$@"
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
}

# cmp (diffutils) is missing on minimal hosts but the installers compare files with it; fetch it when run as root.
if [[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] && ! command -v cmp >/dev/null 2>&1; then pkg_install diffutils >/dev/null || log "WARN: diffutils not installed, cmp is missing"; fi

# Label a directory so containers may read files in it (no-op without SELinux).
selinux_label_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  install -d -m 0755 "$dir"
  selinux_on || return 0
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  # Read the whole list first: grep -q exits at the first match and would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail.
  if ! grep -q "^${dir}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)"; then
    semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${dir}(/.*)?"
  fi
  restorecon -R "$dir"
}

restorecon_if() { if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$@" || true; fi; }

# RHEL-family sudo resets PATH to secure_path, which can leave out /usr/local/bin (so `sudo health` fails).
# Adds a validated drop-in unless some sudoers file already sets a secure_path that includes it.
ensure_secure_path() {
  local f=/etc/sudoers.d/50-secure-path tmp
  command -v visudo >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  if grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path[[:space:]]*=.*/usr/local/bin' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0
  fi
  if ! grep -rhsE '^[[:space:]]*Defaults[[:space:]]+secure_path' /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    return 0   # no secure_path at all (Debian family keeps it in sudoers; others use the caller PATH)
  fi
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  printf 'Defaults secure_path="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin"\n' > "$tmp"
  if visudo -cqf "$tmp"; then
    install -d -m 0750 /etc/sudoers.d
    install -m 0440 -o root -g root "$tmp" "$f"
    log "sudo secure_path now includes /usr/local/bin (${f})"
  else
    echo "WARN: generated sudoers drop-in is invalid, secure_path left as it was" >&2
  fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

# version_ge HAVE WANT: true when dotted version HAVE >= WANT (numeric, sort -V).
version_ge() { [[ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$1" "$2" | sort -V | head -n 1)" == "$2" ]]; }

# require_compose_min WANT WHAT: die before anything is changed when the Docker Compose plugin is older than WANT.
# Why: a stack that needs a newer compose would otherwise fail later at "docker compose config", mid-update.
require_compose_min() {
  local want=$1 what=$2 have
  have=$(docker compose version --short 2>/dev/null || true)
  have=${have#v}
  have=${have%%[!0-9.]*}
  [[ -n "$have" ]] || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer, but 'docker compose version' gives no answer: install the docker-compose-plugin"
  version_ge "$have" "$want" || die "${what} needs Docker Compose ${want} or newer (inline 'configs: content:'), found ${have}: update the docker-compose-plugin package (or Docker Engine) first, then rerun"
}

# Containers that count as a running CI job: GitLab Runner job/service containers and the pods of the GitHub Actions runner
# (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl labels both of its containers io.server-init.github-runner=job).
CI_JOB_LABELS=(com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true io.server-init.github-runner=job)
# Ids of those containers, one per line; fails when docker does not answer (that is not "no jobs").
ci_job_ids() { local l ids=""; for l in "${CI_JOB_LABELS[@]}"; do ids+="$(docker ps -q --filter "label=${l}")"$'\n' || return; done; sed '/^$/d' <<<"$ids" | sort -u; }
ci_jobs_running() { ci_job_ids 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }

require_runner_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  (( n == 0 )) || die "${n} CI job container(s) running, retry when the runner is idle"
}

# Timestamped copy before a change. Skipped when an identical backup already exists, so reruns of an idempotent
# installer do not pile up copies of an unchanged file.
backup() {
  local f=$1 b
  for b in "${f}".bak.*; do
    [[ -f "$b" ]] && cmp -s "$f" "$b" && return 0
  done
  cp -a "$f" "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
}

# edit_with_backup FILE CMD...  runs CMD (which edits FILE in place) and keeps a timestamped copy of the previous content,
# but only when CMD changed the file, so a rerun of an idempotent installer leaves no .bak with the same content as FILE.
edit_with_backup() {
  local f=$1 bak; shift
  # The snapshot lives next to FILE (cp -a keeps its mode), never in /tmp: it can hold a token, and a CMD that dies leaves it behind.
  # mktemp makes the name unique, so a second call on the same file in the same second cannot overwrite (and then delete) the
  # first call's backup of the original content.
  bak=$(mktemp "${f}.bak.$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).XXXXXX")
  cp -a "$f" "$bak"
  "$@"
  if cmp -s "$f" "$bak"; then rm -f "$bak"; fi
}

# Prometheus scrape jobs for the logging stack, shared by runner/install/logging.sh and runner/install/update.sh.
prom_jobs_logging() {
  cat <<'YAML'
  - job_name: loki
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:3100"]
  - job_name: alloy
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:12345"]
YAML
}

# Merge KEY=VALUE entries into the single [[runners]] environment line of config.toml.
runner_env_merge() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml existing list key e line
  [[ $(grep -c '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$cfg") -eq 1 ]] || die "expected exactly one [[runners]] block in $cfg"
  existing=$(grep -E '^  environment = \[' "$cfg" | sed -E 's/^  environment = \[(.*)\]$/\1/' || true)
  list="$existing"
  for e in "$@"; do
    key="${e%%=*}"
    if grep -q "\"${key}=" <<<"$list"; then
      list=$(sed -E "s|\"${key}=[^\"]*\"|\"${e}\"|" <<<"$list")
    else
      list="${list:+${list}, }\"${e}\""
    fi
  done
  line="  environment = [${list}]"
  if grep -qE '^  environment = \[' "$cfg"; then
    sed -i -E "s|^  environment = \[.*\]$|${line}|" "$cfg"
  else
    sed -i -E "0,/^  executor = .*/s||${line}\n&|" "$cfg"
  fi
  chmod 600 "$cfg"
  runner_cfg_owner
}

# When the runner service runs as gitlab-runner (runner/install/users.sh), it must own its config after root edits it.
runner_cfg_owner() {
  local cfg=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
  if [[ -f /etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/10-service-user.conf ]] && id gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    chown -R gitlab-runner:gitlab-runner /etc/gitlab-runner
    chmod 600 "$cfg"
  fi
}

# --- service user for the monitoring and logging stacks (created by runner/install/users.sh) ---------------
MON_USER="${MON_USER:-monitoring}"

# Set MON_UID and MON_GID, or stop if the service user is missing.
mon_ids() {
  id "$MON_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "service user ${MON_USER} missing, run runner/install/users.sh first"
  MON_UID=$(id -u "$MON_USER")
  MON_GID=$(id -g "$MON_USER")
}

# env_set FILE KEY VALUE: set KEY=VALUE in a root-only env file.
env_set() {
  local f="$1" k="$2" v="$3"
  touch "$f"
  chmod 600 "$f"
  if grep -q "^${k}=" "$f"; then
    sed -i "s|^${k}=.*|${k}=${v}|" "$f"
  else
    printf '%s=%s\n' "$k" "$v" >> "$f"
  fi
}

# stack_ids DIR [logging]: write the ids the compose file needs into DIR/.env.
stack_ids() {
  local dir="$1" docker_gid journal_gid
  mon_ids
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_UID "$MON_UID"
  env_set "${dir}/.env" MON_GID "$MON_GID"
  if [[ "${2:-}" == logging ]]; then
    docker_gid=$(getent group docker | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$docker_gid" ]] || die "docker group missing"
    env_set "${dir}/.env" DOCKER_GID "$docker_gid"
    journal_gid=$(getent group systemd-journal | cut -d: -f3)
    [[ -n "$journal_gid" ]] || die "systemd-journal group missing"
    # compose rejects equal group_add items, so the journal group is only added when it differs from docker's.
    if [[ "$journal_gid" != "$docker_gid" ]]; then
      printf 'services:\n  alloy:\n    group_add:\n      - "%s"\n' "$journal_gid" > "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    else
      rm -f "${dir}/docker-compose.override.yml"
    fi
  fi
}

# Config readable by the service user, writable by root only; .env (secrets) stays root-only.
own_stack_dir() {
  local dir="$1"
  chown -R "root:${MON_USER}" "$dir"
  chmod -R u=rwX,g=rX,o= "$dir"
  if [[ -f "${dir}/.env" ]]; then
    chown root:root "${dir}/.env"
    chmod 600 "${dir}/.env"
  fi
}

# Helper container that runs as root next to stack volumes (chown_volumes, the Grafana backup, the README restore command).
# The single pin: alpine 3.20 is end of life. Pinned by the digest of the multi-arch index (amd64 and arm64), so a moved tag cannot change
# what runs as root next to the data. Bump tag and digest here only; every copy must carry the same string (tools/ci/check-pins.sh enforces it): runner/README.md (restore command), runner/ci/smoke.yml,
# runner/ci/mirror-images.yml, tools/ci/runner-container.sh and the generated runner/COMMANDS.md.
HELPER_IMAGE="alpine:3.22@sha256:2e0b81d60597f449baa56dc25d355367869d2dca4cd57e866f1e2b52af3eb55f"

# Images of the opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh). The single pin of each, both by the digest of the multi-arch
# index (amd64 and arm64): the runner image from ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner, the rootless BuildKit sidecar from Docker Hub (moby/buildkit).
# Bump tag and digest here only; the installer and runner/install/update.sh copy them into /etc/github-runner/config.env, and
# tools/ci/check-pins.sh fails when a tracked file spells either image with another pin. GitHub stops queuing jobs to a runner older than
# 30 days (the image is the runner version), so bump GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE at least monthly; health warns after ~25 days.
# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by runner/install/github-runner.sh (sourcing this file)
GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE="ghcr.io/actions/actions-runner:2.338.2@sha256:759a1d94a15b05941aba5196974ff43fe15b4cbba29b694b35cbc32a1166b232"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE="moby/buildkit:v0.34.2-rootless@sha256:c8252268760e1baba80780d63d738ef9f260fb7c7c0973c78494cb9ddd99eda1"

# Create the stack's containers and volumes without starting them, then hand the volumes to the service user.
chown_volumes() {
  local dir="$1" project v
  mon_ids
  project=$(cd "$dir" && docker compose config --format json | jq -r .name)
  (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start --quiet-pull >/dev/null 2>&1) || (cd "$dir" && docker compose up --no-start >/dev/null)
  for v in $(docker volume ls -q --filter "label=com.docker.compose.project=${project}"); do
    # root in the helper only needs to chown and to enter other users' 0700 trees: no network, read-only rootfs, two capabilities, no setuid escalation, symlinks are not followed (-h)
    docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add CHOWN --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH \
      --security-opt no-new-privileges \
      -v "${v}:/v" "$HELPER_IMAGE" chown -Rh "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" /v
  done
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/lib.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/github-runner.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Opt-in ephemeral GitHub Actions runner for the PRIVATE repositories of one GitHub App installation (a personal account), on this host
# next to the GitLab Runner. Installs the controller (runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl) and its systemd unit, the service user
# github-runner, /etc/github-runner/config.env (no secrets) and the GitHub App private key /etc/github-runner/app.pem (mode 0600,
# owner github-runner), pulls the pinned images (common/lib.sh), runs a self-test against GitHub and only then enables the service.
# Each job gets a just-in-time runner in its own pod (network, rootless BuildKit sidecar, runner container); no Docker socket in jobs.
# Needs: Docker, runner/install/job-limits.sh (ci-jobs.slice), a GitHub App (see runner/README.md). Safe to rerun: values already in
# config.env are kept unless you pass them in the environment, a changed file gets a backup.
#
# Asks (read -rp) for what is missing: GH_OWNER (GitHub user), GH_APP_CLIENT_ID (the App's client ID) and the path of the downloaded
# private key (.pem; copied, never printed; delete the download afterwards). Without a terminal pass them in the environment: GH_OWNER,
# GH_APP_CLIENT_ID, GH_KEY_SRC.
# Env (all optional, kept from config.env on a rerun): GH_INSTALLATION_ID (found by itself), GH_LABELS (default
# self-hosted,linux,<arm64|x64>,hetzner), GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID (1), GH_MAX_JOBS (1), GH_POLL_INTERVAL (30), GH_IDLE_TIMEOUT (300),
# GH_EXCLUDE_REPOS, GH_BUILDKIT (1), GH_JOB_CPUS / GH_JOB_MEMORY (the GitLab per-job values from config.toml, else 1.5 / 1536m),
# GH_BUILDKIT_CPUS (1), GH_BUILDKIT_MEMORY (768m), GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL (10.213.0.0/20), GH_MAX_RUNTIME. See runner/README.md.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../common/lib.sh"

ETC=/etc/github-runner
CFG="${ETC}/config.env"
KEY="${ETC}/app.pem"
KEY_RESTART="${ETC}/key-restart-required"
SVC_USER=github-runner
UNIT=github-runner-ctl.service
CTL=/usr/local/bin/github-runner-ctl
SLICE=/etc/systemd/system/ci-jobs.slice
USERNS_DROPIN=/etc/sysctl.d/91-github-runner-userns.conf
GITLAB_CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
DO_PULL=1 DO_SELFTEST=1 DO_START=1 ONLY_SELFTEST=0

usage() {
  sed -n '2,/^set -E/{/^set -E/!p}' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  cat <<USAGE

Usage: $0 [--self-test] [--no-self-test] [--no-start] [--no-pull]
  --self-test     only run the self-test with the installed config: mint a JWT, get an installation token, list the repositories and
                  print which would be served (names and visibility); starts and changes nothing
  --no-self-test  install and enable without the live check against GitHub (offline)
  --no-start      enable the service but do not start it
  --no-pull       do not pull the images now (the controller pulls a missing image before its first job)
Removal: see runner/docs/github-runner.md (Remove it). Stop the controller, review and remove only containers and networks labelled
  io.server-init.github-runner=job; never prune unrelated networks. Running pods survive a controller stop.
USAGE
}

while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --self-test) ONLY_SELFTEST=1 ;;
    --no-self-test) DO_SELFTEST=0 ;;
    --no-start) DO_START=0 ;;
    --no-pull) DO_PULL=0 ;;
    *) usage >&2; die "unknown option: $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done
require_root

run_selftest() {
  runuser -u "$SVC_USER" -- env GHR_CONFIG="$CFG" "$CTL" self-test
}

if (( ONLY_SELFTEST )); then
  [[ -x "$CTL" && -f "$CFG" ]] || die "not installed yet: run $0 first"
  run_selftest
  exit $?
fi

# ---- preflight ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker is not installed"
systemctl is-active --quiet docker || die "docker is not running"
systemctl cat ci-job-isolation.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ci-job-isolation.service missing: install the runner host tools first"
getent group docker >/dev/null || die "no docker group"
[[ -f "$SLICE" ]] || die "${SLICE} missing: run runner/setup.sh --job-limits first (the pods run inside ci-jobs.slice, which caps all CI jobs together)"
read -r cgdrv cgver < <(docker info --format '{{.CgroupDriver}} {{.CgroupVersion}}' 2>/dev/null || echo "? ?")
[[ "$cgdrv" == systemd && "$cgver" == 2 ]] || die "Docker must use cgroup v2 with the systemd cgroup driver (found: ${cgdrv} v${cgver}); --cgroup-parent ci-jobs.slice needs it"
for t in curl jq openssl; do command -v "$t" >/dev/null || pkg_install "$t"; done
command -v runuser >/dev/null || die "runuser (util-linux) is missing"
[[ -f "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl" && -f "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/systemd/${UNIT}" ]] || die "incomplete copy of the repository"

existing() { # existing KEY: the value in config.env, quotes removed
  [[ -f "$CFG" ]] || return 0
  { grep -m1 "^$1=" "$CFG" || true; } | cut -d= -f2- | sed -E 's/^"(.*)"$/\1/'
}
# pick KEY DEFAULT: environment, else config.env, else DEFAULT
pick() {
  local v=${!1:-}
  [[ -n "$v" ]] || v=$(existing "$1")
  printf '%s' "${v:-$2}"
}

# Rootless BuildKit needs user namespaces for non-root (kernel: user.max_user_namespaces > 0). Only written when it is 0.
buildkit_wanted=$(pick GH_BUILDKIT 1)
if [[ "$buildkit_wanted" == 1 ]]; then
  maxns=$(sysctl -n user.max_user_namespaces 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [[ "$maxns" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( maxns == 0 )); then
    printf '# Written by runner/install/github-runner.sh: rootless BuildKit needs user namespaces.\nuser.max_user_namespaces = 28633\n' > "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new"
    if ! cmp -s "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new" "$USERNS_DROPIN" 2>/dev/null; then mv "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new" "$USERNS_DROPIN"; else rm -f "${USERNS_DROPIN}.new"; fi
    sysctl -q -w user.max_user_namespaces=28633 || log "WARN: could not set user.max_user_namespaces now; it applies after a reboot"
    log "user.max_user_namespaces was 0: set to 28633 (${USERNS_DROPIN}); rootless BuildKit needs it"
  else
    log "user.max_user_namespaces = ${maxns}: ok for rootless BuildKit"
  fi
  if [[ "$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" == 1 ]]; then
    log "WARN: kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 (Ubuntu): rootless BuildKit will fail; set it to 0 in /etc/sysctl.d or use GH_BUILDKIT=0"
  fi
fi

# ---- service user ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOLOGIN=$(command -v nologin || echo /sbin/nologin)
if ! id "$SVC_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  useradd -r -U -M -d /nonexistent -s "$NOLOGIN" -c "GitHub Actions runner controller" "$SVC_USER"
  log "created service user ${SVC_USER}"
fi
usermod -s "$NOLOGIN" "$SVC_USER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
usermod -L "$SVC_USER" 2>/dev/null || true
usermod -aG docker "$SVC_USER"   # root-equivalent: it is what the controller needs to start the pods
install -d -m 0750 -o root -g "$SVC_USER" "$ETC"

# ---- the key ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
changed=0
src=${GH_KEY_SRC:-}
if [[ -z "$src" && ! -f "$KEY" ]]; then
  [[ -t 0 ]] || die "no private key yet: pass its path in GH_KEY_SRC (the .pem downloaded from the GitHub App page)"
  read -rp "Path of the downloaded GitHub App private key (.pem): " src
fi
if [[ -n "$src" ]]; then
  [[ -f "$src" && -r "$src" ]] || die "cannot read ${src}"
  openssl rsa -in "$src" -passin pass: -noout >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "${src} is not an RSA private key (download it from the GitHub App page, Generate a private key)"
  if ! cmp -s "$src" "$KEY" 2>/dev/null; then
    [[ ! -f "$KEY" ]] || backup "$KEY"
````
