    install -m 0600 -o "$SVC_USER" -g "$SVC_USER" "$src" "$KEY"
    ( umask 077; : > "$KEY_RESTART" )
    changed=1   # clear cached credentials after a successful self-test, even when config and code are unchanged
    log "private key installed: ${KEY} (mode 0600, owner ${SVC_USER})"
  fi
  if [[ "$(realpath "$src")" != "$(realpath "$KEY")" ]]; then
    log "REMINDER: the downloaded copy ${src} is still on disk: delete it once the self-test passes (shred -u '${src}')"
  fi
fi
[[ -f "$KEY" ]] || die "no ${KEY}"
openssl rsa -in "$KEY" -passin pass: -noout >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "${KEY} is not an RSA private key"
chown "${SVC_USER}:${SVC_USER}" "$KEY"; chmod 0600 "$KEY"
[[ ! -f "$KEY_RESTART" ]] || changed=1   # retry a rotation whose self-test or activation previously failed

# ---- config ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
GH_OWNER=$(pick GH_OWNER "")
if [[ -z "$GH_OWNER" ]]; then
  [[ -t 0 ]] || die "GH_OWNER is not set: pass the GitHub user name in the environment"
  read -rp "GitHub user (owner of the private repositories): " GH_OWNER
fi
GH_APP_CLIENT_ID=$(pick GH_APP_CLIENT_ID "")
if [[ -z "$GH_APP_CLIENT_ID" ]]; then
  [[ -t 0 ]] || die "GH_APP_CLIENT_ID is not set: pass the App's client ID in the environment"
  read -rp "Client ID of the GitHub App (Iv...): " GH_APP_CLIENT_ID
fi
case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) arch=arm64 ;; *) arch=x64 ;; esac
# the per-job limits of the GitLab jobs (same numbers): from config.toml when job-limits.sh wrote them
gl() { [[ -f "$GITLAB_CFG" ]] && sed -nE "s/^[[:space:]]+$1 = \"([^\"]+)\".*/\1/p" "$GITLAB_CFG" | head -n1 || true; }
job_mem_default=$(gl memory); job_cpu_default=$(gl cpus)

# only plain characters: the value goes through sed (env_set) and into a file the controller parses
set_cfg() {
  [[ "$2" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.,@:/+-]*$ ]] || die "$1: unexpected characters in '$2'"
  [[ -n "${CFG_DRY:-}" ]] || env_set "${CFG_TARGET:-$CFG}" "$1" "$2"
}
write_config() {
  set_cfg GH_OWNER "$GH_OWNER"
  set_cfg GH_APP_CLIENT_ID "$GH_APP_CLIENT_ID"
  set_cfg GH_INSTALLATION_ID "$(pick GH_INSTALLATION_ID "")"
  set_cfg GH_LABELS "$(pick GH_LABELS "self-hosted,linux,${arch},hetzner")"
  set_cfg GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID "$(pick GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID 1)"
  set_cfg GH_MAX_JOBS "$(pick GH_MAX_JOBS 1)"
  set_cfg GH_POLL_INTERVAL "$(pick GH_POLL_INTERVAL 30)"
  set_cfg GH_IDLE_TIMEOUT "$(pick GH_IDLE_TIMEOUT 300)"
  set_cfg GH_MAX_RUNTIME "$(pick GH_MAX_RUNTIME 21900)"
  set_cfg GH_EXCLUDE_REPOS "$(pick GH_EXCLUDE_REPOS "")"
  set_cfg GH_BUILDKIT "$buildkit_wanted"
  set_cfg GH_JOB_CPUS "$(pick GH_JOB_CPUS "${job_cpu_default:-1.5}")"
  set_cfg GH_JOB_MEMORY "$(pick GH_JOB_MEMORY "${job_mem_default:-1536m}")"
  set_cfg GH_BUILDKIT_CPUS "$(pick GH_BUILDKIT_CPUS 1)"
  set_cfg GH_BUILDKIT_MEMORY "$(pick GH_BUILDKIT_MEMORY 768m)"
  set_cfg GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL "$(pick GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL 10.213.0.0/20)"
  set_cfg GH_KEY_FILE "$KEY"
  # the images are pinned in common/lib.sh and follow the repository (a bump reaches the host with this script or update.sh)
  set_cfg GH_RUNNER_IMAGE "$GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE"
  set_cfg GH_BUILDKIT_IMAGE "$GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE"
}
CFG_DRY=1 write_config   # checks every value first: a bad one must not leave a half-written file
cfg_candidate=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f -- "$cfg_candidate"' EXIT
if [[ -f "$CFG" ]]; then cp "$CFG" "$cfg_candidate"; fi
CFG_TARGET="$cfg_candidate" write_config
GHR_CONFIG="$cfg_candidate" bash "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl" check-config \
  || die "candidate config is invalid; installed config was not changed"
apply_config() { cat "$cfg_candidate" > "$CFG"; }
if [[ ! -f "$CFG" ]]; then
  printf '# Written by runner/install/github-runner.sh. No secrets here: the private key is %s.\n# Documentation: runner/README.md (GitHub Actions runner).\n' "$KEY" > "$CFG"
  write_config   # a new file: nothing to back up
else
  cfg_before=$(sha256sum < "$CFG")
  edit_with_backup "$CFG" apply_config
  [[ "$cfg_before" == "$(sha256sum < "$CFG")" ]] || changed=1   # restart below so the controller reads the new values
fi
chown "root:${SVC_USER}" "$CFG"; chmod 0640 "$CFG"

# ---- files, unit, images -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
install_if_changed() { # SRC DST MODE
  if ! cmp -s "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || [[ "$(stat -c %a "$2")" != "$(printf '%o' "$((8#$3))")" ]]; then
    [[ ! -f "$2" ]] || backup "$2"
    install -m "$3" "$1" "$2"; restorecon_if "$2"; changed=1; log "installed ${2}"
  fi
}
bash -n "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl" || die "syntax error in the controller"
install_if_changed "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl" "$CTL" 0755
install_if_changed "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/systemd/${UNIT}" "/etc/systemd/system/${UNIT}" 0644
GHR_CONFIG="$CFG" "$CTL" check-config || die "config.env is invalid (see above); fix it and rerun"
systemctl daemon-reload
# ci-job-isolation reads GH_JOB_SUBNET_POOL: it lets the pod networks, and only them, reach the npm cache (docker0 IP, port 4873)
systemctl reload-or-restart ci-job-isolation.service || die "ci-job-isolation failed: inspect journalctl -u ci-job-isolation.service before enabling the runner"

if (( DO_PULL )); then
  log "pulling the pinned images (the runner image is large)"
  docker pull -q "$GHR_RUNNER_IMAGE" >/dev/null
  if [[ "$(existing GH_BUILDKIT)" == 1 ]]; then docker pull -q "$GHR_BUILDKIT_IMAGE" >/dev/null; fi
fi

# ---- self-test, then enable --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
if (( DO_SELFTEST )); then
  log "self-test against GitHub (starts nothing)"
  if ! run_selftest; then
    log "self-test FAILED: service activation is unchanged (an existing service may still be running). Fix the App, then rerun ${0} to self-test and apply activation/restart."
    exit 1
  fi
fi
systemctl enable "$UNIT" >/dev/null 2>&1
if (( DO_START )); then
  if systemctl is-active --quiet "$UNIT"; then
    if (( changed )); then systemctl restart "$UNIT"; log "${UNIT} restarted (running pods keep running)"; fi
  else
    systemctl start "$UNIT"
  fi
  sleep 3
  systemctl is-active --quiet "$UNIT" || { journalctl -u github-runner-ctl -n 20 --no-pager || true; die "${UNIT} is not running"; }
  rm -f -- "$KEY_RESTART"
  log "OK: ${UNIT} running. Use it with runs-on: [self-hosted, hetzner] in a private repository; logs: journalctl -u github-runner-ctl -f; health shows the status"
else
  log "OK: ${UNIT} enabled, not started (--no-start): systemctl start github-runner-ctl"
fi
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/github-runner.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/grafana-domain.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish Grafana on an HTTPS domain via Caddy (automatic Let's Encrypt).
# Requires: monitoring installed, A record pointing to this server (DNS only, no proxy), ports 80/443 open.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DOMAIN="${DOMAIN:-}"
ACME_EMAIL="${ACME_EMAIL:-}"
CADDY_IMAGE="${CADDY_IMAGE:-caddy:2.10.0}"
DIR=/opt/monitoring

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" || -z "$DOMAIN" || -z "$ACME_EMAIL" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: DOMAIN=grafana.example.com ACME_EMAIL=you@example.com $0"
  [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]] && exit 0
  exit 1
fi
require_root
[[ -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml" && -f "$DIR/.env" ]] || die "monitoring stack not found in $DIR"
command -v openssl >/dev/null || pkg_install openssl

server_ip=$(curl -fsS --max-time 5 http://169.254.169.254/hetzner/v1/metadata/public-ipv4 2>/dev/null || curl -4 -fsS --max-time 5 https://ifconfig.me)
dns_ip=$(getent ahostsv4 "$DOMAIN" | awk 'NR==1 { print $1 }')
log "server ip: $server_ip, dns ip: ${dns_ip:-<none>}"
[[ -n "$dns_ip" ]] || die "$DOMAIN does not resolve yet"
[[ "$dns_ip" == "$server_ip" ]] || die "$DOMAIN points to $dns_ip, expected $server_ip (DNS proxy enabled?)"
if ss -ltn | awk '$4 ~ /:(80|443)$/' | grep -q .; then die "ports 80/443 already in use"; fi

# Let's Encrypt (HTTP-01, TLS-ALPN) and visitors reach Caddy on the host network: open 80/443 in the host firewall if
# one runs. Only added, never removed, and SSH rules are not touched.
if command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld; then
  for svc in http https; do
    firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --add-service="$svc" >/dev/null && firewall-cmd --zone=public --add-service="$svc" >/dev/null \
      || die "cannot open ${svc} in firewalld"
  done
  log "firewalld: http and https opened in the public zone"
elif command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 && ufw status 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Status: active'; then
  ufw allow 80/tcp >/dev/null && ufw allow 443/tcp >/dev/null || die "cannot open 80/443 in ufw"
  log "ufw: 80/tcp and 443/tcp opened"
fi

set_env() {
  if grep -q "^$1=" "$DIR/.env"; then sed -i "s|^$1=.*|$1=$2|" "$DIR/.env"; else echo "$1=$2" >> "$DIR/.env"; fi
}
set_grafana_env() {
  set_env GF_SERVER_DOMAIN "$DOMAIN"
  set_env GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL "https://${DOMAIN}/"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_COOKIE_SECURE "true"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_COOKIE_SAMESITE "lax"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_DISABLE_GRAVATAR "true"
  set_env GF_SECURITY_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY "true"
}
edit_with_backup "$DIR/.env" set_grafana_env
chmod 600 "$DIR/.env"

install -d -m 0755 "$DIR/caddy"
sed -e "s|__DOMAIN__|${DOMAIN}|g" -e "s|__ACME_EMAIL__|${ACME_EMAIL}|g" \
  "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/caddy/Caddyfile.tmpl" > "$DIR/caddy/Caddyfile"

cat > "$DIR/docker-compose.override.yml" <<YAML
services:
  caddy:
    image: ${CADDY_IMAGE}
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 128m
    cap_add:
      - NET_BIND_SERVICE
    volumes:
      - ./caddy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy-data:/data
      - caddy-config:/config
    depends_on: [grafana]

volumes:
  caddy-data:
  caddy-config:
YAML
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

docker run --rm -v "$DIR/caddy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro" "$CADDY_IMAGE" \
  caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile

cd "$DIR"
docker compose pull -q caddy
docker compose up -d

ok=0
for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
  if curl -fsS --max-time 5 "https://${DOMAIN}/api/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok=1; break; fi
  sleep 3
done
if [[ "$ok" != "1" ]]; then
  docker compose logs caddy --tail 40
  die "https://${DOMAIN} not reachable, check firewall ports 80/443 and DNS"
fi

echo | openssl s_client -connect "${DOMAIN}:443" -servername "$DOMAIN" 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer -dates
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "http redirect: %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" "http://${DOMAIN}/"
exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk '/:(3000|9090|9100|9252) / && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || die "an internal port is exposed"
log "OK: https://${DOMAIN}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/grafana-domain.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/host-firewall.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Host firewall and fail2ban for the runner host: firewalld on Rocky/Alma/CentOS, ufw on Debian/Ubuntu.
# Self-contained (no lib.sh) so cloud-init can embed it. Safe to rerun.
#
# Nothing is opened except SSH (22 and every port sshd listens on) and, when Grafana is published on a domain
# (override file exists), 80/443. Services of the host
# (monitoring, logging, caches) listen on 127.0.0.1 or the docker0 IP and need no rule. Lockout guard, as in
# server/server-init-*.sh: the firewall is only started or enabled when SSH is in the saved rules, and it is
# stopped again when SSH is not allowed in the running rules. Also open the same ports in the Hetzner Cloud Firewall.
#
# Docker keeps working: on Rocky firewalld puts docker0 into its own docker zone when Docker starts after firewalld;
# if Docker was already running, this script moves docker0 into that zone (no Docker restart). On Debian
# ufw does not touch the chains Docker manages. Jobs are kept away from the host by ci-job-isolation.sh.
# fail2ban: sshd jail on the journal, 5 tries in 10 minutes, 1 hour ban.
set -Eeuo pipefail

JAIL_FILE="${JAIL_FILE:-/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/50-sshd.local}"   # overridable for tests
GRAFANA_OVERRIDE="${GRAFANA_OVERRIDE:-/opt/monitoring/docker-compose.override.yml}"   # exists once grafana-domain.sh ran

log() { echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] $*"; }
die() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0   enables firewalld (Rocky) or ufw (Debian) with SSH allowed, plus the fail2ban sshd jail"
  exit 0
fi
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || die "run as root"

web_published() { [[ -f "$GRAFANA_OVERRIDE" ]]; }

ssh_ports() {
  { echo 22; sshd -T 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "port" { print $2 }'; } | sort -un
}

put_jail() {
  local banaction="$1" tmp ports
  ports=$(ssh_ports | paste -sd, -)   # the jail must watch every port sshd listens on, not only 22
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  {
    if [[ -n "$banaction" ]]; then
      printf '[DEFAULT]\nbanaction = %s\nbanaction_allports = %s[type=allports]\n\n' "$banaction" "$banaction"
    fi
    printf '[sshd]\nenabled  = true\nport     = %s\nbackend  = systemd\nmaxretry = 5\nfindtime = 10m\nbantime  = 1h\n' "$ports"
  } > "$tmp"
  install -D -m 0644 "$tmp" "$JAIL_FILE"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then restorecon "$JAIL_FILE" || true; fi
}

firewalld_setup() {
  local running=0 changed=0 p zone set_zone
  command -v firewall-cmd >/dev/null 2>&1 || dnf -y -q install firewalld || die "cannot install firewalld"
  systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld && running=1
  # SSH is allowed in the public zone, so the uplink must be in it: make it the default zone (as server-init does).
  if (( running )); then zone=$(firewall-cmd --get-default-zone) || die "cannot read the default zone"; else zone=$(firewall-offline-cmd --get-default-zone) || die "cannot read the default zone"; fi
  # Running: the default zone is switched after the reload, so SSH is never refused in between.
  set_zone=0
  if [[ "$zone" != public ]]; then
    log "firewalld: default zone was ${zone}, set to public"
    if (( running )); then set_zone=1; else firewall-offline-cmd --set-default-zone=public >/dev/null || die "cannot set the default zone"; fi
  fi
  # Permanent rules are written first (offline when firewalld is stopped), then the daemon is started or reloaded.
  fw() { if systemctl is-active --quiet firewalld; then firewall-cmd --permanent "$@"; else firewall-offline-cmd "$@"; fi; }
  fw --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || fw --zone=public --add-service=ssh >/dev/null || die "cannot add ssh to the public zone"
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    [[ "$p" == 22 ]] && continue
    fw --zone=public --query-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fw --zone=public --add-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null || die "cannot add port ${p}"
  done
  if web_published; then
    for p in http https; do
      fw --zone=public --query-service="$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fw --zone=public --add-service="$p" >/dev/null || die "cannot add ${p} to the public zone"
    done
    log "firewalld: http and https kept open (Grafana is published on a domain)"
  fi
  # Lockout guard: the saved rules must allow SSH before the firewall runs.
  fw --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "ssh missing from the saved public zone; firewall left as it was"
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    [[ "$p" == 22 ]] && continue
    fw --zone=public --query-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "port ${p} missing from the saved public zone; firewall left as it was"
  done
  if (( running )); then firewall-cmd --reload >/dev/null || die "firewalld reload failed"; else systemctl enable --now firewalld || die "firewalld did not start"; fi
  systemctl enable firewalld >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  if (( set_zone )); then firewall-cmd --set-default-zone=public >/dev/null || die "cannot set the default zone"; fi
  if ! firewall-cmd --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null; then
    systemctl stop firewalld
    die "ssh not allowed after start; firewalld stopped"
  fi
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    [[ "$p" == 22 ]] && continue
    if ! firewall-cmd --zone=public --query-port="${p}/tcp" >/dev/null; then
      systemctl stop firewalld
      die "ssh port ${p} not allowed after start; firewalld stopped"
    fi
  done
  # The default public zone opens cockpit (and mdns on some images); a runner host needs neither. Only these services
  # are removed, never ssh.
  for p in cockpit mdns; do
    if firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --query-service="$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      if firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=public --remove-service="$p" >/dev/null; then changed=1; else log "WARN: could not remove $p from the public zone"; fi
    fi
  done
  if (( changed )); then
    firewall-cmd --reload >/dev/null || die "firewalld reload failed"
    if ! firewall-cmd --zone=public --query-service=ssh >/dev/null; then systemctl stop firewalld; die "ssh not allowed after reload; firewalld stopped"; fi
  fi
  log "firewalld: active, public zone: $(firewall-cmd --zone=public --list-services) $(firewall-cmd --zone=public --list-ports)"
  docker_zone
}

# Docker that was running before firewalld left docker0 in the default zone, where firewalld rejects job traffic to
# the host (the npm cache on the docker0 address). Put docker0 into the docker zone (target ACCEPT, as Docker makes it),
# permanently and now, without restarting Docker. iptables rules (ci-job-isolation.sh) still apply on top.
docker_zone() {
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet docker || return 0
  ip link show docker0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  [[ "$(firewall-cmd --get-zone-of-interface=docker0 2>/dev/null)" == docker ]] && return 0
  if ! firewall-cmd --permanent --get-zones | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx docker; then
    firewall-cmd --permanent --new-zone=docker >/dev/null && firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=docker --set-target=ACCEPT >/dev/null \
      && firewall-cmd --reload >/dev/null || { log "WARN: cannot create the firewalld docker zone; restart Docker while no CI job runs: systemctl restart docker"; return 0; }
  fi
  if firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=docker --add-interface=docker0 >/dev/null && firewall-cmd --zone=docker --change-interface=docker0 >/dev/null; then
    log "firewalld: docker0 put into the docker zone"
  else
    log "WARN: docker0 is not in the docker zone; restart Docker while no CI job runs: systemctl restart docker"
  fi
}

ufw_setup() {
  local p o was_active=0
  command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 || { DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q ufw >/dev/null || die "cannot install ufw"; }
  o=$(ufw status 2>/dev/null) || true
  if grep -q '^Status: active' <<<"$o"; then was_active=1; fi
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do ufw allow "${p}/tcp" >/dev/null || die "cannot allow ${p}/tcp"; done
  if web_published; then
    ufw allow 80/tcp >/dev/null && ufw allow 443/tcp >/dev/null || die "cannot allow 80/443 in ufw"
    log "ufw: 80/tcp and 443/tcp kept open (Grafana is published on a domain)"
  fi
  # Lockout guard: every SSH port must be in the saved rules before ufw is enabled.
  o=$(ufw show added 2>/dev/null) || true
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    grep -qE "^ufw (allow|limit) (in )?${p}/tcp([[:space:]]|\$)" <<<"$o" || die "${p}/tcp missing from the saved ufw rules; ufw left as it was"
  done
  if (( ! was_active )); then
    ufw default deny incoming >/dev/null
    ufw default allow outgoing >/dev/null
    ufw --force enable >/dev/null
  fi
  systemctl enable ufw >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  o=$(ufw status 2>/dev/null) || true
  for p in $(ssh_ports); do
    if ! grep -qE "^${p}/tcp([[:space:]]+\\(v6\\))?[[:space:]]+(ALLOW|LIMIT)" <<<"$o"; then
      if (( ! was_active )); then ufw disable >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
      die "ssh port ${p} not allowed in the running ufw; ufw disabled again"
    fi
  done
  log "ufw: $(ufw status | head -1); allowed: $(ssh_ports | tr '\n' ' ')"
}

# FIREWALL_BACKEND=firewalld|ufw overrides the choice by package manager (used by the tests).
backend="${FIREWALL_BACKEND:-}"
if [[ -z "$backend" ]]; then
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then backend=firewalld; elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then backend=ufw; fi
fi

if [[ "$backend" == firewalld ]]; then
  dnf -y -q install epel-release >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  dnf -y -q install fail2ban-server fail2ban-firewalld >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: fail2ban not available (EPEL?), sshd jail skipped"
  firewalld_setup
  if command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    put_jail ""
    systemctl enable --now fail2ban >/dev/null && systemctl restart fail2ban
  fi
elif [[ "$backend" == ufw ]]; then
  DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q fail2ban >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: fail2ban not installed, sshd jail skipped"
  ufw_setup
  if command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    put_jail nftables
    systemctl enable --now fail2ban >/dev/null && systemctl restart fail2ban
  fi
else
  die "no supported package manager"
fi
if command -v fail2ban-client >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "fail2ban: $(fail2ban-client status 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || true)"
fi
log "OK: host firewall on. If you lock yourself out, use the Hetzner web console: systemctl stop firewalld (or: ufw disable)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/host-firewall.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/host-tools.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install health (plus the sudo secure_path fix so `sudo health` works), cleanup and disk guard scripts plus their systemd timers,
# the job isolation rules (CI jobs cannot reach the metadata service or host services), the weekly Docker/GitLab Runner update,
# and the kernel hardening (sysctl) and core dump settings that the cloud-init files also write.
# Use on servers built without the cloud-init in this repo, or to update the scripts.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs common/health, cleanup, disk guard and systemd timers"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
command -v python3 >/dev/null || die "python3 is required for freshness checks"

install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/common/health" /usr/local/bin/health
restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/health
for f in freshness config-drift; do
  install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/common/$f" "/usr/local/bin/$f"
  restorecon_if "/usr/local/bin/$f"
done
install -d -m 0755 /etc/server-freshness
printf '%s\n' "$REPO_ROOT" | install -m 0644 /dev/stdin /etc/server-freshness/repo
restorecon_if -R /etc/server-freshness
for f in runner-weekly-cleanup.sh runner-disk-guard.sh runner-engine-update.sh ci-job-isolation.sh; do
  install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/runner/scripts/$f" "/usr/local/bin/$f"
  restorecon_if "/usr/local/bin/$f"
done
ensure_secure_path

for u in runner-weekly-cleanup.service runner-weekly-cleanup.timer runner-disk-guard.service runner-disk-guard.timer runner-engine-update.service runner-engine-update.timer ci-job-isolation.service server-freshness.service server-freshness.timer; do
  install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/runner/systemd/$u" "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
  restorecon_if "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
done

# Kernel hardening and no core dumps: the same files and contents as the cloud-init files (keys the kernel lacks are ignored).
install -D -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/common/sysctl-hardening.conf" /etc/sysctl.d/90-ci-hardening.conf
install -D -m 0644 /dev/stdin /etc/security/limits.d/50-nocore.conf <<'LIMITS'
* hard core 0
LIMITS
install -D -m 0644 /dev/stdin /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/50-off.conf <<'COREDUMP'
[Coredump]
Storage=none
ProcessSizeMax=0
COREDUMP
restorecon_if /etc/sysctl.d/90-ci-hardening.conf
sysctl --system >/dev/null || log "WARN: sysctl --system reported an error"

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now runner-weekly-cleanup.timer runner-disk-guard.timer runner-engine-update.timer server-freshness.timer
# Needs Docker (the DOCKER-USER chain). On a host without it the unit is enabled and applies at the next Docker start.
if systemctl is-active --quiet docker; then systemctl enable --now ci-job-isolation.service; else systemctl enable ci-job-isolation.service; fi

DRY_RUN=1 /usr/local/bin/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh >/dev/null
systemctl list-timers 'runner-*' --no-pager
log "OK: run 'health' for a full report (it uses sudo itself when needed)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/host-tools.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/image-prewarm.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Daily pre-pull of all tags of the CI images in a GitLab Container Registry.
# Needs a project deploy token with read_registry scope.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

CRANE_VERSION="${CRANE_VERSION:-v0.20.2}"
CONF=/etc/ci-prewarm.conf
REPOS="${REPOS:-mirror/alpine mirror/node mirror/playwright mirror/snyk mirror/sonar-scanner-cli docker}"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0
Asks for the full path of one image (copy icon in Container Registry) and a deploy token.
Env: REPOS (space separated, relative to the project registry), CRANE_VERSION
USAGE
  exit 0
fi
require_root

case "$(uname -m)" in
  aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
  x86_64)  arch=x86_64 ;;
  *) die "unsupported arch $(uname -m)" ;;
esac

if ! command -v crane >/dev/null; then
  log "installing crane ${CRANE_VERSION}"
  tmp=$(mktemp -d)
  base="https://github.com/google/go-containerregistry/releases/download/${CRANE_VERSION}"
  tarball="go-containerregistry_Linux_${arch}.tar.gz"
  curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/$tarball" "$base/$tarball"
  curl -fsSL -o "$tmp/checksums.txt" "$base/checksums.txt"
  (cd "$tmp" && grep " ${tarball}\$" checksums.txt | sha256sum -c -) || { rm -rf "$tmp"; die "crane checksum mismatch"; }
  tar -xzf "$tmp/$tarball" -C "$tmp" crane
  install -m 0755 "$tmp/crane" /usr/local/bin/crane
  rm -rf "$tmp"
  restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/crane
fi

read -ra repo_list <<<"$REPOS"
[[ ${#repo_list[@]} -gt 0 ]] || die "REPOS is empty"
first_repo="${repo_list[0]}"
read -rp "Paste the full path of ${first_repo} (copy icon in Container Registry): " ref
ref="${ref%%:*}"
[[ "$ref" == registry.gitlab.com/*/"${first_repo}" ]] || die "expected registry.gitlab.com/.../${first_repo}, got: $ref"
BASE="${ref%/"${first_repo}"}"
# /etc/ci-prewarm.conf is sourced as root: accept only plain registry path characters.
path_re='^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$'
[[ "$BASE" =~ $path_re ]] || die "registry path contains unexpected characters: $BASE"
for r in "${repo_list[@]}"; do [[ "$r" =~ $path_re ]] || die "REPOS entry contains unexpected characters: $r"; done

read -rp "Deploy token username (gitlab+deploy-token-...): " dt_user
read -rsp "Deploy token: " dt_token; echo
[[ "$dt_user" == gitlab+deploy-token-* ]] || die "unexpected deploy token username"
printf '%s' "$dt_token" | docker login registry.gitlab.com -u "$dt_user" --password-stdin >/dev/null
unset dt_token
chmod 600 /root/.docker/config.json
crane ls "$BASE/$first_repo" >/dev/null || die "cannot list $BASE/$first_repo with this token"

{
  printf 'BASE=%q\n' "$BASE"
  printf 'REPOS=(%s)\n' "$(printf '%q ' "${repo_list[@]}")"
} > "$CONF"
chmod 644 "$CONF"

install -m 0755 "$REPO_ROOT/runner/scripts/ci-image-prewarm.sh" /usr/local/bin/ci-image-prewarm.sh
restorecon_if /usr/local/bin/ci-image-prewarm.sh
for u in ci-image-prewarm.service ci-image-prewarm.timer; do
  install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/runner/systemd/$u" "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
  restorecon_if "/etc/systemd/system/$u"
done
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now ci-image-prewarm.timer

log "first prewarm run (playwright images are large, this can take minutes)"
systemctl start ci-image-prewarm.service || true
journalctl -t ci-image-prewarm --since "-30min" --no-pager -o cat | grep -E 'OK|NO ARM|FAIL|summary' | sed -E 's/^[0-9T:-]+ //'
log "NO ARM lines: re-mirror those tags with crane copy (see runner/ci/mirror-images.yml)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/image-prewarm.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/job-limits.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Per-job CPU, memory, swap and /dev/shm limits in [runners.docker] of /etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml, plus a systemd
# slice (ci-jobs.slice) that caps the process count and, optionally, the memory of ALL job containers together, so
# one job cannot take the whole host. The limits cover the build container and its `services:` containers (postgres,
# redis, ...). Backs up the file, changes only these keys, and is safe to rerun. A value you already set in
# config.toml is kept unless you pass it in the environment. Swap follows memory (no swap) unless JOB_MEMORY_SWAP
# (JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY_SWAP) is given or the file already has a memory_swap (service_memory_swap).
#
# GitLab Runner has no per-container process limit, so processes are limited per host through the slice: the jobs
# together can start at most JOBS_TASKS_MAX processes and threads (default 4096), and a fork bomb ends there instead of
# exhausting the host. JOBS_MEMORY_MAX (default 3G) is a ceiling for all job containers together; "" or "infinity" turns it off.
#
# Defaults suit a CAX11 (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM) with concurrent = 2: two jobs at 1.5 CPU and 1.5 GB, services at 384 MB,
# and a 3 GB ceiling for all of them leave about 1 GB for the host and its stacks. A bigger host: raise JOB_MEMORY,
# JOB_CPUS and JOBS_MEMORY_MAX and keep concurrent x limit below the hardware. A job that needs more fails with an
# out-of-memory kill (exit 137) instead of freezing the host. The opt-in GitHub Actions runner (runner/install/github-runner.sh) shares
# this slice: its pod is a runner container with the same JOB_CPUS/JOB_MEMORY plus a BuildKit sidecar (768m), one pod at a time, so with it
# installed keep concurrent = 1 (or raise JOBS_MEMORY_MAX on a bigger host) or a busy host hits the ceiling and kills a job.
# gitlab-runner reloads config.toml by itself; running jobs keep their old limits, new jobs get the new ones.
#
# Env: JOB_MEMORY (default 1536m), JOB_MEMORY_SWAP (default = JOB_MEMORY, i.e. no swap), JOB_CPUS (default 1.5),
#      JOB_SHM_SIZE in bytes (default 268435456), JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY (default 384m), JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY_SWAP
#      (default = JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY), JOB_SERVICE_CPUS (default 0.5), JOBS_TASKS_MAX (default 4096),
#      JOBS_MEMORY_MAX (default 3G)
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

CFG="${RUNNER_CONFIG:-/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml}"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  sed -n '2,24p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'
  exit 0
fi
require_root
[[ -f "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^[[:space:]]*\[runners.docker\]' "$CFG" || die "no [runners.docker] section in ${CFG}: register the runner first (runner/install/register-runner.sh)"

mem_default="${JOB_MEMORY:-1536m}"
[[ "$mem_default" =~ ^[0-9]+[kmg]$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_MEMORY: ${mem_default} (for example 1536m)"
swap_default="${JOB_MEMORY_SWAP:-$mem_default}"
[[ "$swap_default" =~ ^[0-9]+[kmg]$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_MEMORY_SWAP: ${swap_default}"
cpus_default="${JOB_CPUS:-1.5}"
[[ "$cpus_default" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_CPUS: ${cpus_default}"
shm_default="${JOB_SHM_SIZE:-268435456}"
[[ "$shm_default" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_SHM_SIZE: ${shm_default}"
smem_default="${JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY:-384m}"
[[ "$smem_default" =~ ^[0-9]+[kmg]$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY: ${smem_default}"
sswap_default="${JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY_SWAP:-$smem_default}"
[[ "$sswap_default" =~ ^[0-9]+[kmg]$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY_SWAP: ${sswap_default}"
scpus_default="${JOB_SERVICE_CPUS:-0.5}"
[[ "$scpus_default" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]] || die "invalid JOB_SERVICE_CPUS: ${scpus_default}"
tasks_max="${JOBS_TASKS_MAX:-4096}"
[[ "$tasks_max" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "invalid JOBS_TASKS_MAX: ${tasks_max}"
mem_max="${JOBS_MEMORY_MAX-3G}"
[[ -z "$mem_max" || "$mem_max" == "infinity" || "$mem_max" =~ ^[0-9]+[KMGkmg]?$ ]] || die "invalid JOBS_MEMORY_MAX: ${mem_max} (for example 3G)"
# systemd only accepts upper-case K/M/G suffixes; a lower-case value would be ignored with a warning.
mem_max="${mem_max^^}"
[[ "$mem_max" == "INFINITY" ]] && mem_max="infinity"

# The slice is the parent cgroup of every job and service container (Docker uses the systemd cgroup driver on these hosts).
slice="${JOBS_SLICE_FILE:-/etc/systemd/system/ci-jobs.slice}"
slice_tmp=$(mktemp)
tmp=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$tmp" "$slice_tmp"' EXIT
{
  echo "# Written by runner/install/job-limits.sh: ceiling for all CI job containers together."
  echo "[Slice]"
  echo "TasksMax=${tasks_max}"
  if [[ -n "$mem_max" && "$mem_max" != "infinity" ]]; then echo "MemoryMax=${mem_max}"; fi
} > "$slice_tmp"
if ! cmp -s "$slice_tmp" "$slice" 2>/dev/null; then
  install -m 0644 "$slice_tmp" "$slice"
  systemctl daemon-reload 2>/dev/null || true
  log "wrote ${slice}"
fi

# Lines: key, value, force (1 when the environment gave the value: it then replaces what config.toml has).
# memory_swap and service_memory_swap follow their memory key when neither is set.
specs=$(printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
  memory "\"${mem_default}\"" "${JOB_MEMORY:+1}" \
  memory_swap "\"${swap_default}\"" "${JOB_MEMORY_SWAP:+1}${JOB_MEMORY:+1}" \
  cpus "\"${cpus_default}\"" "${JOB_CPUS:+1}" \
  shm_size "${shm_default}" "${JOB_SHM_SIZE:+1}" \
  cgroup_parent '"ci-jobs.slice"' 1 \
  service_memory "\"${smem_default}\"" "${JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY:+1}" \
  service_memory_swap "\"${sswap_default}\"" "${JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY_SWAP:+1}${JOB_SERVICE_MEMORY:+1}" \
  service_cpus "\"${scpus_default}\"" "${JOB_SERVICE_CPUS:+1}" \
  service_cgroup_parent '"ci-jobs.slice"' 1)
awk -v specs="$specs" '
  function flush(   k) {
    if (!insec) return
    # Without its own value, swap follows the memory limit of this section (swap below memory is rejected by Docker).
    if (!seen["memory_swap"] && curmem != "") vals["memory_swap"] = curmem
    if (!seen["service_memory_swap"] && cursmem != "") vals["service_memory_swap"] = cursmem
    for (k = 1; k <= n; k++) if (!seen[names[k]]) print "    " names[k] " = " vals[names[k]]
    insec = 0
  }
  function val(line,   v) { v = line; sub(/^[^=]*=[[:space:]]*/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*$/, "", v); return v }
  BEGIN {
    n = split(specs, lines, "\n")
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) { split(lines[i], f, "\t"); names[i] = f[1]; vals[f[1]] = f[2]; force[f[1]] = f[3] }
  }
  /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { flush() }
  /^[[:space:]]*\[runners\.docker\][[:space:]]*$/ { insec = 1; curmem = ""; cursmem = ""; split("", seen); print; next }
  insec {
    # pids_limit is not a GitLab Runner key (an older version of this script wrote it): drop it.
    if ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*pids_limit[[:space:]]*=") next
    for (k = 1; k <= n; k++) {
      nm = names[k]
      if ($0 ~ "^[[:space:]]*" nm "[[:space:]]*=") {
        seen[nm] = 1
        if (nm == "memory") curmem = val($0)
        if (nm == "service_memory") cursmem = val($0)
        if (force[nm]) { if (nm == "memory") curmem = vals[nm]; if (nm == "service_memory") cursmem = vals[nm]; print "    " nm " = " vals[nm]; next }
      }
    }
  }
  { print }
  END { flush() }
' "$CFG" > "$tmp"

if cmp -s "$tmp" "$CFG"; then
  log "job limits already set in ${CFG}"
else
  backup "$CFG"
  cat "$tmp" > "$CFG"
  log "job limits written to ${CFG}"
fi
awk '/^[[:space:]]*\[runners\.docker\]/ { s = 1; next } /^[[:space:]]*\[/ { s = 0 } s && /^[[:space:]]*(memory|memory_swap|cpus|shm_size|cgroup_parent|service_[a-z_]+)[[:space:]]*=/' "$CFG"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/job-limits.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/lock-root.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Disable SSH for root. Run only after "ssh ADMIN@server sudo -n true" works. See runner/install/users.sh --help.
# Extra options go to users.sh; --unlock-root and --help replace the default --lock-root.
set -Eeuo pipefail
mode=(--lock-root)
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --unlock-root|-h|--help) mode=() ;;
  esac
done
exec bash "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/users.sh" "${mode[@]}" "$@"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/lock-root.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/logging.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log collection: Loki (storage, 7 days) + Grafana Alloy (container logs and the systemd journal).
# CI job containers are not collected, their output is the job log in GitLab.
# Alloy reads the Docker socket, which is root-equivalent on the host. Everything listens on 127.0.0.1.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR=/opt/logging
MON=/opt/monitoring
PROM_CFG="${MON}/prometheus/prometheus.yml"
DATASOURCE="${MON}/grafana/provisioning/datasources/loki.yml"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs Loki + Grafana Alloy into $DIR and adds Loki to Grafana if monitoring is installed"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
mon_ids
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not installed"
docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker compose plugin missing"
command -v jq >/dev/null || pkg_install jq
if [[ -f "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml" ]]; then
  log "${DIR} exists: re-applying the repo files and finishing the setup (safe after a failed run)"
elif ss -ltn | awk '$4 ~ /:(3100|9096|12345)$/' | grep -q .; then
  die "port 3100, 9096 or 12345 already in use"
fi
[[ -f /etc/machine-id ]] || die "/etc/machine-id missing, the journal cannot be read"

if [[ ! -d /var/log/journal ]]; then
  log "enabling persistent journal in /var/log/journal"
  install -d -m 2755 -g systemd-journal /var/log/journal
  systemd-tmpfiles --create --prefix /var/log/journal
  systemctl restart systemd-journald
fi

selinux_label_dir "$DIR"
cp -a "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/docker-compose.yml" "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/loki.yaml" "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/config.alloy" "${DIR}/"
stack_ids "$DIR" logging
own_stack_dir "$DIR"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

loki_image=$(awk '/image: grafana\/loki/ { print $2 }' "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml")
alloy_image=$(awk '/image: grafana\/alloy/ { print $2 }' "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml")

cd "$DIR"
docker compose config -q
docker compose pull -q
docker run --rm --user "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" -v "${DIR}/loki.yaml:/etc/loki/config.yaml:ro" "$loki_image" \
  -config.file=/etc/loki/config.yaml -verify-config || die "Loki rejected loki.yaml"
docker run --rm --user "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" --entrypoint /bin/alloy -v "${DIR}/config.alloy:/config/config.alloy:ro" "$alloy_image" \
  fmt /config/config.alloy >/dev/null || die "Alloy rejected config.alloy"
chown_volumes "$DIR"
docker compose up -d --force-recreate

ready=0
for _ in $(seq 1 45); do
  if curl -fsS -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:3100/ready >/dev/null 2>&1 && curl -fsS -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:12345/-/ready >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ready=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
if (( ! ready )); then
  docker compose logs --tail 40
  die "Loki or Alloy did not become ready"
fi

if [[ -d "${MON}/grafana/provisioning/datasources" ]]; then
  cp "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/logging/grafana-datasource.yml" "$DATASOURCE"
  chown "root:${MON_USER}" "$DATASOURCE"
  chmod 640 "$DATASOURCE"
  restorecon_if "$DATASOURCE"
  (cd "$MON" && docker compose restart grafana >/dev/null)
  log "Loki added to Grafana as a datasource"
fi
if [[ -f "$PROM_CFG" ]] && ! grep -q 'job_name: loki' "$PROM_CFG"; then
  backup "$PROM_CFG"
  prom_jobs_logging >> "$PROM_CFG"
  curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/reload || log "WARN: prometheus reload failed"
fi

marker="logging-install-check-$(date +%s)"
logger -t logging-install -- "$marker"
found=0
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  n=$(curl -fsS -G -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range \
        --data-urlencode "query={source=\"journal\"} |= \"${marker}\"" --data-urlencode "since=10m" 2>/dev/null \
      | jq '.data.result | length' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  if [[ "${n:-0}" != "0" ]]; then
    found=1
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
if (( found )); then
  log "journal -> Alloy -> Loki works"
else
  log "WARN: test line not in Loki yet, check: docker compose -f ${DIR}/docker-compose.yml logs alloy"
fi

docker compose ps --format 'table {{.Service}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Status}}'
exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk '/:(3100|9096|12345) / && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || die "a logging port is not bound to 127.0.0.1"
log "OK: logs in Grafana > Explore > Loki, e.g. {unit=\"gitlab-runner.service\"} or {compose_project=\"registry-cache\"}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/logging.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/monitoring-backup.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Back up the Grafana data volume (SQLite database, plugins) before the first start of a new Grafana major.
# Grafana migrates its database forward on start and cannot downgrade: the only way back is this backup plus the old image tag
# (runner/README.md, "Grafana upgrade and rollback"). Called by monitoring.sh and by update.sh before they change the stack.
# Idempotent: it backs up only when the installed image tag and the repo tag are on different majors (or the installed
# version is unknown); a rerun after the compose file was updated is a no-op and the first backup stays.
# It fails (non-zero) when it cannot tell whether there is data to protect (the helper container does not run): never a silent skip.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR="${MON_DIR:-/opt/monitoring}"
# HELPER_IMAGE (alpine, pinned by digest) comes from common/lib.sh, the one place to bump it (also in runner/README.md).
# Read-only root filesystem, no network, no capabilities except reading files of the service user (the volume is owned by it, mode 600/700).
# Without DAC_READ_SEARCH root cannot even enter the directory and `test -s` answers "no database": a silent skip of the backup.
HELPER_ARGS=(--rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --cap-add DAC_READ_SEARCH)
BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR:-/var/backups/monitoring}"
KEEP=3
FROM_TAG=""
TO_TAG=""
FORCE=0
DRYRUN=0

usage() {
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 [--dry-run] [--force] [--from-tag TAG] [--to-tag TAG]

Archives the Grafana data volume to ${BACKUP_DIR}/grafana-<from-version>-<date>.tar.gz (mode 0600, last ${KEEP} kept)
when the Grafana major changes. Grafana is stopped for the copy so the SQLite file is consistent, and started again afterwards.
  --from-tag  version the data belongs to (default: image tag in ${DIR}/docker-compose.yml)
  --to-tag    version about to start (default: image tag in this repo's monitoring compose file)
  --force     back up even when the major does not change
USAGE
}

while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    -n|--dry-run) DRYRUN=1 ;;
    --force) FORCE=1 ;;
    --from-tag) FROM_TAG="${2:?--from-tag needs a value}"; shift ;;
    --to-tag) TO_TAG="${2:?--to-tag needs a value}"; shift ;;
    *) usage >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

grafana_tag() { awk '/image: grafana\/grafana:/ { sub(/.*grafana\/grafana:/, ""); print $1; exit }' "$1"; }
major() { echo "${1%%.*}"; }

require_root
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not installed"

[[ -n "$TO_TAG" ]] || TO_TAG=$(grafana_tag "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/monitoring/docker-compose.yml")
[[ -n "$TO_TAG" ]] || die "cannot read the Grafana tag from the repo compose file"
if [[ -z "$FROM_TAG" && -f "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml" ]]; then FROM_TAG=$(grafana_tag "${DIR}/docker-compose.yml"); fi

vol=$(docker volume ls -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=monitoring --filter label=com.docker.compose.volume=grafana-data | head -n1)
if [[ -z "$vol" ]]; then
  log "grafana backup: no Grafana data volume yet, nothing to back up"
  exit 0
fi

# No compose file (reinstall over a leftover volume): the version is on the stopped container that last used the volume, if any.
if [[ -z "$FROM_TAG" ]]; then
  FROM_TAG=$(docker ps -a --filter "volume=${vol}" --format '{{.Image}}' | awk -F: '/^grafana\/grafana:/ { print $2; exit }')
fi

# Before any container runs, so a normal update on the same major needs no image pull.
if (( ! FORCE )) && [[ -n "$FROM_TAG" && "$(major "$FROM_TAG")" == "$(major "$TO_TAG")" ]]; then
  log "grafana backup: ${FROM_TAG} -> ${TO_TAG} stays on major $(major "$TO_TAG"), no backup needed"
  exit 0
fi

# A dry run only reads: no container, so no image pull. It assumes a database is in the volume.
if (( ! DRYRUN )); then
  # y/n on stdout: a failed docker run (image pull refused or rate limited, no network, daemon down) must not read as "no database",
  # or update.sh would start the new Grafana on data that has no backup.
  has_db=$(docker run "${HELPER_ARGS[@]}" -v "${vol}:/v:ro" "$HELPER_IMAGE" sh -c 'if test -s /v/grafana.db; then echo y; else echo n; fi') \
    || die "grafana backup: cannot check ${vol} (docker run of ${HELPER_IMAGE} failed, image pull or daemon?); not going on without a backup"
  case "$has_db" in
    y) ;;
    n) log "grafana backup: ${vol} holds no database yet, nothing to back up"; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "grafana backup: unexpected answer '${has_db}' while checking ${vol}" ;;
  esac
fi

label=$(printf '%s' "${FROM_TAG:-unknown}" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_')
target="${BACKUP_DIR}/grafana-${label}-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz"
if (( DRYRUN )); then
  log "[dry-run] would back up ${vol}, if it holds a database (${FROM_TAG:-unknown} -> ${TO_TAG}) to ${target}"
  exit 0
fi

install -d -m 0700 "$BACKUP_DIR"
tmp=$(umask 077; mktemp "${BACKUP_DIR}/.grafana-backup.XXXXXX")
stopped=$(docker ps -q --filter "volume=${vol}")
cleanup() {
  rm -f "$tmp"
  if [[ -n "$stopped" ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    docker start $stopped >/dev/null || log "WARN: could not start the Grafana container again, run docker compose up -d in ${DIR}"
  fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [[ -n "$stopped" ]]; then
  log "grafana backup: stopping Grafana for a consistent copy"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  docker stop $stopped >/dev/null
fi
log "grafana backup: ${vol} (${FROM_TAG:-unknown} -> ${TO_TAG})"
docker run "${HELPER_ARGS[@]}" -v "${vol}:/v:ro" "$HELPER_IMAGE" tar -C /v -czf - . > "$tmp"
# Read the listing into a variable first: grep -q exiting early would SIGPIPE tar under pipefail.
listing=$(tar -tzf "$tmp")
grep -Eq '^(\./)?grafana\.db$' <<<"$listing" || die "the archive has no grafana.db, backup discarded"
chmod 600 "$tmp"
mv "$tmp" "$target"
log "grafana backup: wrote ${target} ($(du -h "$target" | cut -f1))"
# An install from before the generated encryption key: its stored credentials are encrypted with Grafana's public default key.
if [[ -f "${DIR}/.env" ]] && ! grep -q '^GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY=' "${DIR}/.env"; then
  log "NOTE: this Grafana uses its built-in default encryption key, so whoever gets the archive can decrypt the data source credentials in it (runner/README.md, Grafana upgrade and rollback)"
fi

# Keep the newest ${KEEP} archives.
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'grafana-*.tar.gz' -printf '%T@ %p\n' | sort -rn | tail -n "+$((KEEP + 1))" | cut -d' ' -f2- \
  | xargs -r rm -f --
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/monitoring-backup.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/monitoring.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install Prometheus + node_exporter + Grafana (all bound to 127.0.0.1) with the runner dashboard.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR=/opt/monitoring

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs the monitoring stack into $DIR"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
mon_ids
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "docker not installed"
docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker compose plugin missing"
command -v jq >/dev/null || pkg_install jq
[[ -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml" ]] && die "$DIR/docker-compose.yml exists, stack already installed"

# A Grafana volume left over from an earlier install is archived before a new major can migrate it (no-op on a clean host).
# The copy-paste block (runner/COMMANDS.md) carries monitoring.sh alone, without the backup script: skip it there.
backup_script="$(dirname "$0")/monitoring-backup.sh"
if [[ -f "$backup_script" ]]; then
  bash "$backup_script"
else
  log "WARN: ${backup_script} not found, a Grafana volume left over from an earlier install is not archived"
fi

selinux_label_dir "$DIR"
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9252/metrics >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: runner metrics on 127.0.0.1:9252 not reachable"

cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/docker-compose.yml" "$DIR/"
cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/grafana" "$DIR/"

if [[ ! -f "$DIR/.env" ]]; then
  pw=$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | cut -c1-24)
  # Grafana encrypts stored credentials (data source passwords, API keys) with secret_key, which is a public default unless set.
  # Generated only on a first install: data that exists under the default key (a volume left over from an earlier install) cannot be
  # read with a new one, so there the default stays. The key belongs next to every backup archive (runner/README.md).
  sk=""
  # A failed `docker volume ls` (daemon down) must not read as "no volume": a key generated over a default-key volume locks its data.
  vols=$(docker volume ls -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=monitoring --filter label=com.docker.compose.volume=grafana-data) \
    || die "cannot list docker volumes (is the Docker daemon running?)"
  if [[ -z "$vols" ]]; then
    sk=$(head -c 96 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | cut -c1-40)
  else
    # The volume may have been written under a key of the earlier install; this run has no way to know it, so it adds none.
    log "NOTE: a Grafana data volume exists, so no new encryption key is generated and Grafana uses its built-in default key"
    log "NOTE: if the earlier install's .env had a GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY line, put that same line back in ${DIR}/.env; Grafana is started by this run on the default key, so after adding it run: cd ${DIR} && sudo docker compose up -d grafana (recreates Grafana with the key). An existing .env is kept, so restoring the earlier .env before the installer also works; see runner/README.md, Grafana upgrade and rollback"
  fi
  (umask 077
   sed "s/^GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=.*/GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${pw}/" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/monitoring/env.example" | grep -v '^#' > "$DIR/.env"
   if [[ -n "$sk" ]]; then printf 'GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY=%s\n' "$sk" >> "$DIR/.env"; fi)
  unset pw sk vols
fi
chmod 600 "$DIR/.env"
stack_ids "$DIR"
own_stack_dir "$DIR"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

prom_image=$(awk '/image: prom\/prometheus/ { print $2 }' "$DIR/docker-compose.yml")
jq empty "$DIR/grafana/dashboards/gitlab-runner.json"
docker compose -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml" config -q
docker run --rm --user "${MON_UID}:${MON_GID}" --entrypoint promtool -v "$DIR/prometheus:/etc/prometheus:ro" "$prom_image" \
  check config /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml

cd "$DIR"
docker compose pull -q
chown_volumes "$DIR"
docker compose up -d

for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/ready >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 2
done
for _ in $(seq 1 15); do
  down=$(curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/targets | jq '[.data.activeTargets[] | select(.health != "up")] | length')
  [[ "$down" == "0" ]] && break
  sleep 2
done

docker compose ps --format 'table {{.Service}}\t{{.State}}\t{{.Status}}'
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/targets | jq -r '.data.activeTargets[] | "\(.labels.job)\t\(.health)\t\(.lastError)"'
ss -ltn | awk 'NR==1 || /:(9090|9100|3000|9252) /'

exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk '/:(9090|9100|3000) / && $4 !~ /^127\.0\.0\.1:/' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || die "a monitoring port is not bound to 127.0.0.1"
log "OK: monitoring up. Grafana password: sudo grep GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD $DIR/.env"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/monitoring.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/npm-cache.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Verdaccio npm pull-through cache on the docker0 bridge IP, exposed to CI jobs via runner env.
# If the cache is down, npm ci in jobs fails (npm has no automatic fallback).
# Storage and the server secret are prepared by the container itself at every start (config "start" in the compose file):
# storage of an older major is moved aside to backup-*, Verdaccio 7 needs a secret of exactly 32 characters.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR=/opt/npm-cache
CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs Verdaccio into $DIR and points runner jobs at it"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
require_compose_min 2.23.1 "npm-cache"   # the compose file carries its start script as inline "configs: content:"
if ! { [[ -f "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$CFG"; }; then die "runner not registered yet, run runner/install/register-runner.sh first"; fi

BRIDGE_IP=$(ip -4 -o addr show docker0 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $4 }' | cut -d/ -f1)
[[ -n "$BRIDGE_IP" ]] || die "docker0 bridge not found"
REG="http://${BRIDGE_IP}:4873/"
require_runner_idle

selinux_label_dir "$DIR"
sed "s/172\.17\.0\.1:4873/${BRIDGE_IP}:4873/" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/npm-cache/config.yaml" > "$DIR/config.yaml"
sed "s/172\.17\.0\.1:4873/${BRIDGE_IP}:4873/" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/npm-cache/docker-compose.yml" > "$DIR/docker-compose.yml"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

cd "$DIR"
docker compose config -q
docker compose pull -q
docker compose up -d
for _ in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS "${REG}-/ping" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done
curl -fsS "${REG}-/ping" >/dev/null || { docker compose logs --tail 30; die "verdaccio did not start"; }
docker compose logs --no-log-prefix verdaccio 2>&1 | grep '^npm-cache:' || true

exposed=$(ss -ltn | awk -v want="${BRIDGE_IP}:4873" '/:4873 / && $4 != want' | wc -l)
[[ "$exposed" == "0" ]] || { ss -ltn | awk '/:4873 /'; die "port 4873 is not bound to ${BRIDGE_IP} only"; }

edit_with_backup "$CFG" runner_env_merge "npm_config_registry=${REG}" "YARN_NPM_REGISTRY_SERVER=${REG}" "YARN_UNSAFE_HTTP_WHITELIST=${BRIDGE_IP}"
systemctl restart gitlab-runner
sleep 3

docker run --rm -e npm_config_registry="$REG" node:22-alpine sh -c \
  'cd /tmp && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install --no-audit --no-fund lodash >/dev/null && echo "npm install via cache OK"' \
  || die "npm install through verdaccio failed"

grep -n 'environment =' "$CFG"
ss -ltn | awk 'NR==1 || /:4873 /'
gitlab-runner verify 2>&1 | grep -E 'is valid|is not valid' || true
log "OK: npm cache at ${REG}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/npm-cache.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/register-runner.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Register a docker-executor runner with a glrt- token and apply the job pickup fix.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

GITLAB_URL="${GITLAB_URL:-https://gitlab.com}"
DESCRIPTION="${DESCRIPTION:-hetzner-$(uname -n)}"
DEFAULT_IMAGE="${DEFAULT_IMAGE:-$HELPER_IMAGE}"
REQUEST_CONCURRENCY="${REQUEST_CONCURRENCY:-2}"
CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0
Env: GITLAB_URL (default https://gitlab.com), DESCRIPTION (default hetzner-<hostname>),
     DEFAULT_IMAGE (default ${HELPER_IMAGE}), REQUEST_CONCURRENCY (default 2)
Per-job limits (memory 1536m, cpus 1.5, shm 256 MB, services 384m, and a ci-jobs.slice with a process and memory ceiling) are added to config.toml; see runner/install/job-limits.sh.
Tags, untagged jobs, protected and locked are set in the GitLab UI when creating the runner.
The token is read interactively and never stored in shell history.
USAGE
  exit 0
fi
require_root
command -v gitlab-runner >/dev/null || die "gitlab-runner not installed"
systemctl is-active --quiet docker || die "docker is not running"
if [[ -f "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$CFG"; then
  die "a runner is already registered in ${CFG}. Remove it first: gitlab-runner unregister --all-runners"
fi

read -rsp "Runner authentication token (glrt-...): " token; echo
[[ "$token" == glrt-* ]] || die "token must start with glrt-"

[[ -f "$CFG" ]] && backup "$CFG"
gitlab-runner register --non-interactive \
  --url "$GITLAB_URL" \
  --token "$token" \
  --executor docker \
  --docker-image "$DEFAULT_IMAGE" \
  --description "$DESCRIPTION" \
  --docker-pull-policy "if-not-present" \
  --docker-volumes "/cache" >/dev/null
unset token

if ! grep -q 'request_concurrency' "$CFG"; then
  sed -i -E "0,/^  name = .*/s//&\n  request_concurrency = ${REQUEST_CONCURRENCY}/" "$CFG"
fi
chmod 600 "$CFG"
# Per-job CPU, memory and process limits (runner/install/job-limits.sh); the runner reloads config.toml by itself.
bash "$(dirname "$0")/job-limits.sh" >/dev/null || log "WARN: job limits not set; run runner/install/job-limits.sh"
runner_cfg_owner
systemctl restart gitlab-runner
sleep 3

gitlab-runner verify 2>&1 | grep -E 'is valid|is not valid' || true
grep -nE '^concurrent|^listen_address|request_concurrency|executor' "$CFG"
if grep -qi bottleneck <<<"$(journalctl -u gitlab-runner --since "-1min" --no-pager)"; then
  log "WARN: runner still reports a request bottleneck"
else
  log "OK: runner registered"
fi
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/register-runner.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/registry-cache.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Docker Hub pull-through cache on 127.0.0.1:5000, wired into the Docker daemon as a mirror.
# Restarts Docker: refuses to run while CI jobs are running.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

DIR=/opt/registry-cache
MIRROR="http://127.0.0.1:5000"
DAEMON=/etc/docker/daemon.json
PROM_CFG=/opt/monitoring/prometheus/prometheus.yml

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs the Docker Hub pull-through cache into $DIR"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
command -v jq >/dev/null || pkg_install jq
require_runner_idle
if [[ -f "$DIR/docker-compose.yml" ]]; then
  log "${DIR} exists: re-applying the repo files and finishing the setup (safe to rerun)"
elif ss -ltn | awk '$4 ~ /:(5000|5001)$/' | grep -q .; then
  die "port 5000 or 5001 already in use"
fi

selinux_label_dir "$DIR"
cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/registry-cache/config.yml" "$REPO_ROOT/runner/stacks/registry-cache/docker-compose.yml" "$DIR/"
restorecon_if -R "$DIR"

cd "$DIR"
docker compose config -q
docker compose pull -q
docker compose up -d
for _ in $(seq 1 15); do curl -fsS "$MIRROR/v2/" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done
curl -fsS "$MIRROR/v2/" >/dev/null || { docker compose logs --tail 30; die "registry cache did not start"; }

if ! jq -e --arg m "$MIRROR" '(.["registry-mirrors"] // []) | index($m)' "$DAEMON" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  backup "$DAEMON"
  tmp=$(mktemp)
  jq --arg m "$MIRROR" '.["registry-mirrors"] = [$m]' "$DAEMON" > "$tmp"
  dockerd --validate --config-file "$tmp" >/dev/null || { rm -f "$tmp"; die "new daemon.json is invalid"; }
  install -m 0644 "$tmp" "$DAEMON"
  rm -f "$tmp"
  restorecon_if "$DAEMON"
  log "restarting docker"
  systemctl restart docker
  sleep 5
  if systemctl cat gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemctl restart gitlab-runner || true; fi
  for _ in $(seq 1 20); do curl -fsS "$MIRROR/v2/" >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 2; done
fi

if [[ -f "$PROM_CFG" ]] && ! grep -q 'job_name: registry-cache' "$PROM_CFG"; then
  backup "$PROM_CFG"
  cat >> "$PROM_CFG" <<'YAML'
  - job_name: registry-cache
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:5001"]
YAML
  curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9090/-/reload || log "WARN: prometheus reload failed"
fi

docker rmi -f busybox:1.36 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
docker pull -q busybox:1.36 >/dev/null
docker info 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 'Registry Mirrors'
curl -fsS "$MIRROR/v2/_catalog" | jq -c .
ss -ltn | awk 'NR==1 || /:(5000|5001) /'
log "OK: Docker Hub pull-through cache at ${MIRROR}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/registry-cache.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/selinux-enforcing.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Switch SELinux to enforcing now and after reboot (Rocky/RHEL). Rollback: setenforce 0.
# Restarts Docker and the runner: refuses to run while CI jobs are running.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  enables SELinux enforcing mode and verifies Docker and the runner still work"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
command -v getenforce >/dev/null || die "SELinux tools not present on this system"
require_runner_idle
systemctl is-active --quiet auditd || log "WARN: auditd not active, denials will not be logged"

setenforce 1
sed -i -E 's/^SELINUX=.*/SELINUX=enforcing/' /etc/selinux/config

getenforce
grep -E '^SELINUX=' /etc/selinux/config
hello=$(docker run --rm hello-world)
grep -m1 Hello <<<"$hello"
systemctl restart docker
systemctl restart gitlab-runner || true
systemctl is-active docker gitlab-runner || true
denials=$(ausearch --input-logs -m avc -ts recent </dev/null 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'avc:' || true)
log "recent SELinux denials: ${denials:-0}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/selinux-enforcing.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/shared-cache.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared host cache /srv/ci-cache mounted into every job as /ci-cache (npm tarballs, Sonar plugins).
# The cache is shared across all projects on this runner: only use it for trusted projects.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/../../common/lib.sh"

HOST_DIR=/srv/ci-cache
MOUNT=/ci-cache
CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  mounts $HOST_DIR into all jobs and sets npm_config_cache and SONAR_USER_HOME"
  exit 0
fi
require_root
if ! { [[ -f "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^\[\[runners\]\]' "$CFG"; }; then die "runner not registered yet"; fi
require_runner_idle

install -d -m 1777 "$HOST_DIR" "$HOST_DIR/npm" "$HOST_DIR/sonar"
if selinux_on; then
  command -v semanage >/dev/null 2>&1 || pkg_install policycoreutils-python-utils
  grep -q "^${HOST_DIR}(/\.\*)?" <<<"$(semanage fcontext -l)" || semanage fcontext -a -t container_file_t "${HOST_DIR}(/.*)?"
  restorecon -R "$HOST_DIR"
fi

add_shared_cache() {
  if ! grep -q "${HOST_DIR}:${MOUNT}" "$CFG"; then
    grep -qE '^    volumes = \["/cache"\]' "$CFG" || die "unexpected volumes line in [runners.docker], edit manually"
    sed -i -E "s|^    volumes = \[\"/cache\"\]|    volumes = [\"/cache\", \"${HOST_DIR}:${MOUNT}:rw\"]|" "$CFG"
  fi
  runner_env_merge "npm_config_cache=${MOUNT}/npm" "SONAR_USER_HOME=${MOUNT}/sonar"
}
edit_with_backup "$CFG" add_shared_cache
systemctl restart gitlab-runner
sleep 3

docker run --rm --user 1000:1000 -v "${HOST_DIR}:${MOUNT}:rw" "$HELPER_IMAGE" \
  sh -c "touch ${MOUNT}/npm/.probe && rm ${MOUNT}/npm/.probe && echo 'non-root write OK'" \
  || die "containers cannot write to ${HOST_DIR}"

grep -nE 'volumes =|environment =' "$CFG"
gitlab-runner verify 2>&1 | grep -E 'is valid|is not valid' || true
log "OK: shared cache ${HOST_DIR} mounted as ${MOUNT} in all jobs"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/install/shared-cache.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/install"
cat > "$R/runner/install/update.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Bring a server built from this repo up to the current repo state, for the installed components only.
# Syncs scripts, systemd units and stack configs. Never touches secrets (passwords, config.toml, tokens),
# the runner registration, daemon.json or SSH settings. In the stacks' .env it only sets MON_UID and MON_GID
# (logging also DOCKER_GID) and keeps the file root-only at mode 600. For logging it also creates or removes
# /opt/logging/docker-compose.override.yml (extra group_add for the journal gid, only when it differs from docker's).
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=../../common/lib.sh
source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../common/lib.sh"

BACKUP_ROOT=/var/backups/server-init-config
KEEP_BACKUPS=5
BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_ROOT}/$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
LOCK=/run/lock/server-init-update.lock
DRYRUN=0
DO_OS=0
DO_PULL=0
DO_ROLLBACK=0
CHANGED=()
SKIPPED=()
WORK=""

usage() {
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 [--dry-run] [--pull] [--os] [--rollback]

Updates what is installed on this server to the state of this repo checkout:
  host tools     health, cleanup, disk guard (+ prewarm if configured), their systemd units, kernel hardening and core dump settings
  monitoring     /opt/monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, node_exporter, Caddy override if present)
                 (a new Grafana major first archives its data volume to /var/backups/monitoring, last 3 kept)
  logging        /opt/logging (Loki, Grafana Alloy)
  registry-cache /opt/registry-cache
  npm-cache      /opt/npm-cache
  github-runner  controller, unit and the two pinned images (common/lib.sh) in /etc/github-runner/config.env; pulls the images
Components that are not installed are skipped.

  -n, --dry-run  show what would change, change nothing
      --pull     git pull --ff-only in this checkout first (needs a git clone, not an scp copy)
      --os       also upgrade OS packages (Docker, GitLab Runner included); never reboots
      --rollback restore the files from the newest backup in ${BACKUP_ROOT} and recreate the stacks
                 (Grafana keeps its newer compose file once the newer Grafana has started on its data: that part is the archive restore in runner/README.md)

Steps that restart Docker-based caches or upgrade packages are skipped while CI jobs are running
and the script exits with code 3; rerun it when the runner is idle.
Every changed file is first copied to ${BACKUP_ROOT}/<timestamp>/ (last ${KEEP_BACKUPS} runs are kept).
USAGE
}

run() {
  if (( DRYRUN )); then
    log "[dry-run] $*"
  else
    "$@"
  fi
}

backup_to_run() {
  local dst="$1"
  [[ -e "$dst" ]] || return 0
  install -d -m 0700 "$BACKUP_ROOT"
  install -d "${BACKUP_DIR}$(dirname "$dst")"
  cp -a "$dst" "${BACKUP_DIR}${dst}"
}

# sync_file SRC DST MODE [replace|inplace]
# Returns 0 if DST was (or would be) changed, 1 if already identical.
# "inplace" keeps the inode: required for files that are single-file bind mounts in containers.
# "replace" writes a new file: required for scripts that may be running right now.
sync_file() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2" mode="$3" how="${4:-replace}" want_mode
  [[ -f "$src" ]] || die "missing source file $src"
  if [[ -f "$dst" ]] && cmp -s "$src" "$dst"; then
    if [[ "$how" == inplace ]]; then
      return 1
    fi
    want_mode=$(printf '%o' "$((8#${mode}))")
    if [[ "$(stat -c '%a' "$dst")" == "$want_mode" ]]; then
      return 1
    fi
  fi
  if (( DRYRUN )); then
    log "[dry-run] would update ${dst}"
    return 0
  fi
  backup_to_run "$dst"
  if [[ "$how" == inplace && -f "$dst" ]]; then
    cat "$src" > "$dst"
  else
    install -d "$(dirname "$dst")"
    install -m "$mode" "$src" "$dst"
  fi
  restorecon_if "$dst"
  log "updated ${dst}"
  return 0
}

# sync_tree SRC_DIR DST_DIR MODE [replace|inplace]: returns 0 if any file changed.
sync_tree() {
  local src="$1" dst="$2" mode="$3" how="${4:-replace}" f rel rc=1
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    rel="${f#"${src}"/}"
    if sync_file "$f" "${dst}/${rel}" "$mode" "$how"; then
      rc=0
    fi
  done < <(find "$src" -type f -print0)
  return "$rc"
}

grafana_tag() { awk '/image: grafana\/grafana:/ { sub(/.*grafana\/grafana:/, ""); print $1; exit }' "$1"; }

# grafana_ran_tag: which Grafana has (or may have) touched the data volume, by what actually ran, not by the compose file on disk
# (an update can sync the new compose file and abort before `docker compose up`, the old Grafana then still runs on unmigrated data).
# Prints the tag of the newest Grafana container that was ever started; nothing when it cannot tell (no docker, no container, or no
# container with a start record). "No started container" is unknown, not "never ran": `docker compose up --force-recreate` removes a
# started container and its start record, and the replacement may have failed before it started.
grafana_ran_tag() {
  local ids rows
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  ids=$(docker ps -aq --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=monitoring --filter label=com.docker.compose.service=grafana 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -n "$ids" ]] || return 0
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rows=$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}} {{.Config.Image}}' $ids 2>/dev/null) || return 0
  # A started container whose image is not grafana/grafana:TAG prints nothing as well.
  awk '$1 !~ /^0001-/ && $2 ~ /grafana\/grafana:/ { sub(/.*grafana\/grafana:/, "", $2); print $2 }' <<<"$rows" | sort -V | tail -n 1
}

# keep_grafana_major CURRENT_COMPOSE BACKUP_COMPOSE [RAN_TAG]: restoring BACKUP_COMPOSE over CURRENT_COMPOSE must not lower the Grafana major.
# Grafana migrates its database forward and cannot read it back, so an older image on migrated data fails or reads stale tables
# (runner/README.md, "Grafana upgrade and rollback"). RAN_TAG is the output of grafana_ran_tag: the Grafana that actually ran decides.
# When it is empty (unknown) or has no numeric major the tag in CURRENT_COMPOSE is assumed to have run: the safe side, keeping a newer image on unmigrated
# data only means the planned upgrade happens, while an older image on migrated data breaks Grafana.
# Prints the tag to keep, or nothing when the restore is safe.
keep_grafana_major() {
  local cur old
  [[ -f "$1" && -f "$2" ]] || return 0
  cur="${3:-}"
  # unknown (empty) or not a version (e.g. latest): the tag on disk is assumed to have run
  [[ "${cur%%.*}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || cur=$(grafana_tag "$1")
  old=$(grafana_tag "$2")
  [[ "${cur%%.*}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "${old%%.*}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
  if (( ${cur%%.*} > ${old%%.*} )); then
    printf '%s\n' "$cur"
  fi
}

restore_files() {
  local f dst keep="" ran how="has already run" mon=/opt/monitoring/docker-compose.yml
  [[ -d "$BACKUP_DIR" ]] || return 0
  ran=$(grafana_ran_tag)
  [[ "${ran%%.*}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || how="may have run (no started Grafana container with a version tag on record)"
  keep=$(keep_grafana_major "$mon" "${BACKUP_DIR}${mon}" "$ran")
  log "restoring files from ${BACKUP_DIR}"
  while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    dst="${f#"${BACKUP_DIR}"}"
    if [[ -n "$keep" && "$dst" == "$mon" ]]; then
      # Not the old file with the image line patched: that would also bring back its older limits (Grafana 13 needs 512m, not 256m).
      continue
    fi
    if (( DRYRUN )); then
      log "[dry-run] would restore ${dst}"
    else
      cp -a "$f" "$dst"
    fi
  done < <(find "$BACKUP_DIR" -type f -print0)
  if [[ -n "$keep" ]]; then
    log "WARN: grafana ${keep} ${how} on the data and cannot be rolled back with files; ${mon} stays as installed (image grafana/grafana:${keep} and its settings), everything else is restored. To go back, restore the archive (runner/README.md, Grafana upgrade and rollback)"
  fi
  run systemctl daemon-reload
}

prune_backups() {
  [[ -d "$BACKUP_ROOT" ]] || return 0
  find "$BACKUP_ROOT" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d | sort | head -n "-${KEEP_BACKUPS}" | xargs -r rm -rf --
}

need_idle() {
  local n
  n=$(ci_jobs_running)
  if (( n == 0 )); then
    return 0
  fi
  SKIPPED+=("$1")
  log "WARN: ${n} CI job container(s) running, skipping $1 (rerun when idle)"
  return 1
}

wait_url() {
  local url="$1" tries="${2:-30}" i
  for ((i = 0; i < tries; i++)); do
    if curl -fsS --max-time 3 "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 2
  done
  return 1
}

reboot_needed() {
  local running latest
  if [[ -f /var/run/reboot-required ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  if command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1 && rpm -q kernel-core >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    running=$(uname -r)
    latest=$(rpm -q kernel-core --qf '%{VERSION}-%{RELEASE}.%{ARCH}\n' | sort -V | tail -n 1)
    if [[ "$running" != "$latest" ]]; then
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  return 1
}

update_os() {
  need_idle "os-packages" || return 0
  if (( DRYRUN )); then
    log "[dry-run] would upgrade OS packages"
    return 0
  fi
  log "upgrading OS packages"
  if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dnf -y upgrade --refresh
  elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    apt-get update -q
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -y -q -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold upgrade
  else
    die "no supported package manager"
  fi
  CHANGED+=("os-packages")
  local svc
  for svc in docker gitlab-runner; do
    if systemctl cat "$svc" >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! systemctl is-active --quiet "$svc"; then
      log "WARN: ${svc} is not active after the upgrade"
    fi
  done
  if reboot_needed; then
    log "REBOOT RECOMMENDED (new kernel or libraries). Do it when the runner is idle; this script never reboots."
  fi
}

script_path() {
  case "$1" in
    health|freshness|config-drift) echo "common/$1" ;;
    *) echo "runner/scripts/$1" ;;
  esac
}

update_host_tools() {
  local f u existed units_changed=0 cleanup_changed=0 isolation_changed=0
  local -a scripts=(health freshness config-drift runner-weekly-cleanup.sh runner-disk-guard.sh runner-engine-update.sh ci-job-isolation.sh)
  local -a units=(runner-weekly-cleanup.service runner-weekly-cleanup.timer runner-disk-guard.service runner-disk-guard.timer
                  runner-engine-update.service runner-engine-update.timer ci-job-isolation.service server-freshness.service server-freshness.timer)
  local -a new_timers=() changed_timers=()

  if [[ -f /etc/ci-prewarm.conf ]]; then
    scripts+=(ci-image-prewarm.sh)
    units+=(ci-image-prewarm.service ci-image-prewarm.timer)
  fi

  # health is shared with plain servers (common/); the other scripts belong to the runner host.
  command -v python3 >/dev/null || die "python3 is required for freshness checks"
  for f in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$f" == freshness ]]; then
      python3 -c 'import ast, sys; ast.parse(open(sys.argv[1]).read())' "${REPO_ROOT}/common/freshness" \
        || die "syntax error in freshness, nothing changed"
    else
      bash -n "${REPO_ROOT}/$(script_path "$f")" || die "syntax error in $(script_path "$f"), nothing changed"
    fi
  done

  printf '%s\n' "$REPO_ROOT" > "${WORK}/freshness-repo"
  if sync_file "${WORK}/freshness-repo" /etc/server-freshness/repo 0644; then
    CHANGED+=("freshness/repo")
  fi

  for f in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if sync_file "${REPO_ROOT}/$(script_path "$f")" "/usr/local/bin/${f}" 0755; then
      CHANGED+=("scripts/${f}")
      if [[ "$f" == runner-weekly-cleanup.sh ]]; then
        cleanup_changed=1
      fi
      if [[ "$f" == ci-job-isolation.sh ]]; then
        isolation_changed=1
      fi
    fi
  done

  for u in "${units[@]}"; do
    existed=0
    if [[ -f "/etc/systemd/system/${u}" ]]; then
      existed=1
    fi
    if sync_file "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/systemd/${u}" "/etc/systemd/system/${u}" 0644; then
      CHANGED+=("systemd/${u}")
      units_changed=1
      if [[ "$u" == *.timer ]]; then
        if (( existed )); then
          changed_timers+=("$u")
        else
          new_timers+=("$u")
        fi
      fi
    fi
  done

  # Kernel hardening and no core dumps (also written by the cloud-init files and by host-tools.sh).
  local ktmp kernel_changed=0
  ktmp=$(mktemp -d)
  printf '* hard core 0\n' > "${ktmp}/50-nocore.conf"
  printf '[Coredump]\nStorage=none\nProcessSizeMax=0\n' > "${ktmp}/50-off.conf"
  if sync_file "${REPO_ROOT}/common/sysctl-hardening.conf" /etc/sysctl.d/90-ci-hardening.conf 0644; then
    CHANGED+=("sysctl/90-ci-hardening.conf"); kernel_changed=1
  fi
  if sync_file "${ktmp}/50-nocore.conf" /etc/security/limits.d/50-nocore.conf 0644; then CHANGED+=("limits.d/50-nocore.conf"); fi
  if sync_file "${ktmp}/50-off.conf" /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/50-off.conf 0644; then CHANGED+=("coredump.conf.d/50-off.conf"); fi
  rm -rf "$ktmp"
  if (( kernel_changed )); then run sysctl --system >/dev/null; fi

  if (( units_changed )); then
    run systemctl daemon-reload
    for u in "${new_timers[@]}"; do
      run systemctl enable --now "$u"
    done
    for u in "${changed_timers[@]}"; do
      if (( DRYRUN )) || systemctl is-active --quiet "$u"; then
        run systemctl restart "$u"
      fi
    done
  fi

  # The isolation rules live in iptables: apply them when the script is new or changed and Docker is up.
  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl is-active --quiet docker 2>/dev/null; then
    if ! systemctl is-enabled --quiet ci-job-isolation.service 2>/dev/null; then
      run systemctl enable --now ci-job-isolation.service
    elif (( isolation_changed )); then
      run systemctl restart ci-job-isolation.service
    fi
  fi

  if (( cleanup_changed && ! DRYRUN )); then
    if ! DRY_RUN=1 /usr/local/bin/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh >/dev/null; then
      restore_files
      die "new runner-weekly-cleanup.sh fails its dry run, files restored"
    fi
  fi
  log "host tools: done"
}

update_monitoring() {
  local dir=/opt/monitoring stage="${WORK}/monitoring" prom_image zopt="" prom=0 graf=0 comp=0
  if [[ ! -f "${dir}/docker-compose.yml" ]]; then
    log "monitoring: not installed, skipping"
    return 0
  fi

  install -d -m 0755 "$stage"
  cp -a "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/monitoring/prometheus/." "${stage}/"
  if [[ -f /opt/registry-cache/docker-compose.yml ]] && ! grep -q 'job_name: registry-cache' "${stage}/prometheus.yml"; then
    cat >> "${stage}/prometheus.yml" <<'YAML'
  - job_name: registry-cache
    static_configs:
      - targets: ["127.0.0.1:5001"]
YAML
  fi
  if [[ -f /opt/logging/docker-compose.yml ]] && ! grep -q 'job_name: loki' "${stage}/prometheus.yml"; then
    prom_jobs_logging >> "${stage}/prometheus.yml"
  fi
  chmod -R a+rX "$stage"

  if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    jq empty "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/gitlab-runner.json" || die "invalid dashboard JSON, nothing changed"
  fi
  if selinux_on; then
    zopt=",z"
  fi
  prom_image=$(awk '/image: prom\/prometheus/ { print $2 }' "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/monitoring/docker-compose.yml")
  docker run --rm --entrypoint promtool -v "${stage}:/etc/prometheus:ro${zopt}" "$prom_image" \
    check config /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml || die "promtool rejected the new Prometheus config, nothing changed"

  # Grafana migrates its database forward on a new major and cannot go back: archive the data volume first (see runner/README.md).
  if (( DRYRUN )); then
    bash "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/install/monitoring-backup.sh" --dry-run || log "WARN: the Grafana backup check failed (dry run only, nothing changed)"
  else
    bash "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/install/monitoring-backup.sh" || die "monitoring: Grafana data backup failed, nothing changed"
  fi

  if sync_file "${stage}/prometheus.yml" "${dir}/prometheus/prometheus.yml" 0644 inplace; then
    prom=1
    CHANGED+=("monitoring/prometheus.yml")
  fi
  if sync_file "${stage}/alerts.yml" "${dir}/prometheus/alerts.yml" 0644 inplace; then
    prom=1
    CHANGED+=("monitoring/alerts.yml")
  fi
  if sync_tree "${REPO_ROOT}/runner/stacks/monitoring/grafana" "${dir}/grafana" 0644 inplace; then
    graf=1
    CHANGED+=("monitoring/grafana")
  fi
