bridge_ip() { docker network inspect bridge -f '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}' 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true; }

# start_pod REPO RUN_ID JOB_ID: network + JIT runner + sidecar + runner container. Any failure removes everything it created and backs off.
# Returns 2 when the pod network pool is full (nothing was created on GitHub's side).
start_pod() {
  local repo=$1 run_id=$2 job_id=$3 pod name dir body rid="" now bk_args=() sec_apparmor=() sec_label=() jit_file zopt="" rc npm_args=() err ip_cache
  now=$(date +%s)
  if command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled 2>/dev/null; then zopt=",Z"; fi   # private label for this pod's own directory
  pod="${now}-$(od -An -N3 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')"
  name="${NAME_PREFIX}${pod}"; dir=$(pod_dir "$pod")
  ensure_image "$GH_RUNNER_IMAGE" || { start_failed "" "$repo" "" image "$LAST_ERROR"; return 1; }
  if [[ "$GH_BUILDKIT" == 1 ]]; then ensure_image "$GH_BUILDKIT_IMAGE" || { start_failed "" "$repo" "" image "$LAST_ERROR"; return 1; }; fi
  install -d -m 0700 "$dir" && install -d -m 0755 "$dir/jit" && [[ "$(stat -c %a "$dir")" == 700 ]] || { start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "" directory; return 1; }
  local -a lab=(--label "${LABEL_JOB}=job" --label "${LABEL_POD}=${pod}" --label "${LABEL_REPO}=${repo}" --label "${LABEL_RUN}=${run_id}"
                --label "${LABEL_STARTED}=${now}" --label "io.server-init.github-runner.job-id=${job_id}")
  # The network comes first: with no free range nothing is created on GitHub's side and the job stays queued.
  rc=0; create_pod_network "$pod" "${lab[@]}" || rc=$?
  if (( rc == 2 )); then cleanup_pod "$pod"; return 2; fi
  if (( rc )); then start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "" network; return 1; fi
  if [[ "$GH_BUILDKIT" == 1 ]] && ! gen_tls "$dir"; then start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "" tls; return 1; fi
  body="${TMP}/jit-request.json"
  jq -n --arg name "$name" --argjson group "$((10#$GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID))" --argjson labels "$LABELS_JSON" \
    '{name: $name, runner_group_id: $group, labels: $labels, work_folder: "_work"}' > "$body" || { start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "" request; return 1; }
  api POST "/repos/${repo}/actions/runners/generate-jitconfig" "repo:${repo}" "$body"
  rm -f "$body"
  if [[ "$API_CODE" != 201 ]]; then
    if [[ "$API_CODE" == 422 ]]; then
      fail_api jit_failed "repo=${repo}" "hint=422: check GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID (now ${GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID}; 1 is assumed for repositories of a personal account) and GH_LABELS" || true
    else
      fail_api jit_failed "repo=${repo}" || true
    fi
    err="$(api_err)"; : > "$API_OUT"
    start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "" jit "$err"; return 1
  fi
  rid=$(jq -r '.runner.id // empty' "$API_OUT")
  jit_file="${dir}/jit/config"
  ( umask 077; jq -r '.encoded_jit_config // empty' "$API_OUT" > "$jit_file" )
  : > "$API_OUT"
  if [[ ! "$rid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ || ! -s "$jit_file" ]]; then
    start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "$rid" jit "answer without runner id or config"; return 1
  fi
  chmod 0644 "$jit_file"   # readable by the runner uid (and by the job itself, same uid); the 0700 parent keeps every other host user out

  if [[ "$GH_BUILDKIT" == 1 ]]; then
    # Rootless BuildKit (docs/rootless.md of moby/buildkit): seccomp and systempaths must be unconfined so runc can create user namespaces and
    # a /proc of its own; AppArmor only where it is active. SELinux (Rocky): container_t may not mount inside a user namespace, so the label is
    # disabled for this one container only. Not added, because they would break rootless BuildKit: --cap-drop ALL (the bounding set also
    # limits the capabilities in the new user namespace), no-new-privileges (newuidmap is setuid) and --read-only (it needs a writable
    # state volume). Limits that do not: CPU, memory without swap, process limit.
    if [[ -r /sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled && "$(cat /sys/module/apparmor/parameters/enabled 2>/dev/null)" == Y ]]; then sec_apparmor=(--security-opt apparmor=unconfined); fi
    if command -v selinuxenabled >/dev/null 2>&1 && selinuxenabled 2>/dev/null; then sec_label=(--security-opt label=disable); fi
    if ! err=$(docker run -d --rm --name "ghr-${pod}-buildkitd" --network "ghr-${pod}" --network-alias buildkitd "${lab[@]}" --label "${LABEL_ROLE}=buildkit" \
        --cgroup-parent ci-jobs.slice --cpus "$GH_BUILDKIT_CPUS" --memory "$GH_BUILDKIT_MEMORY" --memory-swap "$GH_BUILDKIT_MEMORY" --pids-limit "$GH_BUILDKIT_PIDS" \
        --security-opt seccomp=unconfined --security-opt systempaths=unconfined "${sec_apparmor[@]}" "${sec_label[@]}" \
        -v "${dir}/tls-srv:/certs:ro" "$GH_BUILDKIT_IMAGE" \
        --addr tcp://0.0.0.0:1234 --tlscacert /certs/ca.pem --tlscert /certs/cert.pem --tlskey /certs/key.pem 2>&1 >/dev/null); then
      start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "$rid" buildkit "$err"; return 1
    fi
    bk_args=(-v "${dir}/tls-cli:/etc/buildkit-tls:ro${zopt}" -e "BUILDKIT_HOST=tcp://buildkitd:1234")
  fi
  # The npm cache (runner/install/npm-cache.sh) listens on the docker0 IP; ci-job-isolation lets this pool, and only this pool of the br-
  # networks, reach that one port. Same values the GitLab jobs get from config.toml.
  if [[ -f "${GHR_NPM_DIR:-/opt/npm-cache}/docker-compose.yml" ]]; then
    ip_cache=$(bridge_ip)
    if [[ "$ip_cache" =~ ^([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$ ]]; then
      npm_args=(-e "NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY=http://${ip_cache}:4873/" -e "YARN_NPM_REGISTRY_SERVER=http://${ip_cache}:4873/" -e "YARN_UNSAFE_HTTP_WHITELIST=${ip_cache}")
    else
      say warn npm_cache_unavailable "hint=/opt/npm-cache exists but the docker0 address is unknown; jobs use the public registry"
    fi
  fi
  # The entry reads the JIT config from the read-only file and hands it to the Listener as an environment variable of that process only
  # (not in docker inspect, not in the host's process list). It runs Runner.Listener itself instead of run.sh: run.sh restarts the Listener
  # on exit codes 2, 3 and 4 inside the container and turns every other code into 0, so Docker would never see why a runner ended.
  # GH_JIT_PASS=arg is a debugging fallback: --jitconfig on the command line shows the config in /proc/<pid>/cmdline.
  local entry='set -eu; J=$(cat /run/ghr-jit/config); [ -n "$J" ] || exit 1; [ ! -f ./.env ] || { set -a; . ./.env; set +a; }; if [ "${GHR_JIT_PASS:-env}" = arg ]; then exec ./bin/Runner.Listener run --jitconfig "$J"; fi; ACTIONS_RUNNER_INPUT_JITCONFIG=$J; export ACTIONS_RUNNER_INPUT_JITCONFIG; unset J; exec ./bin/Runner.Listener run'
  # Not --rm: the exit code of the Listener is read from the stopped container, which the controller removes.
  if ! err=$(docker run -d --init --name "ghr-${pod}-runner" --network "ghr-${pod}" "${lab[@]}" --label "${LABEL_ROLE}=runner" --label "${LABEL_RID}=${rid}" \
      --cgroup-parent ci-jobs.slice --cpus "$GH_JOB_CPUS" --memory "$GH_JOB_MEMORY" --memory-swap "$GH_JOB_MEMORY" --pids-limit "$GH_JOB_PIDS" --shm-size "$GH_JOB_SHM" \
      --user 1001:1001 --security-opt no-new-privileges --cap-drop ALL \
      -v "${dir}/jit:/run/ghr-jit:ro${zopt}" "${bk_args[@]}" -w /home/runner \
      -e "GHR_JIT_PASS=${GH_JIT_PASS}" -e ACTIONS_RUNNER_PRINT_LOG_TO_STDOUT=1 "${npm_args[@]}" \
      "$GH_RUNNER_IMAGE" sh -c "$entry" ghr-entry 2>&1 >/dev/null); then
    start_failed "$pod" "$repo" "$rid" runner "$err"; return 1
  fi
  START_FAIL=0
  say info pod_started "pod=${pod}" "repo=${repo}" "run=${run_id}" "job=${job_id}" "runner=${rid}" "subnet=${POD_SUBNET}" "buildkit=${GH_BUILDKIT}" "npm_cache=$([[ ${#npm_args[@]} -gt 0 ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "cpus=${GH_JOB_CPUS}" "memory=${GH_JOB_MEMORY}"
}

# ---- discovery ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# queued_jobs REPO: fills FOUND with "run_id job_id" for each queued job that asks only for our labels, including a custom one.
# This only decides whether a pod is started: an idle runner takes any queued job of its repository (see check_assigned_job).
FOUND=()
queued_jobs() {
  local repo=$1 st run runs line
  FOUND=()
  for st in queued in_progress; do
    if ! get_paged "/repos/${repo}/actions/runs?status=${st}" workflow_runs 50 6; then
      if [[ "$API_CODE" == 403 || "$API_CODE" == 404 ]]; then say warn runs_denied "repo=${repo}" "hint=the App needs Actions: read on this repository"; return 0; fi
      fail_api run_list_failed "repo=${repo}" || true; continue
    fi
    if (( PAGED_TRUNCATED )); then say warn runs_truncated "repo=${repo}" "status=${st}" "hint=more than 300 runs; the oldest are looked at first on the next polls only if these finish"; fi
    # A fork pull request would run code of someone else on this host: no pod is started for it unless GH_ALLOW_FORK_RUNS=1.
    runs=$(jq -r --argjson fork "$GH_ALLOW_FORK_RUNS" '.workflow_runs[]? |
      select($fork == 1 or ((.event // "") | startswith("pull_request") | not) or ((.head_repository.full_name // "") == (.repository.full_name // "x"))) | .id' "$PAGED_FILE")
    for run in $runs; do
      [[ "$run" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
      if ! get_paged "/repos/${repo}/actions/runs/${run}/jobs?filter=latest" jobs 100 5; then
        if [[ "$API_CODE" != 403 && "$API_CODE" != 404 ]]; then fail_api job_list_failed "repo=${repo}" "run=${run}" || true; fi
        continue
      fi
      if (( PAGED_TRUNCATED )); then say warn jobs_truncated "repo=${repo}" "run=${run}" "hint=more than 500 jobs in one run"; fi
      while IFS= read -r line; do
        [[ -n "$line" ]] && FOUND+=("$line")
      done < <(jq -r --argjson ours "$LABELS_LC" --argjson custom "$CUSTOM_LC" --arg run "$run" '.jobs[]? |
        select(.status == "queued" and .runner_id == null) |
        ([.labels[]? | ascii_downcase]) as $l |
        select(($l | length) > 0 and (($l - $ours) | length) == 0 and (($l | map(select(. as $x | $custom | index($x))) | length) > 0)) |
        "\($run) \(.id)"' "$PAGED_FILE")
    done
  done
}

discover() {
  local repo run job n need rc
  if (( ACTIVE >= MAX_JOBS )); then return 0; fi
  if (( $(date +%s) < BACKOFF_UNTIL )); then say info discovery_paused "reason=backoff" "until=${BACKOFF_UNTIL}"; return 0; fi
  if [[ "$RATE_REMAINING" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( RATE_REMAINING < RATE_STOP )); then
    LAST_ERROR="GitHub API quota nearly used up (${RATE_REMAINING} left)"; say error discovery_paused "reason=rate_limit" "remaining=${RATE_REMAINING}"; return 0
  fi
  for repo in "${SERVED[@]}"; do
    (( ACTIVE < MAX_JOBS )) || break
    queued_jobs "$repo"
    n=${#FOUND[@]}; need=$(( n - ${IDLE_BY_REPO[$repo]:-0} ))
    if (( n > 0 )); then say info jobs_queued "repo=${repo}" "queued=${n}" "idle_runners=${IDLE_BY_REPO[$repo]:-0}"; fi
    for job in "${FOUND[@]}"; do
      (( need > 0 && ACTIVE < MAX_JOBS )) || break
      run=${job% *}; job=${job#* }
      rc=0; start_pod "$repo" "$run" "$job" || rc=$?
      if (( rc == 0 )); then
        ACTIVE=$((ACTIVE + 1)); IDLE=$((IDLE + 1)); IDLE_BY_REPO[$repo]=$(( ${IDLE_BY_REPO[$repo]:-0} + 1 )); need=$((need - 1))
      elif (( rc == 2 )); then
        return 0   # no free pod network: the jobs stay queued, the next poll retries
      else
        return 0   # a failed start backs off for all repositories; the next poll after the pause retries
      fi
    done
  done
}

# ---- status for health ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
LAST_POLL_OK=0 STARTED_AT=0
write_status() {
  local tmp="${STATE_DIR}/status.json.new"
  jq -n --argjson updated "$(date +%s)" --argjson started "$STARTED_AT" --argjson poll "$LAST_POLL_OK" --argjson tok "$LAST_TOKEN_OK" \
    --arg err "$LAST_ERROR" --arg rem "$RATE_REMAINING" --arg lim "$RATE_LIMIT" --arg rst "$RATE_RESET" \
    --argjson served "${#SERVED[@]}" --argjson skipped "${#SKIPPED[@]}" --argjson active "$ACTIVE" --argjson idle "$IDLE" --argjson max "$MAX_JOBS" \
    --argjson upd "$UPDATE_REQUIRED" --argjson fails "$CONSEC_FAIL" --argjson backoff "$BACKOFF_UNTIL" --arg img "$IMAGE_CREATED" --arg inst "$INSTALL_ID" \
    '{version: 1, updated: $updated, started: $started, last_poll_ok: $poll, last_token_ok: $tok,
      last_error: (if $err == "" then null else $err end),
      rate_remaining: ($rem | tonumber? // null), rate_limit: ($lim | tonumber? // null), rate_reset: ($rst | tonumber? // null),
      served: $served, skipped: $skipped, active_pods: $active, idle_pods: $idle, max_jobs: $max,
      update_required: ($upd == 1), consecutive_failures: $fails, backoff_until: $backoff,
      runner_image_created: ($img | tonumber? // null), installation: $inst}' > "$tmp"
  chmod 0644 "$tmp"; mv -f "$tmp" "${STATE_DIR}/status.json"
}

TICK=0
SWEEP_EVERY=10
tick() {
  local now ok=1
  TICK=$((TICK + 1)); now=$(date +%s)
  LAST_ERROR=""
  if (( now < PAUSE_UNTIL )); then
    # GitHub asked us to wait: no request, but pods are still finished, cleaned up and limited by their runtime (Docker only)
    say warn poll_paused "seconds=$((PAUSE_UNTIL - now))" "reason=rate_limit"
    API_OFF=1; manage_pods 0 || say error docker_unreachable "hint=docker ps or docker network ls failed"; API_OFF=0
    LAST_ERROR="paused by GitHub's rate limit"; save_state; write_status; return 0
  fi
  if ensure_token && list_repos; then
    if [[ "$RATE_REMAINING" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( RATE_REMAINING < RATE_LOW )) && (( TICK % 20 == 1 || RATE_REMAINING < RATE_STOP )); then
      say warn rate_limit_low "remaining=${RATE_REMAINING}" "limit=${RATE_LIMIT:-?}"
    fi
  else
    ok=0
  fi
  # Finish and clean up pods first (this needs only Docker, so it runs even when GitHub does not answer); then, every SWEEP_EVERY polls,
  # at the start and whenever the repository list changed, delete runners that must not exist; then look for work.
  if ! manage_pods; then
    # not "no pods": nothing is cleaned up, swept or started on a poll where docker does not answer
    LAST_ERROR="docker does not answer (docker ps or docker network ls failed)"; say error docker_unreachable "hint=is docker running and is ${USER:-this user} in the docker group?"; ok=0
  fi
  if (( ok )); then
    if (( TICK == 1 || REPOS_CHANGED || TICK % SWEEP_EVERY == 0 )); then sweep_runners; fi
    say info poll "served=${#SERVED[@]}" "skipped=${#SKIPPED[@]}" "active=${ACTIVE}" "remaining=${RATE_REMAINING:-?}"
    discover
    [[ -z "$LAST_ERROR" ]] || ok=0
  fi
  if (( ok )); then LAST_POLL_OK=$(date +%s); fi
  save_state; write_status
  (( ok ))
}

# ---- modes ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# init_dirs: the state directory, its private parts (jobs/ holds the per-pod secrets, so it must be 0700 and ours) and the lock that
# keeps the service and a manual run from working on the same pods at once.
init_dirs() {
  install -d -m 0755 "$STATE_DIR"
  JOBS="${STATE_DIR}/jobs"; CACHE="${STATE_DIR}/cache"; TMP="${STATE_DIR}/tmp"
  install -d -m 0700 "$JOBS" "$CACHE"
  if [[ "$(stat -c '%a:%u' "$JOBS")" != "700:$(id -u)" ]]; then
    say error jobs_dir_unsafe "dir=${JOBS}" "found=$(stat -c '%a:%U' "$JOBS")" "hint=it holds the secrets of the pods: it must be mode 700 and owned by the user that runs the controller"; exit 1
  fi
  exec 8>"${STATE_DIR}/ctl.lock"
  flock -n 8 || { say error already_running "lock=${STATE_DIR}/ctl.lock" "hint=github-runner-ctl is already running (the service?); stop it before a manual run"; exit 1; }
  rm -rf -- "$TMP"; install -d -m 0700 "$TMP"
  API_OUT="${TMP}/api.body"; API_HDR="${TMP}/api.hdr"
}

preflight() {
  local t
  for t in curl jq openssl docker sha1sum flock; do command -v "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { say error missing_tool "tool=${t}"; return 1; }; done
  docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { say error docker_unreachable "hint=is the service user in the docker group and is docker running?"; return 1; }
  [[ -r "$GH_KEY_FILE" ]] || { say error key_missing "key=${GH_KEY_FILE}"; return 1; }
}

common_start() {
  load_config
  validate_config || { local e; for e in "${CFG_ERRORS[@]}"; do say error config_invalid "problem=${e}"; done; exit 2; }
  derive_config
}

run_loop() {
  local stop=0 sleeper=0 rc
  common_start
  init_dirs
  preflight || exit 1
  STARTED_AT=$(date +%s)
  load_state
  trap 'stop=1; [[ $sleeper -gt 0 ]] && kill "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null; true' TERM INT
  say info started "owner=${GH_OWNER}" "labels=${GH_LABELS}" "max_jobs=${MAX_JOBS}" "poll=${POLL}s" "buildkit=${GH_BUILDKIT}" "name_prefix=${NAME_PREFIX}"
  ensure_image "$GH_RUNNER_IMAGE" || true
  while (( ! stop )); do
    rc=0; tick || rc=$?
    (( rc == 0 )) || say warn poll_failed "error=${LAST_ERROR:-unknown}"
    (( stop )) && break
    sleep "$(( POLL + RANDOM % 4 ))" 8>&- & sleeper=$!
    wait "$sleeper" 2>/dev/null || true
    sleeper=0
  done
  say info stopping "note=running pods keep running; the next start adopts them"
}

once() {
  common_start
  init_dirs
  preflight || exit 1
  STARTED_AT=$(date +%s)
  load_state
  tick
}

# self_test: read-only against GitHub (no runner is created, no container started).
self_test() {
  local rc=0 perms name slug k want have
  common_start
  STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ghr-selftest.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -rf -- "$STATE_DIR"' EXIT
  JOBS="${STATE_DIR}/jobs"; CACHE="${STATE_DIR}/cache"; TMP="${STATE_DIR}/tmp"; install -d -m 0700 "$JOBS" "$CACHE" "$TMP"
  API_OUT="${TMP}/api.body"; API_HDR="${TMP}/api.hdr"
  for k in curl jq openssl; do command -v "$k" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL  ${k} is not installed"; return 1; }; done
  echo "config:  ${CONFIG}: valid (owner ${GH_OWNER}, labels ${GH_LABELS}, max ${MAX_JOBS} job(s), runner group ${GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID})"
  if openssl pkey -in "$GH_KEY_FILE" -noout >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "OK    key ${GH_KEY_FILE} parses"; else echo "FAIL  key ${GH_KEY_FILE} is missing, unreadable or not a private key"; return 1; fi
  make_jwt || { echo "FAIL  cannot sign a JWT with the key"; return 1; }
  echo "OK    JWT signed (RS256, iss ${GH_APP_CLIENT_ID})"
  api GET /app jwt
  if [[ "$API_CODE" == 200 ]]; then
    name=$(jq -r '.name // "?"' "$API_OUT"); slug=$(jq -r '.slug // "?"' "$API_OUT")
    echo "OK    GitHub App: ${name} (${slug})"
    for k in administration:write actions:read metadata:read; do
      want=${k#*:}; have=$(jq -r --arg p "${k%%:*}" '.permissions[$p] // "none"' "$API_OUT")
      if [[ "$have" == write || "$have" == "$want" ]]; then echo "OK    permission ${k%%:*}: ${have}"; else echo "FAIL  permission ${k%%:*}: ${have} (needs ${want})"; rc=1; fi
    done
    perms=$(jq -r '(.events // []) | join(",")' "$API_OUT"); echo "info  subscribed webhook events: ${perms:-none} (none is right: this controller polls)"
  else
    echo "FAIL  GET /app: $(api_err) (wrong GH_APP_CLIENT_ID or key?)"; return 1
  fi
  ensure_token || { echo "FAIL  no installation token: ${LAST_ERROR}"; return 1; }
  echo "OK    installation ${INSTALL_ID}: token minted"
  list_repos || { echo "FAIL  cannot list repositories: ${LAST_ERROR}"; return 1; }
  echo "repositories of the installation (${#ALL_REPOS[@]}):"
  local r
  for r in "${SERVED[@]}"; do echo "  SERVE  ${r} (private)"; done
  for r in "${SKIPPED[@]}"; do echo "  SKIP   ${r%% *} (${r#* })"; done
  (( ${#SERVED[@]} > 0 )) || { echo "WARN  no private repository would be served (is the App installed on All repositories?)"; rc=1; }
  if (( ${#SERVED[@]} > 0 )); then
    # the permission that creates and deletes runners, with a token of one repository only (what the controller uses)
    if ensure_repo_token "${SERVED[0]}"; then
      api GET "/repos/${SERVED[0]}/actions/runners?per_page=100" "repo:${SERVED[0]}"
      if [[ "$API_CODE" == 200 ]]; then echo "OK    Administration token for ${SERVED[0]} alone can list its runners"
      else echo "FAIL  listing runners of ${SERVED[0]}: $(api_err)"; rc=1; fi
    else
      echo "FAIL  no Administration token for ${SERVED[0]}: ${LAST_ERROR}"; rc=1
    fi
  fi
  echo "info  API quota: ${RATE_REMAINING:-?} of ${RATE_LIMIT:-?} left"
  echo "info  not tested here: runner group ${GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID} for JIT runners (checked on the first job; a 422 names GH_RUNNER_GROUP_ID in the log)"
  return "$rc"
}

main() {
  case "${1:-run}" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    run) run_loop ;;
    once) once ;;
    check-config) common_start; echo "config OK: ${CONFIG}" ;;
    self-test|--self-test) self_test ;;
    *) usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
}

if [[ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" == "$0" ]]; then
  main "$@"
fi
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/scripts/github-runner-ctl"

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/runner-disk-guard.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Emergency cleanup when the root filesystem crosses HARD_LIMIT percent.
set -Eeuo pipefail
HARD_LIMIT="${HARD_LIMIT:-85}"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  (env: HARD_LIMIT=85) runs runner-weekly-cleanup.sh with RETENTION_DAYS=1 when disk usage >= HARD_LIMIT%"
  exit 0
fi
used=$(df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
if (( used >= HARD_LIMIT )); then
  logger -t runner-disk-guard -- "disk ${used}% >= ${HARD_LIMIT}%, running emergency cleanup"
  RETENTION_DAYS=1 /usr/local/bin/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh
fi
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/runner-disk-guard.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/runner-engine-update.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Weekly upgrade of Docker CE and GitLab Runner while no CI job runs (GitLab jobs, GitHub runner pods): runner and github-runner-ctl
# stopped gracefully, jobs checked again, Docker upgraded and restarted, gitlab-runner last; a job in between: all started again.
# One result line in /var/log/runner-engine-update.log. Env: DRY_RUN=1 plan only; STOP_WAIT seconds for the graceful stop (1800).
set -Eeuo pipefail
LOG="${ENGINE_UPDATE_LOG:-/var/log/runner-engine-update.log}"   # overridable for tests
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
STOP_WAIT="${STOP_WAIT:-1800}"
DROPIN="${ENGINE_UPDATE_DROPIN:-/etc/systemd/system/gitlab-runner.service.d/graceful-stop.conf}"
PKGS=(docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin gitlab-runner)
note() { logger -t runner-engine-update -- "$*" 2>/dev/null || true; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 [--dry-run]   upgrades ${PKGS[*]} when no CI job runs"
  exit 0
fi
[[ "${1:-}" == "--dry-run" ]] && DRY_RUN=1
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
exec 9>/run/runner-engine-update.lock
flock -n 9 || { note "SKIP another update is running"; exit 0; }
# A docker error is not "no jobs".
job_ids() { docker ps -q --filter "label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true" && docker ps -q --filter "label=io.server-init.github-runner=job"; }
if ! jobs=$(job_ids 2>/dev/null); then
  note "SKIP docker does not answer, cannot tell whether jobs run"
  exit 0
fi
if [[ -n "$jobs" ]]; then
  note "SKIP $(wc -w <<<"$jobs") CI job(s) running, will retry next week"
  exit 0
fi
installed=()
if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do rpm -q "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && installed+=("$p"); done
  upgrade() { dnf -y -q upgrade "$@"; }
  pending() { dnf -q check-update "${installed[@]}" >/dev/null 2>&1; [[ $? -eq 100 ]]; }
elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do dpkg -s "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 && installed+=("$p"); done
  upgrade() { DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q --only-upgrade "$@"; }
  pending() { apt-get update -q >/dev/null 2>&1; apt-get -s install --only-upgrade "${installed[@]}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^Inst '; }
else
  note "FAIL no supported package manager"
  exit 1
fi
(( ${#installed[@]} )) || { note "SKIP none of the packages is installed"; exit 0; }
if ! pending; then
  note "OK nothing to upgrade (${installed[*]})"
  exit 0
fi
docker_pkgs=(); runner_pkgs=()
for p in "${installed[@]}"; do if [[ "$p" == gitlab-runner ]]; then runner_pkgs+=("$p"); else docker_pkgs+=("$p"); fi; done
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == 1 ]]; then
  note "DRY-RUN would upgrade ${installed[*]}"
  exit 0
fi
before=$(for p in "${installed[@]}"; do if command -v rpm >/dev/null 2>&1; then rpm -q --qf '%{NAME}-%{VERSION}-%{RELEASE} ' "$p"; else dpkg-query -W -f='${Package}-${Version} ' "$p"; fi; done)
# From here whatever happens: start the runner again.
runner_stopped=0 ctl_stopped=0
ctl_back() { if (( ctl_stopped )); then systemctl start --no-block github-runner-ctl >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; }
runner_back() { systemctl start --no-block gitlab-runner >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; ctl_back; }
trap '[[ $runner_stopped -eq 1 ]] && runner_back' EXIT
runner_state() { systemctl show -p ActiveState --value gitlab-runner 2>/dev/null || echo unknown; }
# SIGQUIT = graceful stop (jobs finish). Returns 1 when still running after STOP_WAIT.
stop_runner_wait() {
  local waited=0 st
  systemctl stop --no-block gitlab-runner
  while :; do
    st=$(runner_state)
    [[ "$st" == inactive || "$st" == failed ]] && return 0
    (( waited >= STOP_WAIT )) && return 1
    sleep 5
    waited=$((waited + 5))
  done
}
no_jobs() { local j; j=$(job_ids 2>/dev/null) && [[ -z "$j" ]]; }
# SIGTERM would end jobs; TimeoutStopSec=infinity: systemd never SIGKILLs the runner.
if ! grep -qs '^KillSignal=SIGQUIT' "$DROPIN" 2>/dev/null || ! grep -qs '^TimeoutStopSec=infinity' "$DROPIN" 2>/dev/null; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$DROPIN")"
  printf '[Service]\nKillSignal=SIGQUIT\nTimeoutStopSec=infinity\n' > "$DROPIN"
  systemctl daemon-reload
fi
runner_stopped=1
# no new GitHub pod during the upgrade
if systemctl is-active --quiet github-runner-ctl 2>/dev/null; then systemctl stop github-runner-ctl && ctl_stopped=1; fi
if ! stop_runner_wait; then
  note "SKIP gitlab-runner did not stop within ${STOP_WAIT}s (jobs still running), will retry next week"
  exit 0
fi
if ! no_jobs; then
  note "SKIP a CI job appeared or docker does not answer after the runner stopped; will retry next week"
  exit 0
fi
if (( ${#docker_pkgs[@]} )) && ! upgrade "${docker_pkgs[@]}" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
  note "FAIL Docker package upgrade failed, see ${LOG}"
  exit 1
fi
# a package scriptlet may have started the runner and it may have taken a job
if [[ "$(runner_state)" != inactive ]]; then
  if ! stop_runner_wait; then
    note "SKIP Docker packages upgraded, but gitlab-runner is busy again; Docker not restarted (retry next week)"
    exit 0
  fi
fi
if ! no_jobs; then
  note "SKIP Docker packages upgraded, but a CI job runs or docker does not answer; Docker not restarted (retry next week)"
  exit 0
fi
bad=""
if (( ${#docker_pkgs[@]} )); then
  systemctl restart docker
  sleep 5
  # reapply the isolation rules
  if systemctl cat ci-job-isolation.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then systemctl restart ci-job-isolation.service || bad+=" ci-job-isolation"; fi
fi
if (( ${#runner_pkgs[@]} )) && ! upgrade "${runner_pkgs[@]}" >>"$LOG" 2>&1; then
  note "FAIL gitlab-runner upgrade failed, see ${LOG}"
  exit 1
fi
systemctl start gitlab-runner || true
runner_stopped=0
ctl_back
sleep 5
for s in docker gitlab-runner; do systemctl is-active --quiet "$s" || bad+=" $s"; done
if [[ -n "$bad" ]]; then
  note "FAIL not active after the upgrade:${bad}; was: ${before}"
  exit 1
fi
note "OK upgraded ${installed[*]}; was: ${before}"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/runner-engine-update.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/scripts"
cat > "$R/runner/scripts/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Weekly cleanup of the GitLab Runner host: Docker, runner caches, packages, logs, temp files.
set -Eeuo pipefail
RETENTION_DAYS="${RETENTION_DAYS:-7}"
JOURNAL_MAX="${JOURNAL_MAX:-500M}"
SHARED_CACHE_DIR="${SHARED_CACHE_DIR:-/srv/ci-cache}"
SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS="${SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS:-14}"
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
CACHE_DIRS=(/home/gitlab-runner/cache /home/gitlab-runner/.cache /var/lib/gitlab-runner/cache /root/.cache)
BUILD_DIRS=(/home/gitlab-runner/builds /var/lib/gitlab-runner/builds)
log()  { logger -t runner-weekly-cleanup -- "$*"; echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*"; }
disk() { df --output=used,avail,pcent -h / | tail -1 | xargs; }
run() {
  log "-> $*"
  [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]] && return 0
  "$@" || log "WARN: failed: $*"
}
wipe_dir() {
  local dir="$1" age="${2:-}"
  [[ -d "$dir" ]] || return 0
  if [[ -n "$age" ]]; then
    log "-> cleaning $dir older than ${age}d"
    [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]] && return 0
    find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -mtime +"$age" -delete 2>/dev/null || log "WARN: partial cleanup of $dir"
  else
    log "-> wiping $dir"
    [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]] && return 0
    find "$dir" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || log "WARN: partial wipe of $dir"
  fi
}
usage() {
  cat <<USAGE
Usage: $0 [--dry-run] [--help]
  --dry-run                   same as DRY_RUN=1: show what would be cleaned without deleting anything
Env:
  RETENTION_DAYS              keep images, builds and temp files newer than N days (default: 7)
  JOURNAL_MAX                 max systemd journal size (default: 500M)
  SHARED_CACHE_DIR            shared CI cache directory (default: /srv/ci-cache)
  SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS   prune shared cache files not accessed for N days (default: 14)
  DRY_RUN=1                   show what would be cleaned without deleting anything
USAGE
}
while (( $# )); do
  case "$1" in
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    -n|--dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    *) usage >&2; echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[[ $EUID -eq 0 ]] || { echo "run as root" >&2; exit 1; }
exec 9>/run/runner-weekly-cleanup.lock
flock -n 9 || { log "another cleanup is running, exit"; exit 0; }
hours=$(( RETENTION_DAYS * 24 ))
log "start (dry_run=${DRY_RUN}), disk before: $(disk)"
if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # docker not answering is not "no jobs"; stderr is kept apart so a warning is not counted as a job
  ps_err=$(mktemp)
  trap 'rm -f "$ps_err"' EXIT
  if ! job_ids=$({ docker ps -q --filter "label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true" && docker ps -q --filter "label=io.server-init.github-runner=job"; } 2>"$ps_err"); then
    log "ERROR: docker is not responding, cleanup skipped: $(cat "$ps_err")"
    exit 1
  fi
  running=$(wc -w <<<"$job_ids")
  if (( running > 0 )); then
    log "WARN: ${running} job container(s) running, skipping cache wipe"
  else
    run /usr/share/gitlab-runner/clear-docker-cache prune-volumes
    if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]]; then
      docker volume ls -q --filter name=runner- | xargs -r docker volume rm >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: some runner volumes in use"
    fi
    for dir in "${CACHE_DIRS[@]}"; do wipe_dir "$dir"; done
  fi
  run docker container prune -f --filter "until=${hours}h"
  run docker image prune -af --filter "until=${hours}h"
  # the prune takes the pinned GitHub runner images too: fetch them again
  for img in $(sed -n 's/^GH_\(RUNNER\|BUILDKIT\)_IMAGE=//p' "${GHR_CONFIG:-/etc/github-runner/config.env}" 2>/dev/null); do
    docker image inspect "$img" >/dev/null 2>&1 || run docker pull -q "$img"
  done
  run docker builder prune -af --filter "until=${hours}h"
  run docker network prune -f --filter "until=${hours}h"
fi
for dir in "${BUILD_DIRS[@]}"; do wipe_dir "$dir" "$RETENTION_DAYS"; done
if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 autoremove --purge -y -q
  run apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 autoclean -q
  run apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=600 clean -q
elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  run dnf -y -q autoremove
  run dnf -q clean all
fi
run journalctl --vacuum-time="$(( RETENTION_DAYS * 2 ))d" --vacuum-size="$JOURNAL_MAX"
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]]; then
  log "-> removing rotated logs older than 30d"
  find /var/log -type f \( -name '*.gz' -o -name '*-[0-9]*' -o -name '*.[0-9]' -o -name '*.old' \) -mtime +30 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  find /tmp /var/tmp -xdev -mindepth 1 -type f -atime +"$RETENTION_DAYS" -delete 2>/dev/null || true
fi
run systemd-tmpfiles --clean
if [[ -d "$SHARED_CACHE_DIR" && "$DRY_RUN" != "1" ]]; then
  log "-> pruning ${SHARED_CACHE_DIR} files not used for ${SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS}d"
  find "$SHARED_CACHE_DIR" -xdev -type f -atime +"$SHARED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_DAYS" -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  find "$SHARED_CACHE_DIR" -xdev -mindepth 2 -type d -empty -delete 2>/dev/null || true
fi
log "done, disk after: $(disk)"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/runner/scripts/runner-weekly-cleanup.sh"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/logging"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/logging/config.alloy" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
// Container logs and the systemd journal to the local Loki.
// CI job containers are skipped: their output is already the job log in GitLab (or in GitHub, for the pods of the GitHub Actions runner).

logging {
  level = "warn"
}

loki.write "local" {
  endpoint {
    url = "http://127.0.0.1:3100/loki/api/v1/push"
  }
}

discovery.docker "containers" {
  host             = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
  refresh_interval = "15s"
}

discovery.relabel "containers" {
  targets = []

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_gitlab_gitlab_runner_managed"]
    regex         = "true"
    action        = "drop"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_io_server_init_github_runner"]
    regex         = "job"
    action        = "drop"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_name"]
    regex         = "/(.*)"
    target_label  = "container"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_project"]
    target_label  = "compose_project"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_service"]
    target_label  = "compose_service"
  }
}

loki.source.docker "containers" {
  host          = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
  targets       = discovery.docker.containers.targets
  labels        = {source = "docker"}
  relabel_rules = discovery.relabel.containers.rules
  forward_to    = [loki.write.local.receiver]
}

loki.relabel "journal" {
  forward_to = []

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__journal__systemd_unit"]
    target_label  = "unit"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__journal_priority_keyword"]
    target_label  = "level"
  }

  rule {
    source_labels = ["__journal_syslog_identifier"]
    target_label  = "identifier"
  }
}

loki.source.journal "system" {
  path          = "/var/log/journal"
  max_age       = "12h"
  labels        = {source = "journal"}
  relabel_rules = loki.relabel.journal.rules
  forward_to    = [loki.write.local.receiver]
}
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/logging/config.alloy"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/logging"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/logging/docker-compose.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
name: logging

services:
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.7.9
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 512m
    command: ["-config.file=/etc/loki/config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./loki.yaml:/etc/loki/config.yaml:ro
      - loki-data:/loki

  # Runs as the monitoring service user. Docker socket and journal access come from group_add
  # (docker and systemd-journal); note that reading the Docker socket is root-equivalent on the host.
  # The journal group is added by docker-compose.override.yml, which stack_ids (common/lib.sh) writes
  # only when its gid differs from the docker gid: compose rejects a group_add list with equal items.
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.21.3
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 256m
    user: "${MON_UID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}:${MON_GID:?run runner/install/users.sh first}"
    group_add:
      - "${DOCKER_GID:?run runner/install/logging.sh}"
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt:
      - label=disable
      - no-new-privileges:true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=127.0.0.1:12345
      - --storage.path=/data
      - --disable-reporting
      - /config/config.alloy
    volumes:
      - ./config.alloy:/config/config.alloy:ro
      - alloy-data:/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log/journal:/var/log/journal:ro
      - /etc/machine-id:/etc/machine-id:ro
    depends_on: [loki]

volumes:
  loki-data:
  alloy-data:
__SIC_EOF__

# Copied to /opt/monitoring/.env by runner/install/monitoring.sh; the password is generated there.
# On a first install the installer also appends GF_SECURITY_SECRET_KEY (random, 40 characters). Grafana encrypts stored credentials

# change it on an install that already has data: what was encrypted under the old key becomes unreadable. Keep the key with every
# backup archive (runner/README.md, "Grafana upgrade and rollback").

GF_SERVER_HTTP_PORT=3000

# Verdaccio 7. The server secret is not a setting here: 7.x reads it only from data/.verdaccio-db.json in the storage and
# accepts exactly 32 characters. The start script in docker-compose.yml creates it (mode 600) and moves older storage aside.
storage: /verdaccio/storage/data
plugins: /verdaccio/plugins

listen:
  - 172.17.0.1:4873

auth:
  htpasswd:
    file: /verdaccio/storage/htpasswd
    max_users: -1

uplinks:
  npmjs:
    url: https://registry.npmjs.org/
    timeout: 60s
    maxage: 30m
    cache: true

packages:
  '@*/*':
    access: $all
    publish: $authenticated
    proxy: npmjs
  '**':
    access: $all
    publish: $authenticated
    proxy: npmjs

server:
  keepAliveTimeout: 60

web:
  enable: false

log:
  type: stdout
  format: pretty
  level: warn
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/config.yaml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/docker-compose.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
name: npm-cache

services:
  verdaccio:
    image: verdaccio/verdaccio:7.0.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 1g
    # The image's default command passes --listen 0.0.0.0:4873, which overrides "listen:" in config.yaml
    # and exposes the cache (access: $all) on every interface. runner/install/npm-cache.sh and update.sh
    # replace 172.17.0.1 below with the docker0 IP, as they do in config.yaml.
    # npm-cache-start.sh (the config below) runs first and then execs verdaccio.
    command: ["sh", "/usr/local/bin/npm-cache-start.sh", "verdaccio", "--config", "/verdaccio/conf/config.yaml", "--listen", "http://172.17.0.1:4873"]
    configs:
      - source: start
        target: /usr/local/bin/npm-cache-start.sh
    volumes:
      - ./config.yaml:/verdaccio/conf/config.yaml:ro
      - verdaccio-storage:/verdaccio/storage

# Runs on every start, so it also covers update.sh, which only syncs this file and config.yaml. In "content:" a literal
# dollar sign is written $$ (compose would interpolate a single one). Inline "content:" needs Docker Compose >= 2.23.1
# (npm-cache.sh and update.sh check it first).
configs:
  start:
    content: |
      set -eu
      S=/verdaccio/storage
      DB=$$S/data/.verdaccio-db.json
      STATE=$$S/.deployed-major
      WANT=7
      say() { echo "npm-cache: $$*" >&2; }
      # live storage = everything except the state file and earlier backups
      live() { for e in "$$S"/* "$$S"/.[!.]*; do [ -e "$$e" ] || continue; case $${e##*/} in backup-*|.deployed-major) ;; *) echo "$$e" ;; esac; done; }
      have=$$(cat "$$STATE" 2>/dev/null || true)
      if [ -z "$$have" ]; then
        if [ -n "$$(live)" ]; then have=6; say "no $$STATE but storage exists: treating it as 6.x"; else have=none; fi
      fi
      if [ "$$have" != "$$WANT" ] && [ -n "$$(live)" ]; then
        B=$$S/backup-$$have.x-$$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
        say "storage of $$have.x found, moving it to $$B (nothing is deleted; $$WANT.x starts empty and refills from npmjs)"
        mkdir "$$B"
        chmod 700 "$$B"
        live | while IFS= read -r e; do mv "$$e" "$$B/"; done
      fi
      # Record the major now, before the secret step: a crash after the move must not make the next start take the fresh 7.x
      # storage for 6.x and move it aside too. Backups can hold old credentials (htpasswd, secret): only the verdaccio uid reads them.
      [ "$$have" = "$$WANT" ] || printf '%s' "$$WANT" > "$$STATE"
      for b in "$$S"/backup-*; do [ -d "$$b" ] && { chmod 700 "$$b" || say "cannot chmod $$b"; }; done
      # 7.x refuses a server secret that is not exactly 32 characters (6.x accepted others), and has no config key or env var for it:
      # it reads it from the storage database. Keep a valid one, otherwise write a new one from the kernel CSPRNG. Never printed.
      mkdir -p "$$S/data"
      cur=$$(sed -n 's/.*"secret":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$$DB" 2>/dev/null || true)
      if [ "$${#cur}" -ne 32 ]; then
        new=$$(od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom | tr -d ' \n')
        [ "$${#new}" -eq 32 ] || { say "cannot generate a secret"; exit 1; }
        if [ -s "$$DB" ]; then
          grep -q '"secret":"' "$$DB" || { say "$$DB has no secret field, not touching it"; exit 1; }
          ( umask 077; sed "s/\"secret\":\"[^\"]*\"/\"secret\":\"$$new\"/" "$$DB" > "$$DB.new" )
        else
          ( umask 077; printf '{"list":[],"secret":"%s"}' "$$new" > "$$DB.new" )
        fi
        mv "$$DB.new" "$$DB"
        say "wrote a new server secret to $$DB (32 characters, mode 600)"
      fi
      chmod 600 "$$DB"
      exec "$$@"

volumes:
  verdaccio-storage:
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/npm-cache/docker-compose.yml"

version: 0.1
log:

    rootdirectory: /var/lib/registry
  delete:
    enabled: true
  cache:

health:
  storagedriver:
    enabled: true
    interval: 10s
    threshold: 3
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/registry-cache/config.yml"

install -d "$R/runner/stacks/registry-cache"
cat > "$R/runner/stacks/registry-cache/docker-compose.yml" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
name: registry-cache

services:
  registry:
    image: registry:3.1.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    mem_limit: 128m
    volumes:
      - ./config.yml:/etc/distribution/config.yml:ro
      - registry-data:/var/lib/registry

volumes:
  registry-data:
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 644 "$R/runner/stacks/registry-cache/docker-compose.yml"

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/admin-tools.sh" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Admin tools for the runner host: htop, btop, ncdu, iotop, mtr, network and disk tools, editors, skopeo, mc, fd, rg, fzf.
# Each package is installed on its own, so one that is missing on this release doesn't stop the rest.
# Also installs the shell aliases, shell history and fzf key bindings (Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T) and, if there is none yet, the tmux config from the init. Safe to rerun.
set -Eeuo pipefail
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0  installs admin tools (htop, btop, ncdu, iotop, mtr, dig, tcpdump, skopeo, mc, fd, rg, fzf, ...), aliases, shell history and tmux config"
  exit 0
fi
require_root

if command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  dnf -y -q install epel-release >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: epel-release not available, EPEL tools will be missing"
  PKGS=(htop btop ncdu iotop mtr nano vim-enhanced rsync wget unzip tar bash-completion skopeo dnf-utils
        bind-utils lsof sysstat tcpdump traceroute nmap-ncat jq git tmux curl mc fd-find ripgrep fzf)
  pkg_one() { dnf -y -q install "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
elif command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  apt-get update -q >/dev/null
  PKGS=(htop btop ncdu iotop mtr-tiny nano vim rsync wget unzip tar bash-completion skopeo
        dnsutils lsof sysstat tcpdump traceroute netcat-openbsd jq git tmux curl mc fd-find ripgrep fzf)
  pkg_one() { DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -q "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
else
  die "no supported package manager"
fi

installed=()
missing=()
for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do
  if pkg_one "$p"; then
    installed+=("$p")
  else
    missing+=("$p")
  fi
done

if [[ -f /etc/default/sysstat ]]; then
  sed -i 's/^ENABLED=.*/ENABLED="true"/' /etc/default/sysstat
fi
if systemctl cat sysstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  systemctl enable --now sysstat >/dev/null 2>&1 || log "WARN: could not enable sysstat collection"
fi

cat > /etc/profile.d/ci-runner.sh <<'EOF'
alias health='sudo /usr/local/bin/health'
alias runner-logs='sudo journalctl -u gitlab-runner -f'
alias runner-errors='sudo journalctl -u gitlab-runner --since "-30min" --no-pager | grep -Ei "error|warn|bottleneck"'
alias runner-jobs='sudo docker ps --filter label=com.gitlab.gitlab-runner.managed=true --format "{{.Names}}  {{.Status}}"'
alias runner-metrics='curl -s 127.0.0.1:9252/metrics | grep "^gitlab_runner_"'
alias dfd='df -h / ; sudo docker system df'
alias dstats='sudo docker stats --no-stream'
EOF
chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/ci-runner.sh
restorecon_if /etc/profile.d/ci-runner.sh

# Shell history, Ctrl+R / Ctrl+T with fzf: one source file, also embedded in server/server-init-*.sh
install -m 0644 "$REPO_ROOT/common/shell-history.sh" /etc/profile.d/90-shell-history.sh
restorecon_if /etc/profile.d/90-shell-history.sh
# Debian and Ubuntu ship HISTSIZE=1000/HISTFILESIZE=2000 in the skeleton ~/.bashrc; bash applies them before the
# first prompt and truncates the history file, so the larger limits in profile.d never take effect. Comment out
# exactly those default lines (other values are a deliberate choice and are kept).
for rc in /etc/skel/.bashrc /root/.bashrc /home/*/.bashrc; do
  [[ -f "$rc" ]] && sed -i -E 's/^(HISTSIZE=1000|HISTFILESIZE=2000)$/# &  (raised in \/etc\/profile.d\/90-shell-history.sh)/' "$rc"
done
# Debian and Ubuntu name the fd binary fdfind
if command -v fdfind >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v fd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ln -sfn "$(command -v fdfind)" /usr/local/bin/fd
fi

# root and every admin in the ssh-users group (runner/install/users.sh) get the tmux config if they have none
homes=(/root)
while IFS= read -r u; do
  [[ -n "$u" ]] && homes+=("$(getent passwd "$u" | cut -d: -f6)")
done < <(getent group ssh-users | cut -d: -f4 | tr ',' '\n')
for home in "${homes[@]}"; do
  [[ -d "$home" ]] || continue
  if [[ -f "${home}/.tmux.conf" ]]; then
    log "kept existing ${home}/.tmux.conf"
    continue
  fi
  cat > "${home}/.tmux.conf" <<'EOF'
set -g mouse on
set -g history-limit 50000
set -g base-index 1
set -g status-right '#H  %H:%M'
EOF
  chown "$(stat -c '%U:%G' "$home")" "${home}/.tmux.conf"
  chmod 644 "${home}/.tmux.conf"
done

log "installed or already present (${#installed[@]}): ${installed[*]}"
if (( ${#missing[@]} )); then
  log "WARN: not available on this release (${#missing[@]}): ${missing[*]}"
fi
for c in htop btop ncdu iotop mtr dig tcpdump skopeo sar mc fd rg fzf; do
  if command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '  %-8s ok\n' "$c"; else printf '  %-8s missing\n' "$c"; fi
done
log "OK: aliases work in new shells (or run: source /etc/profile.d/ci-runner.sh); Docker and journal aliases use sudo"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/admin-tools.sh"

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/config-drift" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Uses the same comparison rules as the daily freshness report.
set -Eeuo pipefail
exec python3 "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")/freshness" --drift "$@"
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/config-drift"

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/freshness" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Read cached maintenance status; refresh explicitly, never apply upgrades."""
import argparse
import datetime
import fcntl
import ipaddress
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request

STACKS = {
    "npm-cache": ("docker-compose.yml", "config.yaml"),
    "registry-cache": ("docker-compose.yml", "config.yml"),
    "logging": ("docker-compose.yml", "loki.yaml", "config.alloy"),
    "monitoring": ("docker-compose.yml",),
}
STATE = Path("/var/lib/server-freshness/report.json")
MAX_AGE = 36 * 3600


class CheckError(Exception):
    pass


def run(argv, timeout=30, accepted=(0,)):
    """Never echo command output on failure: Compose output may contain secrets."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
                                env={**os.environ, "LC_ALL": "C", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"})
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
        raise CheckError(f"{argv[0]} unavailable or timed out") from exc
    if result.returncode not in accepted:
        raise CheckError(f"{argv[0]} failed (exit {result.returncode})")
    return result


def read_json(text):
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise CheckError("invalid JSON response") from exc


def bridge_address():
    rows = read_json(run(["ip", "-j", "-4", "addr", "show", "docker0"]).stdout)
    for row in rows:
        for address in row.get("addr_info", []):
            if address.get("family") == "inet":
                return str(ipaddress.IPv4Address(address["local"]))
    raise CheckError("docker0 IPv4 address unavailable")


def compare_file(source, deployed, findings, expected=None):
    label = str(deployed)
    try:
        want = source.read_bytes() if expected is None else expected
        have = deployed.read_bytes()
    except OSError:
        findings.append({"level": "error", "item": label, "detail": "managed file missing or unreadable"})
        return
    if want != have:
        findings.append({"level": "warning", "item": label, "detail": "differs from repository"})


def runtime_drift(directory, findings):
    # Only retain image and memory fields; never emit interpolated Compose configuration.
    config = read_json(run(["docker", "compose", "--project-directory", str(directory),
                            "config", "--format", "json"]).stdout)
    project = config.get("name")
    if not project or not isinstance(config.get("services"), dict):
        raise CheckError("Compose project/services unavailable")
    ids = run(["docker", "ps", "-aq", "--filter", f"label=com.docker.compose.project={project}"]).stdout.split()
    rows = []
    if ids:
        fmt = '{{json .Config.Labels}}|{{json .Config.Image}}|{{.HostConfig.Memory}}|{{.State.Status}}'
        for line in run(["docker", "inspect", "--format", fmt, *ids]).stdout.splitlines():
            labels, image, memory, status = line.split("|")
            rows.append((read_json(labels), read_json(image), int(memory), status))
    for name, service in config["services"].items():
        if service.get("profiles"):
            continue
        matches = [r for r in rows if r[0].get("com.docker.compose.service") == name
                   and r[0].get("com.docker.compose.oneoff") != "True"]
        item = f"{project}/{name}"
        if not matches:
            findings.append({"level": "warning", "item": item, "detail": "container missing"})
        for _, image, memory, status in matches:
            if status != "running":
                findings.append({"level": "warning", "item": item, "detail": f"container {status}"})
            if image != service.get("image") or memory != int(service.get("mem_limit", 0)):
                findings.append({"level": "warning", "item": item,
                                 "detail": "running image reference or memory limit differs from deployed Compose"})


def drift(repo, root=Path("/")):
    findings = []
    installed = []
    if not (repo / "runner/stacks").is_dir():
        return [{"level": "error", "item": "repository", "detail": "runner/stacks missing or unreadable"}], []
    bridge = None
    for stack, files in STACKS.items():
        directory = root / "opt" / stack
        if not directory.exists():
            continue
        installed.append(directory)
        source = repo / "runner/stacks" / stack
        try:
            for name in files:
                expected = None
                if stack == "npm-cache":
                    bridge = bridge or bridge_address()
                    expected = (source / name).read_bytes().replace(b"172.17.0.1:4873",
                                                                  f"{bridge}:4873".encode())
                compare_file(source / name, directory / name, findings, expected)
            if stack == "monitoring":
                for subtree in ("prometheus", "grafana"):
                    if not (source / subtree).is_dir():
                        raise CheckError(f"repository monitoring/{subtree} missing")
                    for file in sorted((source / subtree).rglob("*")):
                        if not file.is_file():
                            continue
                        relative = file.relative_to(source)
                        expected = file.read_bytes()
                        if relative.as_posix() == "prometheus/prometheus.yml":
                            additions = (
                                ("registry-cache", "registry-cache", "127.0.0.1:5001"),
                                ("logging", "loki", "127.0.0.1:3100"),
                                ("logging", "alloy", "127.0.0.1:12345"),
                            )
                            for component, job, target in additions:
                                if (root / "opt" / component / "docker-compose.yml").exists():
                                    if f"job_name: {job}".encode() not in expected:
                                        expected += (f'  - job_name: {job}\n    static_configs:\n'
                                                     f'      - targets: ["{target}"]\n').encode()
                        compare_file(file, directory / relative, findings, expected)
                if (root / "opt/logging/docker-compose.yml").exists():
                    compare_file(repo / "runner/stacks/logging/grafana-datasource.yml",
                                 directory / "grafana/provisioning/datasources/loki.yml", findings)
            runtime_drift(directory, findings)
        except (CheckError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
            detail = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, CheckError) else "cannot inspect managed stack"
            findings.append({"level": "error", "item": stack, "detail": detail})
    if not installed:
        findings.append({"level": "error", "item": "stacks", "detail": "no installed managed stacks found"})
    return findings, installed


def version(tag):
    match = re.fullmatch(r"v?(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)", tag)
    return tuple(map(int, match.groups())) if match else None


def hub_tags(image):
    name = image.split("@", 1)[0]
    repository, sep, tag = name.rpartition(":")
    if not sep or "/" in tag:
        raise CheckError("image has no explicit version tag")
    if repository.startswith(("docker.io/", "index.docker.io/")):
        repository = repository.split("/", 1)[1]
    elif "." in repository.split("/")[0] or ":" in repository.split("/")[0]:
        raise CheckError("release discovery supports Docker Hub only")
    if "/" not in repository:
        repository = f"library/{repository}"
    current = version(tag)
    if current is None:
        raise CheckError("release discovery requires a stable major.minor.patch tag")
    url = f"https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/{urllib.parse.quote(repository, safe='/')}/tags?page_size=100&ordering=last_updated"
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=15) as response:
            payload = response.read(2_000_001)
        if len(payload) > 2_000_000:
            raise CheckError("Docker Hub response too large")
        data = read_json(payload)
        candidates = [row["name"] for row in data["results"] if version(row.get("name", ""))]
    except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
        raise CheckError("Docker Hub tag lookup unavailable") from exc
    newer = [tag for tag in candidates if version(tag) > current]
    same = [tag for tag in newer if version(tag)[0] == current[0]]
    return {"image": image, "same_major": max(same, key=version) if same else None,
            "newest_sampled": max(newer, key=version) if newer else None,
            "scope": "100 most recently updated tags; stable x.y.z only, not a support/EOL check"}


def packages():
    """Refresh metadata only. This function is never called by --check or health."""
    if shutil.which("dnf"):
        rows = run(["dnf", "-q", "--refresh", "--setopt=*.skip_if_unavailable=False", "check-update"],
                   timeout=150, accepted=(0, 100))
        pattern = re.compile(r"^(\S+)\.(?:aarch64|x86_64|noarch|i686|src)\s+(\S+)\s+\S+")
        updates = sorted({match.group(1) for line in rows.stdout.splitlines()
                          if (match := pattern.match(line))})
        if rows.returncode == 100 and not updates:
            raise CheckError("DNF reports updates but package list could not be parsed")
        security = run(["dnf", "-q", "--cacheonly", "updateinfo", "list", "--security"], timeout=60)
        advisories = {line.split()[0] for line in security.stdout.splitlines()
                      if re.match(r"^\S+\s+(?:\S+/)?(?:Security|Sec\.)\s+", line, re.I)}
        return {"updates": len(updates), "packages": updates, "security_advisories": len(advisories),
                "scope": "enabled DNF repositories"}
    if shutil.which("apt-get"):
        run(["apt-get", "-q", "-o", "APT::Update::Error-Mode=any", "update"], timeout=150)
        result = run(["apt-get", "-s", "-o", "Debug::NoLocking=1", "upgrade"], timeout=60)
        rows = [line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if line.startswith("Inst ")]
        return {"updates": len(rows), "packages": [line.split()[1] for line in rows],
                "security_packages": sum("security" in line.lower() for line in rows),
                "scope": "APT upgrade simulation (held-back packages not included)"}
    raise CheckError("no supported package manager")


def reboot_state():
    if Path("/var/run/reboot-required").exists():
        return "required"
    if shutil.which("needs-restarting"):
        result = run(["needs-restarting", "-r"], timeout=30, accepted=(0, 1))
        if result.returncode == 0:
            return "not-required"
        if "reboot is required" in result.stdout.lower():
            return "required"
    return "unknown"


def collect(repo):
    report = {"schema": 1, "checked_at": int(time.time()), "errors": [], "releases": []}
    for key, callback in (("os", packages), ("reboot", reboot_state)):
        try:
            report[key] = callback()
        except CheckError as exc:
            report["errors"].append(f"{key}: {exc}")
    findings, installed = drift(repo)
    report["drift"] = findings
    images = set()
    for directory in installed:
        try:
            data = read_json(run(["docker", "compose", "--project-directory", str(directory),
                                  "config", "--format", "json"]).stdout)
            images.update(service["image"] for service in data["services"].values() if "image" in service)
        except (CheckError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError):
            report["errors"].append(f"{directory.name}: image inventory unavailable")
    for image in sorted(images):
        try:
            report["releases"].append(hub_tags(image))
        except CheckError as exc:
            report["errors"].append(f"{image}: {exc}")
    report["versions"] = {}
    for name, argv in (("docker", ["docker", "--version"]), ("runner", ["gitlab-runner", "--version"])):
        if shutil.which(argv[0]):
            try:
                output = run(argv).stdout
                match = re.search(r"(?:Version:\s*|version\s+)([0-9][0-9.\w+-]*)", output, re.I)
                report["versions"][name] = match.group(1) if match else "unknown"
            except CheckError as exc:
                report["errors"].append(f"{name}: {exc}")
    return report


def save_report(path, report):
    path.parent.mkdir(mode=0o755, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd, name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".report-", dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as stream:
            json.dump(report, stream, indent=2)
            stream.write("\n")
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
            os.fchmod(stream.fileno(), 0o644)
        os.replace(name, path)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(name):
            os.unlink(name)


def report_status(report, now=None):
    now = time.time() if now is None else now
    if (not isinstance(report, dict) or report.get("schema") != 1
            or not isinstance(report.get("checked_at"), int)
            or not isinstance(report.get("errors"), list)
            or not isinstance(report.get("drift"), list)
            or not isinstance(report.get("releases"), list)):
        raise CheckError("invalid cached report")
    if (not all(isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("level") in ("warning", "error")
                and isinstance(row.get("item"), str) and isinstance(row.get("detail"), str)
                for row in report["drift"])
            or not all(isinstance(row, dict) and "newest_sampled" in row
                       and "same_major" in row and isinstance(row.get("image"), str)
                       for row in report["releases"])
            or not all(isinstance(error, str) for error in report["errors"])
            or not isinstance(report.get("os", {}), dict)):
        raise CheckError("invalid cached report fields")
    age = now - report["checked_at"]
    if age < 0:
        raise CheckError("cached report timestamp is in the future")
    errors = len(report["errors"]) + sum(f["level"] == "error" for f in report["drift"])
    drift_count = sum(f["level"] == "warning" for f in report["drift"])
    releases = sum(bool(row["newest_sampled"]) for row in report["releases"])
    os_updates = report.get("os", {}).get("updates")
    if os_updates is not None and (type(os_updates) is not int or os_updates < 0):
        raise CheckError("invalid cached package update count")
    stale = age > MAX_AGE
    rc = 2 if errors else int(stale or drift_count > 0 or releases > 0
                             or os_updates is None or bool(os_updates) or report.get("reboot") != "not-required")
    summary = (f"OS updates={os_updates if os_updates is not None else 'unknown'}, "
               f"image release candidates={releases}, drift={drift_count}, errors={errors}, "
               f"reboot={report.get('reboot', 'unknown')}, age={int(age // 3600)}h"
               f"{' (STALE)' if stale else ''}")
    return rc, summary


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    mode.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="read cached report only; no network or writes")
    mode.add_argument("--refresh", action="store_true", help="refresh metadata/network checks and write cached report; never upgrade")
    parser.add_argument("--drift", action="store_true", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    parser.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, help="repository root (default: /etc/server-freshness/repo)")
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("/"), help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    parser.add_argument("--state", type=Path, default=STATE)
    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="JSON output")
    parser.add_argument("--summary", action="store_true", help="one-line cached summary")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.drift and (args.refresh or args.summary):
        parser.error("--drift requires --check and cannot use --summary")
    if args.refresh and os.geteuid() != 0:
        parser.error("--refresh requires root (package metadata and report writes)")
    try:
        if args.drift or args.refresh:
            repo = args.repo or Path("/etc/server-freshness/repo").read_text().strip()
            repo = Path(repo)
            if not repo.is_absolute():
                raise CheckError("repository path must be absolute")
        if args.drift:
            findings, _ = drift(repo, args.root)
            if args.json:
                print(json.dumps(findings, indent=2))
            else:
                for row in findings:
                    print(f"{row['level'].upper()}: {row['item']}: {row['detail']}")
                print(f"Checked managed stack files and runtime image/memory; {len(findings)} finding(s)")
            return 2 if any(r["level"] == "error" for r in findings) else int(bool(findings))
        if args.refresh:
            args.state.parent.mkdir(mode=0o755, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with (args.state.parent / ".refresh.lock").open("a") as lock:
                try:
                    fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                except BlockingIOError as exc:
                    raise CheckError("another freshness refresh is running") from exc
                print(f"{datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()} INFO freshness refresh started",
                      file=sys.stderr)
                started = time.monotonic()
                report = collect(repo)
                save_report(args.state, report)
        else:
            report = read_json(args.state.read_text())
        rc, summary = report_status(report)
        if args.refresh:
            print(f"{datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()} INFO freshness refresh completed "
                  f"exit={rc} duration={time.monotonic() - started:.1f}s", file=sys.stderr)
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
        else:
            print(summary)
            if not args.summary:
                print(f"Details: freshness --check --json ({args.state})")
                for error in report["errors"]:
                    print(f"ERROR: {error}")
                for row in report["releases"]:
                    if row["newest_sampled"]:
                        print(f"REVIEW: {row['image']}: same major={row['same_major'] or 'none found'}, "
                              f"newest sampled={row['newest_sampled']}")
                for row in report["drift"]:
                    print(f"{row['level'].upper()}: {row['item']}: {row['detail']}")
                print("Release candidates are sampled stable Docker Hub tags, not support/EOL guarantees.")
        return rc
    except (CheckError, OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        detail = str(exc) if isinstance(exc, CheckError) else "report/input missing, unreadable, or invalid"
        print(f"freshness: {detail}; run sudo freshness --refresh to collect a report", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
__SIC_EOF__
chmod 755 "$R/common/freshness"

install -d "$R/common"
cat > "$R/common/health" <<'__SIC_EOF__'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# health: one-command health and status report for this host (GitLab Runner host or general server)
set -Eeuo pipefail

DISK_WARN=70
DISK_FAIL=85
INODE_WARN=80
MEM_WARN=15
MEM_FAIL=5
LOAD_WARN=1.5
LOAD_FAIL=3
CLAM_SIG_WARN_DAYS=7
QUICK=0
BRIEF=0
WRITE=0
ONLY_CONTAINERS=0
COLOR=1
PROFILE=auto
RUNNER_UNREGISTERED=0
CFG=/etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml
PROM_URL="${PROM_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:9090}"
FORECAST_MIN_HISTORY_H="${FORECAST_MIN_HISTORY_H:-6}"

usage() {
  cat <<'USAGE'
Usage: health [options]

One-command health and status report for this host. Works on a GitLab Runner
host and on a general server.

Run it as a normal user: it re-runs itself through sudo when that needs no password.
Without root and without passwordless sudo it still runs, but skips the root-only
checks (firewall rules, fail2ban, sshd settings, journal, docker, runner).

Options:
  -q, --quick       skip slow checks (runner verify, network, pending updates, needs-restarting)
  -c, --containers  only show health of running containers
  --profile P       server|runner (default: auto = server; runner only when a runner is registered)
  --brief           compact summary (7 lines) of the state the server timers cached, plus live disk, memory,
                    firewall and fail2ban; this is what the admin sees on login
  --write           with --brief, as root: save it to /var/lib/server-health/brief.txt (done by server-health-brief.timer;
                    also runs a full report at most every 6 hours and notifies when it has failures)
  --no-color        plain output without colors
  -h, --help        show this help

Exit codes: 0 all OK, 1 warnings only, 2 at least one failure
USAGE
}

ORIG_ARGS=("$@")
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    -q|--quick) QUICK=1 ;;
    -c|--containers) ONLY_CONTAINERS=1 ;;
    --profile) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "--profile needs a value: runner or server" >&2; exit 2; }; shift; PROFILE="$1" ;;
    --profile=*) PROFILE="${1#--profile=}" ;;
    --no-color) COLOR=0 ;;
    --brief) BRIEF=1 ;;
    --write) WRITE=1 ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

if (( WRITE == 1 && BRIEF == 0 )); then echo "--write needs --brief" >&2; exit 2; fi
case "$PROFILE" in
  auto|runner|server) ;;
  *) echo "invalid --profile '${PROFILE}': use runner or server" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

LIMITED=0
# Not root: re-run through sudo when that works without a password (HEALTH_REEXEC stops loops);
# otherwise run in limited mode and skip the checks that need root.
if [[ $EUID -ne 0 ]]; then
  if [[ -z "${HEALTH_REEXEC:-}" ]] && command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1 && sudo -n true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exec sudo -n -- env HEALTH_REEXEC=1 "$(readlink -f "$0")" "${ORIG_ARGS[@]}"
  fi
  LIMITED=1
fi

if [[ -t 1 && "$COLOR" == "1" && -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]]; then
  C_OK=$'\e[32m'; C_WARN=$'\e[33m'; C_FAIL=$'\e[31m'; C_B=$'\e[1m'; C_D=$'\e[2m'; C_N=$'\e[0m'
else
  C_OK=""; C_WARN=""; C_FAIL=""; C_B=""; C_D=""; C_N=""
fi

N_OK=0; N_WARN=0; N_FAIL=0
FW_STATE=unknown
ok()      { N_OK=$((N_OK + 1));     printf '  %s%-5s%s %s\n' "$C_OK" "OK" "$C_N" "$*"; }
warn()    { N_WARN=$((N_WARN + 1)); printf '  %s%-5s%s %s\n' "$C_WARN" "WARN" "$C_N" "$*"; }
fail()    { N_FAIL=$((N_FAIL + 1)); printf '  %s%-5s%s %s\n' "$C_FAIL" "FAIL" "$C_N" "$*"; }
skip()    { printf '  %s%-5s %s%s\n' "$C_D" "--" "$*" "$C_N"; }
info()    { printf '  %s%-5s %s%s\n' "$C_D" "" "$*" "$C_N"; }
section() { printf '\n%s%s%s\n' "$C_B" "$*" "$C_N"; }
have()    { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
gt()      { awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN { exit !(a > b) }'; }
isnum()   { [[ "${1:-}" =~ ^-?[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$ ]]; }
num()     { awk -v x="$1" -v d="${2:-1}" 'BEGIN { printf "%.*f", d, x }'; }
unit_exists() { systemctl list-unit-files "$1" --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; }
is_runner()   { [[ "$PROFILE" == "runner" ]]; }
detect_profile() {
  [[ "$PROFILE" == "auto" ]] || return 0
  # Default is a plain server. Only a host with a registered runner gets the runner checks;
  # gitlab-runner installed but never registered is still a plain server.
  if [[ -r "$CFG" ]] && grep -q '^[[:space:]]*\[\[runners\]\]' "$CFG" 2>/dev/null; then
    PROFILE=runner
  else
    PROFILE=server
    # Without root the 0600 config.toml can't be read, so "not registered" would be a guess.
    if [[ -e "$CFG" && ! -r "$CFG" ]]; then RUNNER_UNREGISTERED=2
    elif have gitlab-runner || unit_exists gitlab-runner.service; then RUNNER_UNREGISTERED=1; fi
  fi
}
http_code()   { curl -s -o /dev/null -m "${2:-5}" -w '%{http_code}' "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; }

human_age() {
  local s="$1"
  if (( s < 3600 )); then echo "$(( s / 60 ))m"
  elif (( s < 86400 )); then echo "$(( s / 3600 ))h$(( s % 3600 / 60 ))m"
  else echo "$(( s / 86400 ))d$(( s % 86400 / 3600 ))h"; fi
}

prom_q() {
  curl -fsS -m 10 -G "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode "query=$1" 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1] // empty' 2>/dev/null || true
}

prom_qv() {
  curl -fsS -m 10 -G "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode "query=$1" 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -r '.data.result[] | ((.metric | to_entries | map(.value) | join(",")) as $k | "\($k)=\(.value[1])")' 2>/dev/null || true
}

print_summary_and_exit() {
  section "Summary"
  printf '  %s%d OK%s  %s%d WARN%s  %s%d FAIL%s\n' \
    "$C_OK" "$N_OK" "$C_N" "$C_WARN" "$N_WARN" "$C_N" "$C_FAIL" "$N_FAIL" "$C_N"
  if (( N_FAIL > 0 )); then exit 2; fi
  if (( N_WARN > 0 )); then exit 1; fi
  exit 0
}

check_system() {
  section "System"
  local pretty="unknown"
  if [[ -r /etc/os-release ]]; then
    pretty=$(awk -F= '/^PRETTY_NAME=/ { gsub(/"/, "", $2); print $2 }' /etc/os-release)
  fi
  info "$(uname -n) | ${pretty} | $(uname -m) | kernel $(uname -r)"
  info "uptime $(uptime -p 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^up //') | $(nproc) vCPU"

  local cores load5 per_core
  cores=$(nproc)
  read -r _ load5 _ _ _ < /proc/loadavg
  per_core=$(awk -v l="$load5" -v c="$cores" 'BEGIN { printf "%.2f", l / c }')
  if gt "$per_core" "$LOAD_FAIL"; then
    fail "load ${load5} (5 min), ${per_core} per core"
  elif gt "$per_core" "$LOAD_WARN"; then
    warn "load ${load5} (5 min), ${per_core} per core"
  else
    ok "load ${load5} (5 min), ${per_core} per core"
  fi

  local mem_total mem_avail mem_pct msg
  mem_total=$(awk '/^MemTotal:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)
  mem_avail=$(awk '/^MemAvailable:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)
  mem_pct=$(( mem_avail * 100 / mem_total ))
  msg="memory $(( (mem_total - mem_avail) / 1024 ))/$(( mem_total / 1024 )) MB used, ${mem_pct}% available"
  if (( mem_pct < MEM_FAIL )); then fail "$msg"
  elif (( mem_pct < MEM_WARN )); then warn "$msg"
  else ok "$msg"; fi

  local swap_total swap_free
  swap_total=$(awk '/^SwapTotal:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)
  swap_free=$(awk '/^SwapFree:/ { print $2 }' /proc/meminfo)
  if (( swap_total > 0 )); then
    local swap_pct=$(( (swap_total - swap_free) * 100 / swap_total ))
    msg="swap $(( (swap_total - swap_free) / 1024 ))/$(( swap_total / 1024 )) MB used (${swap_pct}%)"
    if is_runner; then info "$msg"
    elif (( swap_pct >= 80 )); then warn "$msg, memory pressure"
    else ok "$msg"; fi
  else
    info "swap: none"
  fi

  local kills ooms victims
  # Count kills, not every related kernel line. One kill emits several matches.
  if (( LIMITED )); then
    kills=""
    skip "OOM kills: needs root (kernel log)"
  else
    kills=$(journalctl -k -b --no-pager -o cat 2>/dev/null | grep 'Out of memory: Killed process' || true)
  fi
  if [[ -n "$kills" ]]; then
    ooms=$(grep -c . <<<"$kills")
    victims=$(sed -nE 's/.*Killed process [0-9]+ \(([^)]+)\).*/\1/p' <<<"$kills" | sort | uniq -c | awk '{printf "%s x%s, ", $2, $1}' | sed 's/, $//')
    warn "${ooms} OOM kill(s) since boot${victims:+ (${victims})} (journalctl -k -b | grep 'Killed process')"
  elif (( ! LIMITED )); then
    ok "no OOM kills since boot"
  fi

  local disk_pct disk_info inode_pct
  disk_pct=$(df --output=pcent / | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9')
  disk_info=$(df -h --output=used,size / | tail -1 | awk '{ print $1 "/" $2 }')
  msg="disk / ${disk_pct}% used (${disk_info})"
  if (( disk_pct >= DISK_FAIL )); then fail "$msg"
  elif (( disk_pct >= DISK_WARN )); then warn "$msg"
  else ok "$msg"; fi

  inode_pct=$(df --output=ipcent / 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | tr -dc '0-9' || true)
  if (( ${inode_pct:-0} >= INODE_WARN )); then
    warn "inodes / ${inode_pct}% used"
  fi

  local failed
  failed=$(systemctl --failed --no-legend --plain 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1 }' | tr '\n' ' ' || true)
  if [[ -n "${failed// /}" ]]; then
    fail "failed units: ${failed}"
  else
    ok "no failed systemd units"
  fi

  if have timedatectl; then
    local sync
    sync=$(timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ "$sync" == "yes" ]]; then ok "clock synchronized (NTP)"
    else warn "clock not synchronized (timedatectl)"; fi
  fi

  if have cloud-init; then
    local ci
    ci=$(cloud-init status 2>/dev/null | awk -F': ' '/^status:/ { print $2 }' || true)
    case "$ci" in
      done) ok "cloud-init done" ;;
      running) warn "cloud-init still running" ;;
      "") skip "cloud-init status unknown" ;;
      *) warn "cloud-init status: ${ci}" ;;
    esac
  fi
  return 0
}

check_security() {
  section "Security"
  if have getenforce; then
    local mode denials raw rc=0
    mode=$(getenforce 2>/dev/null || true)
    case "$mode" in
      Enforcing) ok "SELinux enforcing" ;;
      Permissive) warn "SELinux permissive (logs only, does not block)" ;;
      *) warn "SELinux ${mode:-unknown}" ;;
    esac
    # ausearch treats a pipe on stdin as the audit log and blocks until it closes.
    # health is often started over ssh, so force the on-disk logs and bound the query.
    if (( LIMITED )); then
      skip "SELinux denials: needs root"
    elif ! have ausearch; then
      skip "ausearch not installed"
    else
      raw=$(timeout 10 ausearch --input-logs -m avc -ts today </dev/null 2>/dev/null) || rc=$?
      if (( rc == 124 )); then
        skip "SELinux denial query timed out"
      elif (( rc != 0 && rc != 1 )); then
        skip "could not query SELinux denials (ausearch exit ${rc})"
      else
        denials=$(grep -c 'avc:' <<<"$raw" || true)
        if (( ${denials:-0} > 0 )); then
          warn "${denials} SELinux denials today (ausearch --input-logs -m avc -ts today)"
        else
          ok "no SELinux denials today"
        fi
      fi
    fi
  fi

  if (( LIMITED )); then
    skip "sshd settings, listening ports, pending updates: need root (run as root for the full report)"
  elif have sshd; then
    local sshd_t root_login
    sshd_t=$(sshd -T 2>/dev/null || true)
    if grep -qx 'passwordauthentication no' <<<"$sshd_t"; then
      ok "SSH password login disabled"
    elif is_runner; then
      fail "SSH password login enabled"
    else
      warn "SSH password login enabled (set PasswordAuthentication no)"
    fi
    root_login=$(awk '/^permitrootlogin / { print $2 }' <<<"$sshd_t")
    if is_runner; then
      case "$root_login" in
        no)  ok "SSH root login disabled" ;;
        yes) fail "SSH root login with password allowed" ;;
        *)   warn "SSH root login by key still allowed (${root_login:-unknown}); disable: sudo bash -c \"cd /root/server-init-config && runner/setup.sh --lock-root\"" ;;
      esac
      if grep -q '^allowgroups ' <<<"$sshd_t"; then
        ok "SSH limited to groups: $(awk '/^allowgroups / { printf "%s ", $2 }' <<<"$sshd_t")"
      else
        warn "SSH not limited by AllowGroups (runner/install/users.sh sets it)"
      fi
    else
      case "$root_login" in
        yes) warn "SSH root login with password allowed (PermitRootLogin yes)" ;;
        *)   info "SSH root login: ${root_login:-unknown}" ;;
      esac
    fi
  fi

  local members u shell pid ru
  members=$(getent group docker 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f4 | tr ',' '\n' | grep -vxE 'gitlab-runner|github-runner' | grep . | tr '\n' ' ' || true)
  if [[ -n "${members// /}" ]]; then
    warn "users in the docker group (root-equivalent): ${members}; use sudo docker instead"
  else
    if is_runner; then
      if getent group docker 2>/dev/null | cut -d: -f4 | tr ',' '\n' | grep -qx 'github-runner'; then ok "docker group: only gitlab-runner and github-runner"; else ok "docker group: only gitlab-runner"; fi
    else ok "docker group: no members"; fi
  fi
  for u in gitlab-runner github-runner monitoring; do
    id "$u" >/dev/null 2>&1 || continue
    shell=$(getent passwd "$u" | cut -d: -f7)
    case "$shell" in
      */nologin|*/false) ok "service user ${u}: no login shell" ;;
      *) warn "service user ${u} has login shell ${shell}" ;;
    esac
  done
  if have systemctl && systemctl is-active --quiet gitlab-runner 2>/dev/null; then
    pid=$(systemctl show -p MainPID --value gitlab-runner 2>/dev/null || true)
    ru=$(ps -o user= -p "${pid:-0}" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
    if [[ "$ru" == root ]]; then
      warn "gitlab-runner service runs as root (runner/install/users.sh switches it to gitlab-runner)"
